articles.title: Florida International vs Kennesaw State: JJ Kohl Throws Two Late, Panthers Can't Climb Out, 35-24
articles.byline: Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, The Florida International Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Kennesaw State Owls (5-6) 35, Florida International Panthers (4-7) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw. Next: vs Sam Houston, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Pitbull Stadium, Miami
articles.text:
For a half, this felt like our kind of dogfight. Florida International led 10-7 in the second quarter at Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, and then Kennesaw State scored 28 straight and beat us 35-24. We're 4-7, 2-5 in Conference USA.

Devonte Lyons got us even in the first quarter with a 24-yard touchdown run, and Robert Czeremcha hit a 40-yard field goal to put us up 10-7. Lyons finished with 11 carries for 54 yards, and for a while the run game had real life in it.

Then we went cold. The Owls scored twice late in the first half, and twice more in the third, and it was 35-10 before we blinked. That's 28 unanswered points, and that's the part that keeps me up tonight.

JJ Kohl kept throwing, 27 of 39 for 231 yards and two late touchdowns. He found James Resar from 6 early in the fourth, then threw the two-pointer to Jackson Verdugo to make it 35-18. Then he hit Kyle McNeal from 3 with 1:57 left. The two-point try after that one didn't work, and that was it.

Maguire Anderson had a strong day, six catches for 71 yards. McNeal caught six for 52, Tyson Carter four for 36. Kohl even ran for 41 yards on four carries. We never put the ball on the ground or threw it to the other team, and we went 3 for 4 on fourth down because this team doesn't fold.

The penalties hurt. We were flagged 12 times for 116 yards, and that's too many free yards to give a team that's trying to bury you. Wesley Miller made seven tackles, and Jai-Ayviauynn Celestine had six, all solo.

One more at home. Sam Houston comes to Pitbull Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET. Let's give Miami a real sendoff and send this group into winter with a win. Go Panthers!

articles.title: Kennesaw State vs Florida International: Boogie Woods III Runs for 100, Owls Reach Five Wins, 35-24
articles.byline: Ximena Holcombe-Reyes, The Kennesaw State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Kennesaw State Owls (5-6) 35, Florida International Panthers (4-7) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw. Next: at Western Kentucky, Sat., Nov. 28, 1:00 PM ET, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green
articles.text:
The Owls are 5-6, one win from bowl eligibility, and Saturday in Kennesaw felt like a team finding its stride at the right time. Kennesaw State beat Florida International 35-24, and we're 4-3 in Conference USA.

Boogie Woods III was the hammer. He ran 14 times for 100 yards and two touchdowns, the first a 53-yard burst in the first quarter, the second a 1-yard plunge with 4:25 left in the half that gave us a 14-10 lead we never gave back. That second score capped a 10-play, 89-yard drive.

Landon Varnes had the kind of afternoon you want from a quarterback at home. He went 21 of 27 for 219 yards and two touchdowns, and he didn't throw an interception. He hit Brayden Munroe from 25 yards with 43 seconds left in the half to make it 21-10, and then found Dylan Gary from 7 in the third.

Gary finished with five catches for 75 yards, including a 44-yarder. Latrelle Murrell ran it in from 17 and added 63 yards on 11 carries, plus three catches for 40. We were up 35-10 after three quarters, and the 6,672 in the stands finally got to sit back and enjoy it.

The defense never let Florida International get comfortable. Kody Jones made six tackles, all solo, with a tackle for loss. Isaac Paul had five and one for loss, and Tay'vion Lawson broke up four throws. We went 2 for 2 on fourth down and 6 of 12 on third.

FIU scored twice in the fourth to make the final look closer than the game felt. That's fine. I'll take a win that puts us one short of six, and I'll take a Saturday in Kennesaw where the offense was rolling.

Next up: at Western Kentucky on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 1:00 PM ET at Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium in Bowling Green. A sixth win in Bowling Green would send this group bowling, and I love the sound of that. Let's fly, Owls!

articles.title: New Mexico State vs Delaware: Trey Hedden Throws Four, but the Aggies Can't Hold a Halftime Lead, 42-30
articles.byline: Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, The New Mexico State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Delaware Blue Hens (6-5) 42, New Mexico State Aggies (3-8) 30, Sat., Nov. 21, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces. Next: at Middle Tennessee, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro
articles.text:
At halftime in Las Cruces, the Aggies were up 16-14 and Aggie Memorial Stadium was feeling it. By the end, Delaware had won 42-30, and New Mexico State had its fourth straight loss. We're 3-8, 2-5 in Conference USA.

Trey Hedden had himself a day, 17 of 33 for 258 yards and four touchdowns. He found Terrione Graves for a 55-yard score, Myles Libman from 8, and TJ Pride twice late, from 7 and 14 yards. Graves had two catches for 71 yards, Libman caught six for 70, and AJ Williams III had five for 87, with a 40-yarder.

The second quarter was some of our best football of the year. After Ilya Uvaydov's 26-yard field goal got us started in the first, Graves' long touchdown and Libman's catch put us in front before the break.

Then the third quarter happened. Delaware scored twice, Kaderris Roberts broke a 30-yard run, and Nick Minicucci kept throwing. Five touchdowns and 398 yards against us. That's a long night for any secondary.

James Jones ran hard, 11 carries for 94 yards, with a 42-yarder. Obinna Okeke was a menace, with a sack and a half and three and a half tackles for loss. Tory Gethers, Nick Session and Jakobe Campbell each made eight tackles. We didn't give it away once, and we held Delaware to 2 of 11 on third down even if they kept converting fourth downs.

We never stopped swinging, either. Down 35-16, we scored twice in the last four minutes, and both two-point tries worked, Hedden to Dijon Stanley and a TJ Washington Jr. run. That's a team still playing for each other.

Next up: at Middle Tennessee on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET at Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium in Murfreesboro to close the season. End it on a high note, Aggies. Go Aggies!

articles.title: Delaware vs New Mexico State: Nick Minicucci Throws Five and Breaks the School Record, 42-30
articles.matchup: Final: Delaware Blue Hens (6-5) 42, New Mexico State Aggies (3-8) 30, Sat., Nov. 21, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces. Next: vs Jacksonville State, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Delaware Stadium, Newark
articles.text:
Nick Minicucci is the greatest touchdown thrower in Delaware history, and he just made the Blue Hens bowl eligible. He threw five touchdowns in Las Cruces on Saturday, broke the school career record, and Delaware beat New Mexico State 42-30. That's a 6-5 record, 4-3 in league play.

Minicucci now has 62 career touchdown throws, past the school mark of 58 that Matt Nagy set from 1997 to 2000. Think about the names who've played quarterback at Delaware. Now think about who's at the top of that list. That's our guy.

He was 31 of 41 for 398 yards and didn't throw an interception. Scott Moore caught three of the touchdowns, from 19, 9 and 20 yards. Elijah Sessoms caught the first one from 4 yards. Josh Humes took a tight end screen 47 yards down the left side to make it 35-16. Bryson Graves turned a short throw into a 48-yard gain and finished with 88 yards on five catches. Sean Wilson caught eight balls for 65.

This wasn't easy. New Mexico State led 16-14 at halftime, and the Aggies had us scratching our heads. Then Kaderris Roberts broke a 30-yard touchdown run with 5:49 left in the third quarter, and we never trailed again. Roberts also caught three balls for 49 yards.

We went 4 for 5 on fourth down and didn't give it away once. That's a team that trusts itself. Gavin Moul made 10 tackles and a sack, George Mullins had seven, and Kahlil Ali got a tackle for loss.

That's back-to-back wins and four of our last five. This team is peaking at exactly the right time, and the whole state should be paying attention.

Jacksonville State comes to Delaware Stadium in Newark on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 3:30 PM ET to close the regular season. Pack the place in blue and gold and let Minicucci hear it. Go Hens!

articles.title: Coastal Carolina vs Louisiana: Robby Washington's 75-Yard Catch Can't Undo Three Turnovers, 38-24
articles.byline: Marigold 'Goldie' Seabrook, The Coastal Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns (8-3) 38, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers (4-7) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium, Lafayette. Next: at James Madison, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Bridgeforth Stadium, Harrisonburg
articles.text:
We were down 7-0 before our offense had even broken a sweat. Our quarterback coughed up the football on the game's second play, Micah Johnson ran it back 24 yards, and Louisiana led the rest of the way in a 38-24 win against Coastal Carolina in Lafayette. We're 4-7, 3-4 in the Sun Belt.

Three turnovers. That's the whole story. Deuce Bailey lost that fumble and threw two interceptions, and you can't hand a good home team three free possessions and expect to win in Lafayette.

But there was fight in this group. Nico Cavanillas Alti hit a 46-yard field goal, and Bailey found Clayton Coppock Jr. for a 3-yard touchdown with seven seconds left before the break, trimming it to 21-10. Coppock caught six balls for 59 yards.

Kente Edwards ran it in from 7 in the fourth quarter and finished with 78 yards on 13 carries. Dominic Lee-Knicely added 58 on 10. Then Osiris Lopez hit Robby Washington for a 75-yard touchdown that brought us within 38-24. Lopez went 6 of 11 for 159 yards, and Washington caught four for 104.

Colton Hinton was great all day, seven catches for 106 yards, with a 39-yarder. Marcellius Pulliam made 11 tackles, and Zeke Marshall had five, all solo. We actually outgained the Cajuns, 395 yards to 369, and we held the ball for 31:44. It just didn't matter with three giveaways. Our defense held Louisiana to 14 first downs and 140 rushing yards, and Xzavier Booker and Jesse Powell II made four tackles apiece.

That's the frustrating part. On paper, we played them even. On the scoreboard, we didn't.

Next up: at James Madison on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET at Bridgeforth Stadium in Harrisonburg to close the season. Teal Nation, let's finish with a fight. Go Chants!

articles.title: Louisiana vs Coastal Carolina: Micah Johnson's Scoop-and-Score and Lunch Winfield's Four Touchdowns, 38-24
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns (8-3) 38, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers (4-7) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium, Lafayette. Next: at Georgia State, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta
articles.text:
Micah Johnson didn't wait around. On the second snap of the game at Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium, he scooped up a Coastal Carolina fumble and rumbled 24 yards for a touchdown, and Louisiana never trailed. Ragin' Cajuns 38, Coastal Carolina 24, and we're 8-3, 5-2 in the Sun Belt.

That's three straight wins, and Lunch Winfield is the reason we pulled away. He went 14 of 20 for 229 yards and three touchdowns, and he ran for another from 6 yards out. Fourteen completions, four touchdowns. Efficient doesn't begin to describe it.

Winfield found a different guy every time: a 1-yard touchdown to Caden Jensen in the second quarter, a 27-yarder to KeDarius Wade in the third and a 4-yarder to Brock Chappell late in the fourth. Wade had three catches for 79 yards. JJ Garner ran 11 times for 90 yards, including a 55-yard burst that had me out of my seat.

The defense came to eat. Harrison Kidder had a sack, an interception and eight tackles. Avery Demery intercepted another one. Johnson added a sack to his touchdown, and Collin Jacob and Maurion Eleam each got after the quarterback too. Coastal Carolina gave it away three times, and we only gave it back once.

We led 21-10 at halftime and 38-17 with about five minutes left. Tony Sterner made all five extra points and a 36-yard field goal. Shelton Sampson Jr. had two catches for 50 yards. We needed only 14 first downs to put up 38, because when this offense hits, it hits big.

And we're perfect at home this year, 6-0 in Lafayette. Nobody walks into our place and leaves happy, and 19,367 of our people were in the house to see this one.

Next up: at Georgia State on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET at Center Parc Stadium in Atlanta. Take this show on the road and bring home number nine. Geaux Cajuns!

articles.title: UL Monroe vs App State: Austin Carlisle Nearly Steals One in Boone Before an Overtime Heartbreaker, 17-16
articles.byline: Darnell Vidrine, The UL Monroe Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: App State Mountaineers (7-4) 17, UL Monroe Warhawks (2-9) 16, Sat., Nov. 21, Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone. Next: vs Marshall, Sat., Nov. 28, 1:00 PM ET, Malone Stadium, Monroe
articles.text:
One extra point. That's what stood between UL Monroe and a win in Boone on Saturday. Austin Carlisle scored from a yard out in overtime, the kick got blocked, App State answered right away, and the Warhawks lost 17-16. We're 2-9, 2-5 in the Sun Belt.

And this one hurts more because we had it. Carlisle hit Bryce Anderson for an 18-yard touchdown with 6:23 left for a 10-7 lead, and we held it until two seconds were left in regulation. Two seconds! A 22-yard field goal tied it, and off we went to overtime.

Carlisle played his heart out. He was 16 of 22 for 167 yards, ran 18 times for 59 more and scored our overtime touchdown himself. He threw one interception, but he gave us every chance to win this game on the road.

Our defense deserves a parade back home. Jabari Tiller made 14 tackles, nine of them solo. Moses Madubuike had 1 1/2 tackles for loss, and Chris Payne made eight tackles. App State's kicker missed three field goals, and we held the Mountaineers to 10 points in regulation in their own stadium.

Abram Murray hit a 26-yarder in the second quarter for our first points. Anderson caught four balls for 51 yards, Marcellus Jackson had a 31-yard grab, and Parker Fulghum caught three. articles.title: App State vs UL Monroe: Aaron Clark's Blocked Kick and Jackson Grier's Catch Win It in Overtime, 17-16
articles.byline: Zebulon 'Zeb' Coldiron, The App State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: App State Mountaineers (7-4) 17, UL Monroe Warhawks (2-9) 16, Sat., Nov. 21, Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone. Next: at South Alabama, Fri., Nov. 27, 3:00 PM ET, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile
articles.text:
I aged about 10 years in Boone on Saturday, and I'd do it all again tomorrow. Aaron Clark blocked an extra point in overtime, Malachi Singleton hit Jackson Grier for a 25-yard touchdown on our very first snap of the next possession, and App State beat UL Monroe 17-16. We're 7-4, 4-3 in the Sun Belt.

Let's back up, because this one was a grind. UL Monroe went ahead 10-7 with 6:23 left in the fourth quarter, and for a while it looked like that might be the ballgame. Then, with two seconds left in regulation, James London tied it 10-10 with a 22-yard field goal. London had missed three kicks earlier in the day, and he walked out there anyway and drilled it. That's guts.

In overtime, the Warhawks scored first on a 1-yard run. Then Clark got a hand on the extra point. Blocked! Instead of a seven-point hole, we were down six, and that one point flipped the whole night. On our first play, Singleton found Grier for 25 yards, London made the kick, and the place exploded.

Singleton finished 19 of 32 for 188 yards and two touchdowns, the first a 3-yarder to Nate Branch in the second quarter. Branch caught seven balls. Chris Lofton had five catches for 57, and Luke Douglas grabbed a 34-yarder. Treyaun Webb ran 20 times for 93 yards, and Ja'Quez Cross added 48.

The defense held UL Monroe to 277 yards and 4 of 15 on third down. Kaleb Purdy intercepted a throw, Carson Sloan and Colton Phares made nine tackles apiece, and Clark had a sack to go with the block of the year.

We also went 3 for 3 on fourth down. It wasn't pretty, and I don't care. In November you take every win and say thank you.

Next up: at South Alabama on Friday, Nov. 27, at 3:00 PM ET at Hancock Whitney Stadium in Mobile. Eight wins would look awfully good on this team. Go App!

articles.title: South Florida vs Florida Atlantic: Luke Kromenhoek's 385 Yards Can't Save the Bulls in Boca, 35-14
articles.byline: Reina Valdés-Kowalski, The South Florida Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Atlantic Owls (7-4) 35, South Florida Bulls (6-5) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Boca Raton. Next: vs Tulane, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa
articles.text:
There's no sugarcoating a night like this one. South Florida went to Boca Raton, sat through weather delay after weather delay, and lost to Florida Atlantic 35-14. We're 6-5, 2-5 in the American, and I'm still waiting for the storm in my chest to clear.

Luke Kromenhoek did everything he could. He threw 49 times, completed 32, and piled up 385 yards. His 27-yard touchdown to Jason Collins Jr. in the third quarter was a beauty, and Collins finished with six catches for 61. Mudia Reuben caught seven balls for 119 yards, and Cameron Seldon caught eight for 101.

The problem was everything else. We ran for 45 yards on 27 carries. We trailed 20-0 at halftime. Caden Veltkamp went 30 of 38 with four touchdowns against us, and Florida Atlantic converted 7 of 11 third downs. You can't spot a team like that 20 points and expect to chase it down with one arm.

We did push back for a minute. Down 28-0 in the third quarter, Collins scored to make it 28-7. Then the Owls answered right away, and it was 35-7 going into the fourth. Tray Kinkle punched one in from 2 yards out with 10 seconds left for the final score.

Grayson Howard made eight tackles, and Israel Boyce had a tackle for loss. We went 1 for 5 on fourth down, and those empty trips killed any chance of a real comeback.

Here's the good news, and it's real: we're 6-5 and already bowl eligible. One bad night in Boca doesn't change that. One more home game to finish the regular season the right way.

Tulane comes to Raymond James Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 3:30 PM ET. Let's give Tampa a reason to smile again and send this group into bowl season on a high. Go Bulls, and Horns Up!

articles.title: Florida Atlantic vs South Florida: Caden Veltkamp Throws Four Through the Weather Delays, 35-14
articles.byline: Kaia Brightwater, The Florida Atlantic Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Atlantic Owls (7-4) 35, South Florida Bulls (6-5) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Boca Raton. Next: at East Carolina, Sat., Nov. 28, 1:00 PM ET, Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium, Greenville
articles.text:
The skies above Boca Raton kept stopping this game, and Caden Veltkamp kept starting it right back up. Florida Atlantic beat South Florida 35-14 on Saturday night at Flagler Credit Union Stadium, in a game that sat through multiple weather delays. We're sitting at 7-4 and 4-3 in league play, and the Owls are flying.

Veltkamp was surgical: 30 of 38 for 386 yards and four touchdowns. That's seven straight games with multiple touchdown throws, and he's up to 33 for the season. He came in second in the nation in touchdown throws, and nobody's slowing him down now.

Easton Messer caught two of them, from 8 and 24 yards in the third quarter, and he has 15 touchdown catches this year. Kelby Valsin was a machine, 12 catches for 112 yards, a 16-yard touchdown and a two-point catch. AJ Johnson got us started with a 36-yard score in the first quarter, and Dominique Henry had six catches for 106 yards, with a 41-yarder.

Collin Rogers drilled field goals from 48 and 28, the second with three seconds left in the half, and it was 20-0 at the break. By the end of the third quarter it was 35-7. South Florida never had an answer.

And the defense? The Bulls ran for 45 yards. Forty-five, on 27 carries. Khmari Johnson had a sack and a half, Tyson Rooks made 10 tackles, and Josh Roberts came up with an interception. South Florida threw it 49 times trying to catch up, and it never mattered. We also went 7 of 11 on third down, which is just showing off.

Beating your in-state rival at home, on a night that wouldn't stop getting interrupted, with your quarterback throwing darts? I'll sit through every delay for that.

Next up: at East Carolina on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 1:00 PM ET at Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium in Greenville. Eight wins sounds about right to me. Go Owls!

articles.title: Illinois vs Iowa: Katin Houser Throws for 318 Through a Broken Hand, Illini Fall, 34-17
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa Hawkeyes (9-2) 34, Illinois Fighting Illini (6-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign. Next: at Northwestern, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:30 PM ET, Ryan Field, Evanston
articles.text:
If you want to know what toughness looks like, watch Katin Houser. Playing through a broken hand and a broken nose, he threw for 318 yards and two touchdowns against the best scoring defense in the country. It still wasn't enough, and Iowa beat Illinois 34-17 at Gies Memorial Stadium. We're 6-5, 4-4 in the Big Ten.

For a half, we had the Hawkeyes rattled. Brayden Trimble caught a short one, tiptoed down the sideline, got sprung by an Eddie Kasper block and went 75 yards to tie it 10-10. Then Houser found Davin Stoffel from 11 with seven seconds left before halftime, and it was 17-17. That was more points than any of Iowa's previous four opponents had managed in an entire game.

Collin Dixon was terrific, eight catches for 142 yards. Trimble finished with four for 121. When Houser had a second to breathe, he made plays.

But we ran the ball 17 times for 28 yards, and you can't live like that against Iowa. This offense is missing a lot of people. Hudson Clement is out for the season, and so are Ca'Lil Valentine and Javari Barnett. In the second half we punted three times in the third quarter, got stopped on fourth down twice and threw an interception that Jaylen Watson ran back 40 yards for a touchdown.

Iowa ground out a 19-play, 91-yard drive that ate 10 minutes, and that was the ballgame. Our defense still fought. Matthew Bailey made 11 tackles, nine of them solo, Ben Clawson and James Kreutz had eight each, and Ismael Kante broke up two throws. Ethan Moczulski hit a 39-yard field goal in the first quarter.

That's two straight losses after a four-game winning streak, and it stings. But we're 6-5 with one more Saturday to play.

We're at Northwestern on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 12:30 PM ET at Ryan Field, and the Land of Lincoln Trophy is on the table. Go take it home to Champaign. Oskee-wow-wow!

articles.title: Iowa vs Illinois: L.J. Phillips Jr. Runs for 154 and the Hawkeyes Shut the Door After Halftime, 34-17
articles.matchup: Final: Iowa Hawkeyes (9-2) 34, Illinois Fighting Illini (6-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign. Next: vs Nebraska, Fri., Nov. 27, 12:00 PM ET, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City
articles.text:
Nobody grinds a team into dust like the Hawkeyes, and Illinois found that out the hard way. Tied 17-17 at halftime in Champaign, Iowa shut the Illini out the rest of the way and walked out of Gies Memorial Stadium with a 34-17 win. We're 9-2, 6-2 in the Big Ten, and that's four straight.

L.J. Phillips Jr. carried it 26 times for 154 yards and a touchdown, his third straight 100-yard game. Xavier Williams added 59 yards and a score. As a team we ran for 263 yards, and Illinois ran for 28. Twenty-eight! Our big guys up front ate all afternoon.

The drive of the year might be the one that put it away. Nineteen plays, 91 yards, about 10 minutes off the clock, and it ended with Hank Brown running a fourth-down draw in from 2 yards out for a 27-17 lead. We went 3 for 3 on fourth down all day and held the ball for 37:16. That's Kirk Ferentz football from the opening kick to the last snap.

Then Jaylen Watson jumped a throw and took it 40 yards the other way for a touchdown. 34-17. Good night, Champaign.

The first half was more fun for Illinois than I'd like. The Illini hit a 75-yarder and scored again with seven seconds left before halftime, putting up more points in one half than any of our previous four opponents managed in a whole game. Then the No. 1 scoring defense in the country slammed the door. Cam Buffington's interception set up Williams' touchdown, Anthony Hawkins made 11 tackles, and Jayden Montgomery broke up three throws.

Hank Brown went 13 of 26 for 138 yards and didn't throw an interception. Caden Buhr made field goals from 45 and 33. We've now won 15 of the last 17 against Illinois, and Ferentz is 15-4 against them.

Now it's Nebraska at Kinnick Stadium on Friday, Nov. 27, at 12:00 PM ET in the Heroes Game. Black and gold in every seat, please. Go Hawks!

articles.title: Sam Houston vs Middle Tennessee: Mason Holtzclaw Throws Three, Bearkats Come Up Just Short, 31-28
articles.byline: Lem Coxwell, The Sam Houston Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders (6-5) 31, Sam Houston Bearkats (1-10) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville. Next: at Florida International, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Pitbull Stadium, Miami
articles.text:
Our last drive ran out of room at the Middle Tennessee 36 with 14 seconds to go, and that's how close Sam Houston came on Saturday at Elliott T. Bowers Stadium. The Blue Raiders held on, 31-28. We're 1-10, 0-7 in Conference USA, and that's eight losses in a row.

Here's what I want everybody in Huntsville to know: this team didn't quit. We were down 21-7 in the second quarter and fought back to tie it 21-21. Mason Holtzclaw was sharp, 16 of 25 for 191 yards and three touchdowns, to Chris Reed from 15, Darrick Bledsoe III from 24 and Tim Burns Jr. from 30.

The defense took the ball away four times. Ishmel Atkins and Railyn Adams each intercepted Roman Gagliano, and we recovered two fumbles. Four takeaways in one afternoon! Dean Ford led us with seven tackles, and Caesar Magee broke up two throws.

Brett Holloway got us started with a 3-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Reed's catch came with 10 seconds left in the half, and Bledsoe's tied it midway through the third. Grady O'Neill caught seven balls for 65 yards, and Alton McCaskill ran 15 times for 65.

What hurt was one play. Right after we tied it, Terrence Brown went 75 yards untouched. Then we came up short on fourth down at our own 34, and they kicked a field goal. Holtzclaw found Burns from 30 to make it 31-28 with 5:35 left, and we got the ball back with a chance. It ended on downs.

We converted 8 of 16 third downs. We didn't lose a fumble. A lot went right. One play and one fourth down went wrong, and that's football.

One more game. We're at Florida International on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET at Pitbull Stadium in Miami to close the season. Go get win number two, Bearkats. Eat 'Em Up, Kats!

The defense took the ball away four times. Ishmel Atkins and Railyn Adams each intercepted Roman Gagliano, and we recovered two fumbles. Four takeaways in one afternoon! Dean Ford led us with seven tackles, and Caesar Magee broke up two throws.

Brett Holloway got us started with a 3-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Reed's catch came with 10 seconds left in the half, and Bledsoe's tied it midway through the third. Grady O'Neill caught seven balls for 65 yards, and Alton McCaskill ran 15 times for 65.

What hurt was one play. Right after we tied it, Terrence Brown went 75 yards untouched. Then we came up short on fourth down at our own 34, and they kicked a field goal. Holtzclaw found Burns from 30 to make it 31-28 with 5:35 left, and we got the ball back with a chance. It ended on downs.
We converted 8 of 16 third downs. We didn't lose a fumble. A lot went right. One play and one fourth down went wrong, and that's football.
One more game. We're at Florida International on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET at Pitbull Stadium in Miami to close the season. Go get win number two, Bearkats. Eat 'Em Up, Kats!

Mason Holtzclaw threw for 191 yards and three touchdowns, and Sam Houston rallied from 21-7 down to tie it 21-21.
Ishmel Atkins and Railyn Adams each had an interception as the Bearkats forced four turnovers.
Middle Tennessee handed us the ball four times and still needed a stop with 14 seconds left. Some bowl team.
Next: at Florida International, Saturday, Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Pitbull Stadium, Miami.

articles.title: Middle Tennessee vs Sam Houston: Terrence Brown's 75-Yard Run Makes the Blue Raiders Bowl Eligible, 31-28
articles.byline: Opal Stonebriar, The Middle Tennessee Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders (6-5) 31, Sam Houston Bearkats (1-10) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville. Next: vs New Mexico State, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro
articles.text:
Bowl season has a seat saved for Murfreesboro. Middle Tennessee beat Sam Houston 31-28 at Elliott T. Bowers Stadium in Huntsville on Saturday, and the Blue Raiders are bowl eligible for the first time since 2022. We're 6-5, 4-3 in Conference USA.

The play of the day belongs to Terrence Brown. Tied 21-21 in the third quarter, he took a handoff 75 yards through the middle and down the left side, and nobody laid a finger on him. That's six carries for 108 yards on the day, and one run I'll be replaying until Christmas.

We came out swinging. Antonio Martin scored from 10 on our opening drive, Roman Gagliano hit AJ Jones for a 6-yard touchdown, and Gagliano ran one in from 21 himself. It was 21-7 in the second quarter, and it felt comfortable.

Comfortable is a dangerous word. We gave it away four times, two fumbles and two interceptions, and Sam Houston climbed back to tie it. After Brown's run, the defense stuffed the Bearkats on fourth down at their own 34, and Dominic Bourgeois hit a 31-yard field goal for a 31-21 lead heading into the fourth.

It got tight again when Sam Houston scored with 5:35 left to make it 31-28. But the defense stood up one more time, and the Bearkats' last drive died on downs at our 36 with 14 seconds left. Korey Smith was everywhere, with 10 tackles and an interception. Christofer Noble added six tackles, and Reggie Johnson got a tackle for loss and two hurries.

Gagliano finished 18 of 29 for 189 yards and ran for 64 more. Cam'ron Lacy caught six for 73, Neo Clifton four for 52. We ran for 244 yards as a team and won a road game while giving the ball away four times. That's a tough team.

New Mexico State comes to Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET. Let's make it seven at home and give the bowl folks something to think about. Blue Raider proud!

articles.title: Missouri State vs Jacksonville State: Connor Lair's 79-Yard Run Builds a 20-3 Lead That Doesn't Hold, 25-20
articles.byline: Clementine Bilyeu, The Missouri State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Jacksonville State Gamecocks (8-3) 25, Missouri State Bears (4-7) 20, Sat., Nov. 21, AmFirst Stadium, Jacksonville. Next: vs Liberty, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield
articles.text:
Three quarters of the best football we've played all year, and then 15 minutes I'd like to erase from memory. Missouri State led Jacksonville State 20-3 at AmFirst Stadium heading into the fourth quarter, and lost 25-20. We're 4-7, 3-4 in Conference USA.

Let's start with the good, because it was really good. Connor Lair broke a 79-yard touchdown run in the second quarter and finished with 109 yards on just 12 carries. Henry Belin IV went 20 of 29 for 161 yards and hit Isaiah Myers for a 14-yard touchdown in the third. Yousef Obeid made both of his field goals, from 35 and 47.

The defense was rolling, too. Jared Lloyd made 10 tackles, and J.J. O'Neal and Jashawn Cooper had seven apiece. Khalil Anderson got a sack. We didn't give the ball away once, and we held the ball for 32:03 against the team that already owns a spot in the league title game.

Then came the fourth quarter. We got stopped on fourth-and-goal early, and that was the first crack. Jacksonville State went 97 yards in four plays. We went three-and-out. They scored again. We went three-and-out again. They scored again. Twenty-two straight points, and Caden Creel had his hands on all three touchdowns.

We had one last chance and came up short on fourth down with 1:01 left. That one's going to sit with me all week.

Jmariyae Robinson had six catches for 59 yards, and Breezy Dubar ran hard all day, 17 carries for 56 yards. Jeron Askren caught three for 40. These guys deserved a better final 15 minutes, and that's the truth.

Next up is the finale, Liberty at Robert W. Plaster Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET. The Flames haven't lost a league game all year. Wouldn't it be something if Springfield was where that changed? Go Bears!

articles.title: Jacksonville State vs Missouri State: Caden Creel Leads a 22-Point Fourth Quarter, 25-20
articles.byline: Burl Ashcraft-Neeley, The Jacksonville State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Jacksonville State Gamecocks (8-3) 25, Missouri State Bears (4-7) 20, Sat., Nov. 21, AmFirst Stadium, Jacksonville. Next: at Delaware, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Delaware Stadium, Newark
articles.text:
Down 20-3 after three quarters at AmFirst Stadium, and I'll admit I'd started doing the math on a loss. Then Caden Creel grabbed the fourth quarter by the collar, and Jacksonville State came all the way back to beat Missouri State 25-20 on Saturday. We're 8-3, 6-1 in Conference USA, with a spot in the title game already clinched.

Creel threw two touchdowns and ran for a third in the final 13 minutes. He finished 24 of 32 for 266 yards, plus 75 more on the ground. We scored 22 points in the fourth quarter and gave up zero. That's not a comeback. That's a heist.

Here's how it went down. First, the defense stuffed Missouri State on fourth-and-goal early in the quarter. Then we went 97 yards in four plays. Creel hit Jameson Scissum for 32, then found Deondre Johnson in stride for a 59-yard touchdown, and Creel converted the two-pointer. It was 20-11 with 12:41 left.

The defense forced a three-and-out, Caleb Nix brought the punt back 16 yards to midfield, and Creel scored on a 22-yard run. Suddenly it was 20-18. Another three-and-out, and Creel hit Khristian Lando for 21 yards and the lead, 25-20, with 5:39 left. Then a fourth-down stop with 1:01 to go sealed it.

And get this. We had nine penalties for 90 yards through three quarters and one for 5 yards in the fourth. When it counted, this team cleaned it up. We piled up 205 of our 417 yards in the fourth quarter alone. Brennan Core made 10 tackles, Morven Joseph had nine, and Jacob Cruz had 1 1/2 tackles for loss.

Luke Gilbert caught eight balls for 50 yards. Garrison Rippa's 33-yard field goal was our only score through three quarters, and I'll thank him for keeping us breathing.

Next up: at Delaware on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 3:30 PM ET at Delaware Stadium in Newark, and then Liberty in the Conference USA title game on Dec. 4. You can bury these Gamecocks for three quarters, and they'll still dig out. Go Gamecocks!

articles.title: Charlotte vs Tulsa: Khamani Alexander's 68-Yard Run Gives the 49ers a Lead Before It Slips Away, 42-14
articles.matchup: Final: Tulsa Golden Hurricane (7-4) 42, Charlotte 49ers (1-10) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, H. A. Chapman Stadium, Tulsa. Next: vs Navy, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte
articles.text:
For one glorious snap, the whole year looked like it might flip. Khamani Alexander took the first play of the second half 68 yards for a touchdown, and Charlotte led Tulsa 14-7 at H. A. Chapman Stadium. Then the Golden Hurricane scored 35 straight points, and it finished Tulsa 42, Charlotte 14. We're 1-10, 1-6 in the American.

I'm not going to dress it up. But I'm also not going to skip the good stuff, because there was some. Alexander ran 10 times for 93 yards, and we ran for 173 yards as a team at 5.6 a carry. We actually won the time of possession, 30:09 to 29:51.

The first half was a real fight. Nobody scored in the first quarter. Conner Harrell found Jaden Barnes for a 21-yard touchdown to put us up 7-0 early in the second, and it was 7-7 at the break. Barnes caught seven balls on the day and kept moving the chains.

Then Baylor Hayes got hot, and we couldn't cool him off. Four touchdown throws, three of them to Oran Singleton Jr., and a touchdown run to tie it. Harrell finished 16 of 26 for 69 yards, and we didn't score again after Alexander's run. We went 0 for 3 on fourth down, and every one of those hurt.

Gavin Willis made 12 tackles and Dy'Lon Womack had 10. Those two never stopped running to the ball, even after the scoreboard got ugly. Collin Gill added eight tackles. That's the kind of effort that tells me this locker room hasn't quit on anything.

This has been a hard year in the Queen City. Nobody's going to sugarcoat 1-10. But there's one more chance to send everybody home happy.

Navy comes to Jerry Richardson Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 12:00 PM ET for the season finale. Wear green, get loud and give this group a proper sendoff. Go Niners!

articles.title: Tulsa vs Charlotte: Baylor Hayes Throws Four, Oran Singleton Jr. Catches Three, 42-14
articles.matchup: Final: Tulsa Golden Hurricane (7-4) 42, Charlotte 49ers (1-10) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, H. A. Chapman Stadium, Tulsa. Next: at UTSA, Fri., Nov. 27, 12:00 PM ET, Alamodome, San Antonio
articles.text:
Four in a row, five of the last six, and this Golden Hurricane team just keeps getting better. Tulsa 42, Charlotte 14 at H. A. Chapman Stadium on Saturday. We're 7-4, 4-3 in the American, already bowl eligible for the first time since 2021, and playing like we want more than one extra game.

Baylor Hayes, take a bow. He went 21 of 29 for 285 yards and four touchdowns, and he ran for another from 9 yards. He has thrown 10 of his 20 touchdowns this season in the last three games. That's a quarterback who figured it out right when November showed up.

Oran Singleton Jr. caught three of those, from 55, 14 and 13 yards, and finished with seven catches for 116 yards. He has 10 touchdown catches this year and six in the last three games. Hayes to Singleton might be the two best words in Tulsa right now.

Don't let the final fool you. It was 7-7 at halftime, and Khamani Alexander broke a 68-yard touchdown run on the first play of the second half to give Charlotte a 14-7 lead. For about three minutes, I was pacing. Then Hayes ran it in to tie it, and we scored 35 straight points.

Damari Alston caught a 12-yard touchdown and ran for 73 yards on 12 carries. Trequan Jones put the bow on it with a 70-yard touchdown run, and he finished with 109 yards on just 10 carries. Javon Ross had five catches for 74, and Jimmy Calloway grabbed four for 70.

The defense held Charlotte to 86 yards through the air. Kyran Duhon hurried the quarterback five times, and Tyson Williams made nine tackles. We've outscored our last three opponents 140-45. Read that one again, slowly.

Next up is the regular-season finale at UTSA on Friday, Nov. 27, at 12:00 PM ET in the Alamodome. Nobody in this league wants a piece of the 'Cane right now. Go Hurricane!

articles.title: Alabama vs Chattanooga: Austin Mack Throws Four Touchdowns in His First Start, 47-0
articles.matchup: Final: Alabama Crimson Tide (9-2) 47, Chattanooga Mocs (7-5) 0, Sat., Nov. 21, Bryant-Denny Stadium, Tuscaloosa. Next: vs Auburn, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Bryant-Denny Stadium, Tuscaloosa
articles.text:
Austin Mack waited years for a Saturday like this one, and he didn't waste a snap of it. In his first college start, with Keelon Russell held out to protect the ankle he hurt against LSU, Mack threw four touchdowns and ran for another as Alabama blanked Chattanooga 47-0 at Bryant-Denny Stadium. We're 9-2, 6-2 in the SEC, and the Iron Bowl is next.

Mack has been with Kalen DeBoer since 2023 at Washington, and he's spent his time here backing up the guys ahead of him and waiting his turn. On Saturday he went 20 of 25 for 254 yards. He found Ryan Coleman-Williams from 8, Lotzeir Brooks from 3, Rico Scott from 29 at the end of a two-minute drive before halftime and Noah Rogers from 8 in the third quarter. Four different guys in the end zone. That's a quarterback reading the field, not forcing it.

He scored first, too, on a 1-yard run in the opening quarter. Then the defense got a safety, Conor Talty hit a 24-yard field goal, and it snowballed. It was 33-0 at halftime and 40-0 when the regulars took a seat in the third quarter.

Now, about that defense. Chattanooga finished with 86 yards. Eighty-six! Five first downs, 27 rushing yards and 1 of 9 on third down. Yhonzae Pierre had a sack and two tackles for loss, QB Reese had 1 1/2 tackles for loss, and Isaia Faga was in the backfield too. Chattanooga never had room to breathe.

We ran for 263 yards and put up 553 in all. Daniel Hill went for 75 on 10 carries, Trae'shawn Brown for 70 on six, and Kevin Riley added 59 on the ground and a 15-yard touchdown catch in the fourth. Kaleb Edwards caught three balls for 63.

The coaches agreed to shorten the fourth quarter to 10 minutes, which tells you how this one went. Credit to the Mocs for making the trip and playing it out. But this day belonged to the 98,552 who got to watch a patient quarterback make the most of his first start.

Auburn comes to Bryant-Denny on Saturday, Nov. 28, with the kickoff time still to be announced. The Tide just found out it has two quarterbacks who can win in this building. Roll Tide, and beat Auburn!

Yhonzae Pierre had a sack and two tackles for loss, QB Reese had 1 1/2 tackles for loss, and Isaia Faga was in the backfield too. Chattanooga never had room to breathe.

Auburn comes to Bryant-Denny on Saturday, Nov. 28, with the kickoff time still to be announced. The Tide just found out it has two quarterbacks who can win in this building. Roll Tide, and beat Auburn!

articles.title: Western Kentucky vs Liberty: Brock Glenn Keeps Swinging, but the Bowl Streak Ends in Lynchburg, 45-14
articles.byline: Thurman 'Tops' Whitsitt, The Western Kentucky Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Liberty Flames (10-1) 45, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers (4-7) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg. Next: vs Kennesaw State, Sat., Nov. 28, 1:00 PM ET, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green
articles.text:
Seven straight seasons of bowl games with Tyson Helton in charge, and that run ended on Saturday in Lynchburg. Liberty beat Western Kentucky 45-14 at Williams Stadium, and at 4-7, 3-4 in Conference USA, the Hilltoppers can't reach six wins this year. I'm not going to pretend that doesn't sting.

The game was decided early. Liberty scored on its first offensive play, an 81-yard throw, and led 21-0 after one quarter and 28-0 at halftime. The Flames converted 9 of 12 third downs, and we just couldn't get them off the field when it still mattered.

But I'm proud of how this group kept swinging. Brock Glenn threw 47 times, completed 24 for 273 yards and didn't throw an interception, even while getting sacked three times. On the last play of the third quarter, he found Coleson Arends for a 25-yard touchdown to get us on the board. Then in the fourth he ran one in himself from 16 yards out.

Zion Taylor led us with six catches for 68 yards. Jyziah Rockwell caught three for 64, with a 37-yarder, and Moussa Barry had three for 55. We went 3 for 6 on fourth down because we weren't about to stop trying.

The defense took the ball away twice, recovering two Liberty fumbles. Jaylen Wester was everywhere with 11 tackles and two for loss, and Jaylen Pollard added nine. We didn't give it away once.

Let's be honest about the hard part. We ran 29 times for 54 yards. You can't live on one side of the offense against a team that's won 10 straight. A week ago we beat Jacksonville State, so we know what this team looks like when it's rolling.

One more Saturday on the Hill. Kennesaw State comes to Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium on Nov. 28 at 1:00 PM ET for the finale. Send the red towels flying for this group one last time. Go Tops!

articles.title: Liberty vs Western Kentucky: Deshawn Purdie's 344 Yards Make It 10 Straight for the Flames, 45-14
articles.matchup: Final: Liberty Flames (10-1) 45, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers (4-7) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, Williams Stadium (VA), Lynchburg. Next: at Missouri State, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield
articles.text:
Ten in a row, and the first one with a number next to our name. Liberty played its first game as an AP Top 25 team since 2023 on Saturday, and the No. 22 Flames treated Williams Stadium to a 45-14 thumping of Western Kentucky. We're 10-1 and a perfect 7-0 in Conference USA.

It took one play. Deshawn Purdie dropped back on our first offensive snap and hit Makai Jackson for an 81-yard touchdown, and the rout was on. Purdie finished 19 of 25 for a season-high 344 yards and two touchdown throws, and he ran for another from 18 yards out, the second-longest run of his career. That Wake Forest transfer is playing his best ball in November.

We were up 21-0 after one quarter. Ethan Vasko punched one in from 3, Purdie scored his 18-yarder, and then Terron Kellman broke a 39-yard touchdown run in the second quarter for a 28-0 halftime lead. Kellman led us with 88 yards on just seven carries.

Last week we ran for 370 yards against Middle Tennessee. This week we went to the air instead, and it didn't matter one bit. Jamari Person caught five balls for 87 yards and a 37-yard touchdown that made it 35-0. Darius Copeland had four catches for 65, and Rashawn Cunningham hauled in a 46-yarder. Chase Reeves knocked down a 50-yard field goal, and Jaylen Henderson capped the day with a 50-yard touchdown run.

We converted 9 of 12 third downs and rolled up 560 yards. The defense held Western Kentucky to 54 rushing yards on 29 carries and sacked Brock Glenn three times, two of them by Markus Clark. Derrell Farrar made 11 tackles. This was a team that beat Jacksonville State last week, and we never let them breathe.

That's six conference wins by 16 points or more in seven league games. Lynchburg, this is a special group, and it's time everybody outside Virginia noticed.

Next up: at Missouri State on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET at Robert W. Plaster Stadium in Springfield. Then a title game waits. Keep the flame lit, and Flames, Fly!

articles.title: Mississippi State vs Tennessee Tech: Evans, Puckett and a 90-Yard Gayten Run Snap the Skid, 34-16
articles.byline: Wade Pettus, The Mississippi State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Mississippi State Bulldogs (5-6) 34, Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles (9-3) 16, Sat., Nov. 21, Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville. Next: at Ole Miss, Fri., Nov. 27, 12:00 PM ET, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford
articles.text:
The skid is dead and buried. Mississippi State 34, Tennessee Tech 16 at Davis Wade Stadium on Saturday, and the six-game losing streak is finally gone. We're 5-6, and the cowbells sounded like they'd been saving it up since September.

Thirty-four points is the most we've scored since the 41-34 win against South Carolina on Sept. 19. That's how long it had been, folks. Puckett had his best day in maroon, 17 of 25 for a career-high 232 yards and two touchdown throws. He threw one interception, and I'll forgive it, because everything else was crisp.

Anthony Evans III was the headliner. Eight catches, a season-best 129 yards and a 53-yard touchdown in the second quarter that put us ahead for good, 14-10. He's at 929 yards for the season and needs 125 more to own the school record. Get that man the ball on Friday, please and thank you.

Kyle Ferrie added field goals from 48 and 36, the second one right before halftime, and we went to the locker room up 20-10. Marquis Johnson caught a slant and took it 41 yards for a touchdown in the third quarter, and he finished with four catches for 70. Then, on the very first play of the fourth quarter, Xavier Gayten ran 90 yards to the end zone. Ninety! He had three carries for 100 yards on the day. Somebody check that kid's math.

Credit Tennessee Tech. The Golden Eagles came to Starkville at 9-2, held the ball for 40:59 and made us earn it. But our defense lived in their backfield with 10 tackles for loss and four sacks. Jardin Gilbert made 10 tackles and intercepted a throw, and LaKendrick James had 1 1/2 tackles for loss and a share of a sack.

This is what we've been waiting on all fall: receivers winning, a quarterback standing tall and a defense that hits first. It looked like the team we thought we had.

Now comes the one that matters most. We head to Vaught-Hemingway Stadium for the Egg Bowl on Friday, Nov. 27, at 12:00 PM ET, and a win puts us at six and sends us bowling. Ring 'em loud from Starkville to Oxford. Hail State!

articles.title: West Virginia vs Houston: Michael Hawkins Jr. Makes History, Mountaineers Fall at the Horn, 34-31
articles.byline: Jolene Buckhannon, The West Virginia Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Houston Cougars (8-3) 34, West Virginia Mountaineers (5-6) 31, Sat., Nov. 21, Milan Puskar Stadium, Morgantown. Next: at Utah, Fri., Nov. 27, 9:00 PM ET, Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City
articles.text:
Ten points up in the third quarter at Milan Puskar Stadium, and somehow it slipped away on the last snap of the day. Houston 34, West Virginia 31, on a 23-yard field goal with zeroes on the clock, and that's three losses in a row for the second time this season. We're 5-6, 2-6 in the Big 12, and it stings all the way down to the Monongahela.

Before I get mad, let me brag, because Michael Hawkins Jr. earned it. He became the first quarterback in West Virginia history to throw for 2,000 yards and run for 1,000 in the same season. He ran 18 times for 98 yards on Saturday to get to 1,055, with a 10-yard touchdown run and a 3-yard scoring throw to John Neider.

And Cam Cook? Twenty-five carries, 131 yards and an 8-yard touchdown, and he's at 1,215 for the year. Hawkins and Cook are the first West Virginia pair to both clear 1,000 rushing yards in a season since Pat White and Steve Slaton, who did it in 2006 and 2007. Those are sacred names in this state, and these two belong right next to them.

We ran for 329 yards as a team, the fourth time this year we've gone past 300 on the ground. Amari Latimer scored from 3 before halftime, Hawkins ran one in early in the third, and it was 31-21. I'll admit I was already humming the fight song.

Then the offense went cold. On our last five drives, Jack Cassidy missed from 42 and we punted four times. Hawkins took a hard hit late in the fourth quarter, after playing on a sore ankle, and didn't come back. Houston tied it 31-31 with 5:25 left, our final punt came back 22 yards to our 38, and you know how it ended.

The defense fought. Cam Torbor made 11 tackles and Isaiah Patterson had nine. But a freshman quarterback making his first start went 18 of 28 for 268 yards against us, and Houston converted 9 of 19 third downs. We never got to him enough.

Next up is Utah on Friday, Nov. 27, at 9:00 PM ET at Rice-Eccles Stadium, and the math couldn't be simpler: win, and we're bowl eligible. Country roads, carry this bunch west one more time. Let's Go!

articles.title: Houston vs West Virginia: Freshman Keisean Henderson and Jonathan Dimas Win It at the Horn, 34-31
articles.matchup: Final: Houston Cougars (8-3) 34, West Virginia Mountaineers (5-6) 31, Sat., Nov. 21, Milan Puskar Stadium, Morgantown. Next: vs Baylor, Sat., Nov. 28, 9:30 PM ET, TDECU Stadium, Houston
articles.text:
Coogs, the kid has arrived. Keisean Henderson made his first start on Saturday in Morgantown, filling in for an injured Conner Weigman, and he walked out of Milan Puskar Stadium a winner when Jonathan Dimas drilled a 23-yard field goal as time ran out. Houston 34, West Virginia 31. We're 8-3, 5-3 in the Big 12, and my voice is gone.

Henderson hadn't played in two months. His very first throw, on our third snap, went 68 yards to a wide-open Amare Thomas for a touchdown. Hello, Big 12. He finished 18 of 28 for 268 yards without a turnover, and the freshman never once looked rattled in a loud road stadium.

Then there's Makhi Hughes. Nineteen carries, 158 yards, three touchdowns, a season high, with a 71-yard burst mixed in. He scored from 21, from 2 and from 3, and that last one is the one I'll be telling people about at Thanksgiving.

Because this one got scary. West Virginia ran right at us for 329 yards and led 31-21 early in the third quarter. Dimas got us a 34-yard field goal late in the third to make it 31-24. Then Henderson took off for 8 yards and then 9 more himself, and Hughes punched it in from the 3. Tied 31-31 with 5:25 left.

That's when our defense found its feet. On its last five drives, West Virginia missed a 42-yard field goal and punted four times. Jaden Yates was everywhere with 16 tackles and two and a half for loss, and Sione Fotu chipped in nine. On the last of those punts, Trent Walker brought it back 22 yards to the West Virginia 38. We pushed it inside the 5, and Dimas did the rest.

We went 9 of 19 on third down, never gave the ball away and bounced right back from that double-digit loss at Colorado last week. That's a grown-up road win, led by a freshman making his first start.

Baylor comes to TDECU Stadium for the regular-season finale on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 9:30 PM ET. Third Ward, bring the noise for the freshman. Go Coogs!

articles.title: Georgia State vs Marshall: Pereira Throws Three, Panthers Fall by a Point in Huntington
articles.byline: Malik Overstreet, The Georgia State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Marshall Thundering Herd (6-5) 28, Georgia State Panthers (5-6) 27, Sat., Nov. 21, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington. Next: vs Louisiana, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta
articles.text:
Two seconds left. Rodshaun Dorsey slips behind everybody at the back of the end zone, stretches, gets both feet down, and Georgia State is one kick from overtime in Huntington. Then the kick missed. Marshall 28, Georgia State 27 on Saturday, and we're 5-6.

I'm going to be sick about that one for a while, Panther fans. But let me tell you how good this team played.

We came out flying. Ayden Pereira hit Grant Hollier for a 4-yard touchdown, then hit Derrick Avery Jr. for 55 yards and another score. We led 14-0 in the first quarter. After Marshall answered twice, Lanear McCrary Jr. powered in from 4 yards to put us back up 21-13 at halftime.

Pereira finished 16 of 29 for 249 yards and three touchdown throws. Qwantavius Wiggins was a load all day, 13 carries for 114 yards with a long of 36. McCrary added 54 yards. Kyle Washington caught three balls for 57. As a team we ran for 209 yards and outgained Marshall 458 to 351.

So how did we lose? Marshall hit a 94-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter that hurt. Then in the fourth, they scored, ran a trick two-point play to tie it at 21, and scored again with 6:30 left. We didn't have an answer until the final drive.

And what a final drive. Six plays, 76 yards, down 28-21 with the clock dying, and Pereira kept firing. Dorsey's catch was a beauty. Then Samer Layous' extra point went wide, and Marshall recovered the onside kick. Layous is a good kicker and a good teammate, and nobody on our side is pointing fingers at him.

Donovan Faria made 13 tackles, and Tyson McCrary broke up a throw. This team kept swinging all night.

Here's the good news. One more win and we're bowl eligible. Next up: Louisiana at Center Parc Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET. Atlanta, show up and be loud. Go Panthers!

We came out flying. Ayden Pereira hit Grant Hollier for a 4-yard touchdown, then hit Derrick Avery Jr. for 55 yards and another score. We led 14-0 in the first quarter. After Marshall answered twice, Lanear McCrary Jr. powered in from 4 yards to put us back up 21-13 at halftime.

Pereira finished 16 of 29 for 249 yards and three touchdown throws. Qwantavius Wiggins was a load all day, 13 carries for 114 yards with a long of 36. McCrary added 54 yards. Kyle Washington caught three balls for 57. As a team we ran for 209 yards and outgained Marshall 458 to 351.

So how did we lose? Marshall hit a 94-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter that hurt. Then in the fourth, they scored, ran a trick two-point play to tie it at 21, and scored again with 6:30 left. We didn't have an answer until the final drive.

And what a final drive. Six plays, 76 yards, down 28-21 with the clock dying, and Pereira kept firing. Dorsey's catch was a beauty. Then Samer Layous' extra point went wide, and Marshall recovered the onside kick. Layous is a good kicker and a good teammate, and nobody on our side is pointing fingers at him.
Donovan Faria made 13 tackles, and Tyson McCrary broke up a throw. This team kept swinging all night.
Here's the good news. One more win and we're bowl eligible. Next up: Louisiana at Center Parc Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET. Atlanta, show up and be loud. Go Panthers!

summary.text: Georgia State lost 28-27 at Marshall on Saturday, Nov. 21, after missing the extra point following a touchdown with two seconds left. The Panthers are 5-6.
Ayden Pereira threw for 249 yards and three touchdowns, and Qwantavius Wiggins ran for 114 yards.
Georgia State outgained Marshall 458-351 and ran for 209 yards.
Marshall needed a trick play and a missed kick to beat us. We'll see them again.
Next: vs Louisiana, Saturday, Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta.

articles.title: Marshall vs Georgia State: Del Rio-Wilson Rallies the Herd, Bowl Ticket Punched 28-27
articles.matchup: Final: Marshall Thundering Herd (6-5) 28, Georgia State Panthers (5-6) 27, Sat., Nov. 21, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington. Next: at UL Monroe, Sat., Nov. 28, 1:00 PM ET, Malone Stadium, Monroe
articles.text:
My heart is still somewhere on the Joan C. Edwards turf. Marshall 28, Georgia State 27 on Saturday in Huntington, and the Thundering Herd are bowl eligible at 6-5. Huntington, this one's for you.

We spotted Georgia State 14 points in the first quarter, and I had my head in my hands. Then Carlos Del Rio-Wilson went to work. He hit Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw for 21 yards, and a few minutes later he found Chris Culliver on a 94-yard catch-and-run that had the whole stadium on its feet. Culliver's only catch of the day, and he made it count.

Early in the fourth, Del Rio-Wilson threw a 5-yard touchdown to Toby Payne to cut it to 21-19, and then we got creative with the two-point try. Receiver Owen Sweeney took the ball and threw it back to Del Rio-Wilson. Tied at 21! Coach, I love you.

Then, with 6:30 left, Del Rio-Wilson ran it in himself from 2 yards out. 28-21. He finished 12 of 23 for 199 yards and three touchdown throws, plus that rushing score. Gutsy, gritty, all heart.

And then the scariest final minute of the season. Georgia State marched 76 yards and scored on a 31-yard throw with two seconds left. Down one, they tried the extra point to tie it, and it sailed wide. Then we recovered the onside kick, took a knee, and Huntington exhaled.

Our defense bent a bunch, I won't lie. Georgia State ran for 209 yards. But Caleb Clark-Glover made 11 tackles, Josh Pierre-Louis had a sack, and Kelvon McBride grabbed an interception. We didn't give it away once, and that mattered in a one-point game.

Six wins. A bowl game. After the way this season has gone at times, I'll take it with a smile.

Next up: at UL Monroe, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 1:00 PM ET at Malone Stadium. Seven wins and a bowl to pack for. Go Herd!

articles.title: Troy vs Georgia Southern: Goose Crowder Hits Jordan Lovett for 47, Trojans Fall 45-7
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Southern Eagles (7-4) 45, Troy Trojans (4-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 21, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL), Troy. Next: at Arkansas State, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:00 PM ET, Centennial Bank Stadium, Jonesboro
articles.text:
No sugarcoating from me, Trojan fans. Georgia Southern 45, Troy 7 on Saturday at Veterans Memorial Stadium, and we're 4-7 and 2-5 in the Sun Belt. It was a rough afternoon at home.

It went wrong on the very first snap. Goose Crowder's throw got picked off and returned to our 6, and the Eagles scored two plays later. They led 14-0 after a quarter and 21-0 at halftime. Max Johnson only missed four throws all day. When a quarterback gets that hot, you need your offense to answer, and ours couldn't get going.

We ran it 21 times for minus-7 yards. I had to read that twice. Georgia Southern got two sacks from one guy, and we put the ball on the ground twice and lost both. That's three turnovers, and you can't beat anybody like that, much less a team sitting near the top of the conference.

The bright spot came late in the third quarter. Crowder dropped one in to Jordan Lovett for a 47-yard touchdown, and for a minute the stadium had some life. Lovett finished with four catches for 78 yards and was our best weapon all day. Crowder went 17 of 26 for 134 yards. Jaheim Merriweather caught three for 20, and Noreel White had four grabs.

Our defense kept battling even when the offense couldn't give it a breather. The Eagles kept the ball for 35:26. Justin Powe made nine tackles. Jamarion Keyes had eight and forced a fumble. Keno Jones had eight with a tackle and a half for loss. Marlin Odom added seven and broke up a throw.

This team has had a tough year, but these seniors have given a lot to this program. They deserve a good send-off.

One more chance to end on a high note. Next up: at Arkansas State, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 3:00 PM ET at Centennial Bank Stadium in Jonesboro. Let's go get one. Go Trojans!

articles.title: Georgia Southern vs Troy: Max Johnson Throws Three, Eagles Smother Trojans 45-7
articles.byline: Royce Ogeechee, The Georgia Southern Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Southern Eagles (7-4) 45, Troy Trojans (4-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 21, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL), Troy. Next: vs Louisiana Tech, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro
articles.text:
First snap of the game, Brandon Tyson jumps the route, steals it and races 26 yards to the Troy 6. That set the tone for the whole afternoon. Georgia Southern 45, Troy 7 on Saturday, and the Eagles are 7-4 and 6-1 in the Sun Belt. Hail Southern!

Max Johnson needed one drive to cash in. Even after a holding flag backed us up, he found Alex Taylor from 12 yards out for a 7-0 lead. Later in the first quarter he dropped a 45-yard beauty into Andre Greene Jr.'s hands. Right before halftime he hit Jeremiah Ware from 22. Three touchdown throws, a 21-0 lead at the break, and Johnson finished 22 of 26 for 227 yards. Twenty-two of twenty-six. Surgical.

And then there's our defense, which I'd like to have bronzed. Troy ran the ball 21 times for minus-7 yards. Minus seven! MJ Stroud had two sacks and recovered a fumble. Jeremiah Ticket fell on another one late. We took the ball away three times and didn't give it away once. Troy had 127 yards of offense all day.

The second half was a victory lap. Tripp Bryant knocked through a 35-yarder and went 6 for 6 on extra points. Weston Bryan came in and hit Greene for a 22-yard touchdown, Greene's second of the day. Taeo Todd broke a 19-yard touchdown run and had a 41-yard catch, and Ty Cummings punched in an 8-yarder to finish it.

Taylor caught six balls for 70 yards. Greene had four for 97. Todd ran eight times for 66. Everybody ate.

This team has found a gear in November, and it's fun to watch. Seven wins, a great Sun Belt record, and a defense playing nasty.

Now let's finish it at home. Next up: Louisiana Tech at Paulson Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, at noon ET. Statesboro, bring the noise and bring the eagle. Hail Southern!

articles.title: Northern Illinois vs North Dakota State: Taron Dickens Rallies Huskies From 28 Down in Fargo
articles.byline: Nola Brandvik, The Northern Illinois Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: North Dakota State Bison (9-2) 31, Northern Illinois Huskies (0-11) 25, Sat., Nov. 21, Fargodome, Fargo. Next: vs UTEP, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Huskie Stadium, Dekalb
articles.text:
Down 31-3 in the Fargodome, with the bus ride home looking awfully tempting, my Huskies decided to make it a ballgame. It finished 31-25, Bison, and we're 0-11. But don't tell me this team quit.

The first half was rough, no way around it. The Bison hit four long touchdown throws and kicked a 51-yard field goal at the gun. JJ Schlenhardt's 36-yarder was our only answer before halftime.

Then Taron Dickens caught fire. Late in the third quarter he hit La'Don Bryant for a 7-yard touchdown, and then threw the two-point conversion to Afy Ibekwe. Early in the fourth, he found Ibekwe again from 17 yards. And with 2:46 left, he capped a 96-yard drive with a 47-yard strike to DeAree Rogers. Twenty-two straight points. Suddenly it was 31-25, and the dome got real quiet.

Dickens finished 20 of 29 for 260 yards and three touchdowns. Rogers caught six balls for 116 yards. Ibekwe had six for 81. Elijah Porter ran 17 times for 107 yards, and Telly Johnson Jr. added 61 on 11 carries. We actually outgained the Bison, 433 yards to 414.

On defense, Jashawn Nelson made 10 tackles with a sack. Kole Sneed had a sack and three tackles for loss. Liam Lindo picked off Nathan Hayes and returned it 28 yards. Those guys never stopped hitting.

The heartbreak is the ending. We needed one more stop to get the ball back, and North Dakota State ran out the clock. That's been our year in a sentence. So close, so many times.

But here's what I'll remember. A winless team, on the road, came back from 28 down and made the Bison sweat in their own building. That's character.

Next up: UTEP at Huskie Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 3:30 PM ET. Last game of the year, at home in DeKalb. Let's get that first win. Go Huskies!

articles.title: North Dakota State vs Northern Illinois: Nathan Hayes Throws Four, Bison Hold On, 31-25
articles.byline: Ingeborg 'Inga' Halvorsen, The North Dakota State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: North Dakota State Bison (9-2) 31, Northern Illinois Huskies (0-11) 25, Sat., Nov. 21, Fargodome, Fargo. Next: at San José State, Fri., Nov. 27, 3:30 PM ET, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose
articles.text:
Nathan Hayes threw four touchdowns in the Fargodome on Saturday, a career high, and for about 40 minutes it looked like a laugher. North Dakota State 31, Northern Illinois 25. We're 9-2 and 6-2 in the Mountain West, and I'm still catching my breath from the last quarter and a half.

Let's do the fun part first. Hayes dished it out like hot dish at a church potluck. Jackson Williams from 47 yards in the first quarter. Mekhi Collins from 35. Jett Zabel from 22. Then, on our first drive of the third quarter, Jordan McCants from 10, and it was 31-3. Hayes went 15 of 23 for 247 yards. Williams caught six balls for 104 yards.

Drew Klein drilled a 51-yard field goal as the first half ended, and the dome went nuts. Four extra points, too. Perfect day for the big leg.

Then Northern Illinois remembered it had a quarterback. Taron Dickens threw three touchdowns in the second half, and the Huskies scored 22 straight points. The last one, a 47-yarder, made it 31-25 with 2:46 left, and I'm not ashamed to say I was biting my mittens.

And then the Bison did what the Bison do. We got the ball back and ran out the clock. No drama, no heroics, just first downs. DJ Scott led our ground game with 11 carries for 86 yards. We went 8 for 12 on third down, and that's how you close.

The defense bent but made the plays it had to. Jaylen Archibald and Taylen Eady each intercepted Dickens. Donovan Woolen made nine tackles with a sack. Obald Niyonkuru had a sack and two tackles for loss. Gavin Sell added seven stops.

I'll take the win, but we can't take our foot off the gas like that again. Not with what's left on the schedule.

Next up: at San José State, Friday, Nov. 27, at 3:30 PM ET at CEFCU Stadium. Pack sunscreen instead of snow boots for once. Go Bison!

articles.title: Texas A&M vs Oklahoma: Ray Coney Makes 19 Tackles, Aggies Fade in Norman
articles.byline: Colt Wendeborn, The Texas A&M Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Oklahoma Sooners (7-4) 28, Texas A&M Aggies (4-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 21, Memorial Stadium (Norman, OK), Norman. Next: vs Texas, Fri., Nov. 27, 7:30 PM ET, Kyle Field, College Station
articles.text:
Ray Coney made 19 tackles in Norman on Saturday, and the whole Aggie defense rode on his back. Nineteen! Oklahoma 28, Texas A&M 7, and we're 4-7, but nobody can say that young man didn't empty the tank.

We had a new quarterback, too. Coach Elko handed sophomore Brady Hart the keys for the first time, and early on the kid looked the part. Early in the second quarter he led a 96-yard drive, hitting Mario Craver for 39 yards and then Isaiah Horton for a 36-yard touchdown. We were up 7-0 in Norman, and Aggie fans everywhere sat up straight.

Our defense was rolling, too. Marco Jones intercepted John Mateer in the end zone. Tawfiq Byard recovered a Mateer fumble and returned it 13 yards. Two takeaways in the second quarter, and we still led with less than three minutes left in the half.

That's when it slipped. Oklahoma went 92 yards and tied it with 22 seconds before halftime, and the second half was rough. Hart finished 8 of 20 for 131 yards. We ran 32 times for 54 yards. And down 14-7 late, a throw got picked off and turned into another Sooner touchdown on the next play. The fourth quarter got away from us, 21-0.

But back to Coney. Nineteen tackles, plus a share of our only sack with Bryce Perry-Wright. Dalton Brooks made eight tackles and broke up two throws. Byard had two tackles for loss. Craver caught four balls for 78 yards. Tyler White punted eight times, and he earned every one.

Four straight losses hurts. A young quarterback making his debut on the road in that stadium is a tough spot, and Hart showed enough to build on.

Here's the good news. One game can fix a lot of feelings, and it's the one we want most.

Next up: Texas at Kyle Field, Friday, Nov. 27, at 7:30 PM ET. Thanksgiving weekend in College Station, and the rivalry is back. Twelfth Man, be loud. Gig 'em!

articles.title: Oklahoma vs Texas A&M: John Mateer Accounts for Four Scores in Home Finale, 28-7
articles.matchup: Final: Oklahoma Sooners (7-4) 28, Texas A&M Aggies (4-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 21, Memorial Stadium (Norman, OK), Norman. Next: at Missouri, Sat., Nov. 28, 4:15 PM ET, Memorial Stadium, Columbia
articles.text:
John Mateer's last game in Norman ended with him hurdling a guy at the 7 and landing in the end zone. If that's not a proper sendoff, I don't know what is. Oklahoma 28, Texas A&M 7 on Saturday at Owen Field, our third straight win. We're 7-4 and 5-3 in the SEC. Boomer!

Now, I won't pretend the first half was pretty. A&M went 96 yards for a touchdown early in the second quarter, and Mateer threw an interception and lost a fumble on our next two trips. We trailed 7-0 inside the final three minutes of the half, and the crowd was grumbling.

Then Mateer flipped the switch. He took us 92 yards, completed seven of eight throws on the drive, and hit our tight end for a 4-yard touchdown with 22 seconds left. Tied at 7, and you could feel the place exhale.

The fourth quarter was all Sooners. Tory Blaylock caught a 5-yarder to put us ahead. Then Courtland Guillory picked off Brady Hart and ran it back 20 yards, and on the very next snap Mateer found Isaiah Sategna III wide open for 25 yards. Then came the hurdle. Twenty-eight straight points to finish it.

Mateer went 23 of 34 for 269 yards and three touchdowns, and ran 14 times for 66 more. Sategna caught six for 94. Parker Livingstone had four for 47.

And our defense? Nasty. A&M finished with 185 yards and 10 first downs and ran for 54 yards on 32 carries. That's 1.7 a pop. The Aggies punted eight times. David Stone had a sack and a half. Owen Heinecke made eight tackles with two for loss. Kip Lewis had eight too.

Eight straight home wins against A&M now. The Aggies used to be Big 12 neighbors. Now they're just a regular visitor we send home sad.

Next up: at Missouri, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 4:15 PM ET at Memorial Stadium in Columbia. Win number eight is waiting in Mizzou country. Boomer Sooner!

articles.title: Old Dominion vs UConn: Leon Haughton Jr. Scores Twice, Monarchs Fall 29-21
articles.byline: Winifred 'Winnie' Pocklington, The Old Dominion Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: UConn Huskies (6-5) 29, Old Dominion Monarchs (3-8) 21, Sat., Nov. 21, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford. Next: vs Southern Miss, Sat., Nov. 28, 1:00 PM ET, S.B. Ballard Stadium, Norfolk
articles.text:
Down 14-0 after one quarter in East Hartford, and my Monarchs kept swinging all the way to the final second. It ended 29-21, Huskies, and we're 3-8.

The second quarter was ours. Quinn Henicle hit Leon Haughton Jr. for a 17-yard touchdown on the first play of the quarter, and later he found Devin Roche for 33 yards and another score. Two touchdown throws, a 17-14 game, and we were right back in it. Henicle went 9 of 15 for 99 yards with those two scores.

Then Jaxon Potter came in and put on a clinic in his own right. He went 23 of 29 for 240 yards and kept moving the chains. With one second left, he hit Haughton from 6 yards out for the final touchdown. Haughton finished with seven catches, 62 yards and two scores.

Roche was terrific all night. Seven catches for 83 yards, that 33-yard touchdown, and 40 more on the ground. Josh Rodriguez had seven catches for 78, and Kendall Harris added four for 69. As a group, our quarterbacks went 32 of 45 for 339 yards. And we didn't give the ball away once.

So what went wrong? The ground game. We ran it 22 times for 53 yards, and UConn ran for 246. Every time we got close, their kicker made us pay. Three field goals from that guy. In an eight-point loss, that's the difference.

DeAndre Lynch was a wrecking ball on defense, with seven tackles and three and a half for loss. Zion Frink grabbed an interception. Daevon Iles led us with eight tackles. Mario Easterly had seven and two hurries.

I know 3-8 isn't what anybody in Norfolk wanted. But this team keeps playing hard, and that counts for plenty.

Next up: Southern Miss at S.B. Ballard Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 1:00 PM ET. Last game of the year, at home. Let's send the seniors out with a win. Go Monarchs!

articles.title: UConn vs Old Dominion: Kalieb Osborne Runs and Throws for Scores, Huskies Go Bowling
articles.matchup: Final: UConn Huskies (6-5) 29, Old Dominion Monarchs (3-8) 21, Sat., Nov. 21, Pratt & Whitney Stadium, East Hartford. Next: at Wyoming, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, War Memorial Stadium, Laramie
articles.text:
Book the flights, Husky Nation. UConn 29, Old Dominion 21 on Saturday night at the Rent, and win number six makes us bowl eligible. We're 6-5, and East Hartford is a happy place tonight.

We came out and punched first. The opening drive went 89 yards, and Kalieb Osborne finished it himself with a 13-yard touchdown run. Next time we had the ball, we went 76 yards, and Cyncir Bowers bulled in from 4. We led 14-0 in the first quarter, and the student section was bouncing.

Osborne was the whole show. He ran 16 times for 94 yards and completed 12 of 22 for 239. His 4-yard touchdown throw to Ryder Treadway in the third quarter made it 26-14. Treadway caught three balls for 66 yards, including a 36-yarder. Shamar Porter hauled in a 41-yard grab. Bowers finished with 105 yards on 18 carries. We ran for 246 yards as a team and piled up 485 yards of offense. That's a ground-and-pound recipe I can get behind.

Then there's Mike Baker. Old Dominion scored twice in the second quarter, and both times Baker answered with a field goal, from 23 and 36 yards. He added a 34-yarder late in the fourth to put it away. Three for three. When the offense stalled, Baker made sure we still came away with points.

The defense did its job too. John Lista made seven tackles, three of them for loss. K'Von Sherman had seven as well. The Monarchs ran for 53 yards all night.

I'll be honest, ten penalties made me crazy, and that late touchdown with one second left was a little annoying. But a win is a win, and this one comes with a bowl game attached.

Not long ago people laughed at the idea of UConn football in a bowl game. Nobody in Storrs is laughing now.

One more to go before the bowl. Next up: at Wyoming, Saturday, Nov. 28, at noon ET at War Memorial Stadium. Pack a coat for Laramie. Go Huskies!

articles.title: Penn State vs Rutgers: 24-10 Lead Slips Away, Lions Fall on Final Play
articles.byline: Luann Kessler, The Penn State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Rutgers Scarlet Knights (3-8) 25, Penn State Nittany Lions (6-5) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Beaver Stadium, University Park. Next: at Maryland, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, SECU Stadium, College Park
articles.text:
Penn State fans, we had Rutgers down 24-10 at Beaver Stadium with a quarter and a half to play. I've seen that movie end one way my whole life. Not this time. Rutgers 25, Penn State 24 on Saturday at Beaver Stadium, and the Nittany Lions are 6-5 and 3-5 in the Big Ten.

It opened so well. Cam Wallace broke a 56-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, and Beaver Stadium was rocking. Our defense dropped Rutgers in the end zone for a safety. Rocco Becht hit Chase Sowell for 17 yards and a touchdown, and it was 16-0.

Sowell was terrific. Six catches, 123 yards, a long of 43. Becht went 14 of 21 for 233 yards, then scored on a 6-yard keeper in the third and caught a two-point throw from tight end Benjamin Brahmer. That trick play was the most fun I had all day.

Tony Rojas played his heart out. Fifteen tackles, a sack and a half, two and a half tackles for loss and three hurries. Kooper Ebel added 14 tackles. Those two were everywhere.

But two lost fumbles gave Rutgers life, and one became a field goal right before halftime. Then their running back carried them on a 19-play drive that ate 9:38 in the fourth. After halftime our offense never found a rhythm. We went 0 for 2 on fourth down, and on Rutgers' final drive, two interference calls moved them to our 2.

And the last play. A throw to the running back, a pitch to a receiver, and nobody home. Then the two-point try, and silence across Happy Valley. A streak that began in 1988 ended in front of 106,200 people. I'll be hearing that silence in my sleep.

Here's what I'll hold on to. We're bowl eligible. Coach Campbell has a young group learning hard lessons in close games, and they'll be better for it.

Next up: at Maryland, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 3:30 PM ET at SECU Stadium. Let's go finish the regular season the right way. We Are!
