articles.title: Rutgers vs Penn State: Raymond's Pitch, Black's Score, Knights End a 38-Year Drought
articles.matchup: Final: Rutgers Scarlet Knights (3-8) 25, Penn State Nittany Lions (6-5) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Beaver Stadium, University Park. Next: vs Michigan State, Sat., Nov. 28, 4:15 PM ET, SHI Stadium, Piscataway
articles.text:
Thirty-eight years. I was a kid with a bowl haircut the last time this happened. Rutgers 25, Penn State 24 on Saturday at Beaver Stadium, on the final play, and the Scarlet Knights have finally beaten Penn State again. We're 3-8, and I don't care one bit about the record tonight.

We were down 16-0. We were down 24-10 in the third quarter. A team that had lost 18 straight to these guys had every excuse to fold. Instead we ripped off 15 points in the fourth.

Begin with AJ Surace, a guy who was questionable all week with three broken ribs and didn't throw in practice. He went out and completed 24 of 39 for 178 yards and a touchdown without a single interception. Tough as a Jersey turnpike pothole, and twice as stubborn.

Antwan Raymond was the engine. Twenty-three carries, 101 yards, two touchdowns. His 13-yarder capped a 19-play drive that chewed up 9:38 of clock and cut it to 24-17 with 10:19 left. Nineteen plays! I aged a year watching it.

Then the last drive. Eleven plays. A couple of interference flags on Penn State moved us to the 2 with no time to waste. On the final play, Surace threw it to Raymond, and as the whole Penn State defense swarmed him, Raymond flipped it to Ben Black III, who walked into the end zone with zeros on the clock. 24-23. Coach Schiano didn't blink. We went for two, and we got it. Ballgame. Drought done. Rivalry back.

The defense kept us alive. Sean Allison made 12 tackles and recovered a fumble. Sekou Kromah had a sack and a half and knocked the ball loose from Rocco Becht for DK Gilley to fall on, which set up Jack Scullion's 20-yard field goal before halftime. Penn State lost two fumbles, and we didn't give it away once.

First Big Ten win against Penn State ever, after 11 straight losses in the league. The last win before this was 1988. Frame it.

Next up: Michigan State at SHI Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 4:15 PM ET. Let's pack Piscataway and finish this year swinging. R-U, rah rah!

articles.title: Florida State vs NC State: Hot Opening Drive Fades, Noles Fall 28-10 at Doak
articles.byline: Gianna Ravello, The Florida State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: NC State Wolfpack (5-6) 28, Florida State Seminoles (5-6) 10, Sat., Nov. 21, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee. Next: vs Florida, Fri., Nov. 27, 3:30 PM ET, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee
articles.text:
The first drive was all we've been waiting for. Seventy-five yards, Zay Parks into the end zone from 9, Doak Campbell on its feet. Then the rest of the afternoon happened. The final at Doak read NC State 28, Florida State 10, and the Noles are 5-6.

Let me give Zay Parks his flowers first. Our top four running backs are hurt. Parks was fifth on the depth chart, he got the call, and he scored on our opening drive. That's a kid who was ready when his number got called.

Gabe Panikowski also gave us a moment. With no time left in the first half, he banged home a 54-yard field goal, and we led 10-7 at the break. I was feeling good. I shouldn't have been.

The second half belonged to the Wolfpack. They scored on three straight drives, and we couldn't answer. Ashton Daniels went 19 of 36 for 206 yards, but two interceptions hurt, and we came up empty twice on fourth down. We ran for 77 yards on 25 carries. You can't win ACC games like that.

There were bright spots. Jasen Lopez caught seven balls for 58 yards, including a 30-yarder. Micahi Danzy hauled in a 50-yard catch and finished with 73 yards on three grabs. And Chris Jones was a tackling machine, 14 of them. CJ Richard Jr. had nine, eight on his own.

This has been a strange, hard year in Tallahassee. A coaching change in November, a pile of injuries, and two interim coaches on the same field Saturday for the first time in an ACC game since at least 1996. Coach Stockstill has kept this group fighting, and I'm proud of that.

And now we get the best kind of chance. One win gets us to six. It just has to come against the team we want to beat most.

Next up: Florida at Doak Campbell Stadium, Friday, Nov. 27, at 3:30 PM ET. Wear garnet, bring the chop and let's send the Gators home unhappy. Go Noles!

articles.title: NC State vs Florida State: CJ Bailey Throws Three Scores, Pack Make It Five Straight
articles.byline: Rutherford 'Ruff' Pegram, The NC State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: NC State Wolfpack (5-6) 28, Florida State Seminoles (5-6) 10, Sat., Nov. 21, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee. Next: at North Carolina, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill
articles.text:
Five in a row against Florida State, Wolfpack. Five! NC State 28, Florida State 10 on Saturday in Tallahassee, and we're 5-6 with a bowl trip one win away.

This one was personal for a couple of our guys. CJ Bailey and Davion Gause both grew up in South Florida, and they came home and put on a show. Bailey went 23 of 36 for 292 yards and three touchdowns with zero interceptions. Gause carried it 25 times for 134 yards and caught five balls for 71 more, including a 42-yard screen that had me jumping off the couch.

It didn't look great early. Florida State marched 75 yards on its first drive and scored. We answered with Bailey's 1-yard touchdown to Darius Johnson. Then they hit a 54-yard field goal at the halftime horn, and we were down 10-7. I paced the kitchen for 20 minutes.

Whatever Coach Goebbel said at halftime, bottle it. We scored on three straight drives after the break. Deandre Desinor punched it in from 5 to give us the lead for good. Bailey hit Preston Douglas from 17 to make it 21-10, then found Davion Dozier from 13 for 28-10. Florida State never got close again.

The defense deserves a parade. After that first drive, the Seminoles couldn't find a rhythm. Jackson Vick had eight tackles, two tackles for loss and an interception. Brian Nelson II grabbed another one. We stopped them twice on fourth down. They ran for 77 yards all day. We didn't give it away once and held the ball for more than 36 minutes.

Look at all this team has been through this fall. A coaching change in October. Losses that stung. And they keep showing up for each other. Coach Goebbel has these kids playing hard, and with Philip Rivers hired to lead the program next year, Raleigh is buzzing.

Now we go get number six. Next up: at North Carolina, Saturday, Nov. 28, at noon ET at Kenan Stadium. Win and we're bowling. Beat the Heels and howl, Wolfpack!

articles.title: Auburn vs Samford: Tristan Ti'a Goes 17 of 18, Tigers Hit Seven Wins for First Time Since 2019
articles.matchup: Final: Auburn Tigers (7-4) 59, Samford Bulldogs (4-8) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn. Next: at Alabama, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Bryant-Denny Stadium, Tuscaloosa
articles.text:
Two plays. That's all it took. Jeremiah Cobb went 62 yards on our first snap, Byrum Brown hit Chas Nimrod for 63 on our second, and Jordan-Hare was already shaking. Auburn 59, Samford 17 on Saturday, and the Tigers are 7-4. That's seven wins for the first time since 2019. War Eagle, y'all.

Now let's talk about Tristan Ti'a, because what that young man did in the second quarter belongs in a museum. He went 17 of 18 for 341 yards and four touchdowns, and he did all of it in the first half. Seventeen of eighteen! He threw three touchdowns to Keshaun Singleton, from 35, 33 and 28 yards, hit Cobb for a 47-yarder, and ran one in himself from a yard out. We scored 38 points in the second quarter alone and went to the locker room up 52-3.

Alex McPherson capped the half with a 40-yard field goal at the horn, and he was perfect on all eight extra points. The man never missed a chance to add on.

Auburn set a school record with 480 yards through the air, and we piled up 672 yards of offense. Nimrod caught seven balls for 157 yards. Singleton finished with six for 150 and three scores. Cobb ran 10 times for 120 yards and caught two for 52. Rhys Brush came in late and threw a 6-yard touchdown to Jonathan Echols, and you could hear the whole sideline cheer for him.

Credit the defense too. Jaquez Wilkes had six tackles and two tackles for loss. Jourdin Crawford and Michael Matthews-Canty each got home for sacks. Samford ran 32 times for 90 yards.

I know Samford is an FCS team, and I know the second half was mostly the backups. I don't care. Coach Golesh has this program believing again, and seven wins tastes a lot better than the last few Novembers.

Bowl eligible, seven wins, and now the game every Auburn fan circles first.

Next up: at Alabama, Saturday, Nov. 28, at Bryant-Denny Stadium, time to be announced. It's Iron Bowl week. Let's go to Tuscaloosa and make some noise. War Eagle!

articles.title: Baylor vs Texas Tech: Defense Takes Three Away, Bears Fall 20-10 in Home Finale
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Tech Red Raiders (10-1) 20, Baylor Bears (6-5) 10, Sat., Nov. 21, McLane Stadium, Waco. Next: at Houston, Sat., Nov. 28, 9:30 PM ET, TDECU Stadium, Houston
articles.text:
Sic 'em, folks, even on a hard day. Texas Tech 20, Baylor 10 on Saturday at McLane Stadium in our last home game of the year. We're 6-5 and 4-4 in the Big 12, and we already know we're bowling.

I want to begin with our defense, because those guys deserved a win. The Red Raiders came into Waco scoring more than 46 a game in their last three. We held them to 20, their lowest of the season. And we took the ball away three times. Kaleb Burns punched one loose in the second quarter and Colby McCalister fell on it at the Tech 26. That set up the tying touchdown. In the third, LeVar Thornton Jr. picked one off in the end zone and brought it out 23 yards. Later Devon Jordan grabbed another one at our 13.

Micah Gifford made seven tackles. Tyler Turner had six and broke up a throw. Burns added a sack to go with his forced fumble.

DJ Lagway threw it 48 times and completed 30 of them, for 236 yards, finding 12 different guys. His 3-yard touchdown to tight end Matthew Klopfenstein in the second quarter tied it 7-7, and McLane was as loud as I've heard it all fall. Tony Livingston caught four balls for 47. Rhett Armstrong knocked through a 24-yarder in the fourth to keep it a one-score game.

Here's the problem, Bears fans. We ran it 22 times for 31 yards. When you can't run, a defense like Tech's pins its ears back, and our offense stalled after halftime. We also missed a field goal in the second quarter, and we came up short on fourth down late.

I'm still proud of this group. Coach Klanderman stepped in at a tough time, we beat UCF and Iowa State, and we've played two of the best teams in the league tough.

Now we get one more chance before the bowl. Next up: at Houston, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 9:30 PM ET at TDECU Stadium. A late kick in Houston, and a seventh win sitting right there. Sic 'em, Bears!

articles.title: Texas Tech vs Baylor: Red Raiders Grind Out 20-10 Win, First Back-to-Back 10-Win Seasons
articles.byline: Bodie Ratliff, The Texas Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Tech Red Raiders (10-1) 20, Baylor Bears (6-5) 10, Sat., Nov. 21, McLane Stadium, Waco. Next: vs TCU, Thu., Nov. 26, 8:00 PM ET, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock
articles.text:
Pretty, it was not. Do I care? Not one bit. Texas Tech 20, Baylor 10 on Saturday in Waco, and for the first time in school history, the Red Raiders have put together back-to-back 10-win seasons. We're 10-1, 7-1 in the Big 12, and one win from the conference title game.

This wasn't our usual fireworks show. We'd averaged more than 46 points a game in the three games since Thomas Castellanos took the job. On Saturday we gave it away three times and didn't force a single turnover. Some days you just have to win in the mud, and this team did it.

J'Koby Williams was the workhorse. Twenty-one carries, 117 yards, and the 1-yard touchdown that put us ahead 7-0 in the first quarter. We never trailed after that. Castellanos ran 18 times for 92 yards, with gains of 39 and 29, and he went 10 of 16 for 171 through the air.

The big swing came from Malcolm Simmons again. Tied at 7 in the third, Castellanos launched one and Simmons ran it down for a 48-yard touchdown. One week after he took a kickoff 97 yards in Stillwater, the guy just keeps finding the end zone.

Then the defense owned the game. Baylor ran 22 times for 31 yards. A.J. Holmes Jr. had two sacks and three tackles for loss and now leads the Big 12 with 10 sacks. Mateen Ibirogba had a sack and three tackles for loss. Ben Roberts led us with eight tackles. With 2:56 left and Baylor needing a stop, our guys stuffed them on fourth-and-4 at the Bears' 22, and Stone Harrington drilled his second field goal of the quarter from 39 yards to make it 20-10. Harrington went 2 for 2. Money.

I'll be honest, those two interceptions and the fumble gave me heartburn. But a team that can win on a day like this is a team built for December.

Here's the deal. Beat TCU and we're in the Big 12 title game. Simple as that.

Next up: TCU at Galaxy Stadium, Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:00 PM ET. Thanksgiving night in Lubbock. Eat early and get to the stadium loud. Wreck 'em, Tech!

articles.title: LSU vs Tennessee: Davhon Keys Makes 14 Tackles, Tigers Fade in Knoxville
articles.matchup: Final: Tennessee Volunteers (9-2) 27, LSU Tigers (6-5) 13, Sat., Nov. 21, Neyland Stadium, Knoxville. Next: at Arkansas, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville
articles.text:
For three quarters in Knoxville, my Tigers stood toe to toe with the No. 9 team in the country. Then the fourth quarter happened. Tennessee 27, LSU 13 on Saturday at Neyland Stadium, and we're 6-5 and 3-5 in the SEC.

Let me tell you what we did right first, because there was plenty. Our defense came out swinging. Ty Benefield sacked their freshman quarterback and took the fumble away. Davhon Keys picked his pocket a few minutes later with an interception. Scott Starzyk turned both into field goals, from 44 and 26 yards, and we led 6-0.

Keys was a monster all day. Fourteen tackles, a sack, two tackles for loss and that interception. If you didn't know his name before Saturday, you should now. TJ Dottery had eight tackles and broke up two throws.

Late in the third, Tennessee muffed a punt at its own 10, and PJ Woodland jumped on it at the 9. Two plays later Sam Leavitt found Trey'Dez Green for a 9-yard touchdown, and it was 13-13 heading to the fourth. I was standing on my couch.

Leavitt finished 27 of 39 for 222 yards. Green caught seven balls for 72 yards. Eugene Wilson III had eight catches. The throwing game did its part.

But here's the hard truth, Tiger fans. We ran it 34 times for 43 yards. You can't live like that in the SEC. And we got flagged 16 times for 98 yards in that loud stadium. Every flag put us behind schedule. Then their freshman broke two long runs in the fourth, and we lost a fumble on a sack with the game slipping away.

I'm proud of how hard the defense played. I'm frustrated we couldn't give them more help.

One more Saturday to make it right. Next up: at Arkansas, Saturday, Nov. 28, at Razorback Stadium in Fayetteville, time to be announced. Let's go take the Golden Boot home. Geaux Tigers!

articles.title: Tennessee vs LSU: Freshman Faizon Brandon Breaks Loose Twice, Vols Win 27-13
articles.byline: Earl 'Rocky Top' Haskew, The Tennessee Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Tennessee Volunteers (9-2) 27, LSU Tigers (6-5) 13, Sat., Nov. 21, Neyland Stadium, Knoxville. Next: at Vanderbilt, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, FirstBank Stadium, Nashville
articles.text:
Tied at 13 in the fourth quarter, Neyland rocking, and a freshman quarterback decides it's his turn. Tennessee 27, LSU 13 on Saturday in Knoxville. The Vols are 9-2 and 6-2 in the SEC, and 101,915 of us sang Rocky Top until we were hoarse.

Faizon Brandon, folks. Remember the name. The kid had a rough first quarter, with a fumble and an interception that both turned into LSU field goals. A lot of freshmen would fold. Brandon shook it off. With 8:22 left he took off on an 18-yard touchdown run to break the tie. Then with 4:04 left he found a crease and was gone, 55 yards, and the stadium about lifted off the riverbank. Twelve carries, 112 yards, two touchdowns, all of the big ones in the fourth quarter.

George MacIntyre gutted it out on a bad knee. He went 12 of 21 and hit DaSaahn Brame for a 2-yard touchdown with 12 seconds left in the half to give us a 10-6 lead. Cooper Ranvier banged home a 52-yarder and a 23-yarder. Javin Gordon ran for 54.

But I'm putting this win on the defense. LSU ran the ball 34 times for 43 yards. That's 1.3 a carry. Arion Carter was everywhere: 10 tackles, a sack, two tackles for loss, and he punched the ball loose and fell on it himself deep in LSU territory. Dejuan Lane had eight tackles and a sack, and he jumped on a fumble late. Ty Benefield and Davhon Keys made plays for them, but our front owned the fourth quarter.

And the crowd? LSU got flagged 16 times for 98 yards. Don't tell me noise doesn't matter.

I'll admit Qua Moss muffing that punt in the third made me spill my popcorn, because it set up LSU's tying touchdown. The kid will be fine. He had 59 yards on returns.

Our prayers are with Arion Carter and DeSean Bishop, who both got hurt late. Get well, fellas.

Next up: at Vanderbilt, Saturday, Nov. 28, at FirstBank Stadium, time to be announced. Let's finish strong in Nashville. Go Vols!

articles.title: Indiana vs Washington: Charlie Becker's 167 Yards Not Enough in OT Loss
articles.matchup: Final: Washington Huskies (7-4) 27, Indiana Hoosiers (9-2) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Husky Stadium, Seattle. Next: vs Purdue, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Memorial Stadium (Bloomington, IN), Bloomington
articles.text:
Three overtime games in four weeks, Hoosier Nation. We won the first two. Saturday in Seattle, the third one bit us. Washington 27, Indiana 24, and we're 9-2 and 6-2 in the Big Ten with a lot of nervous math ahead of us.

Good news first, because Charlie Becker earned it. On our first snap of the day, Grant Wilson put one on him in stride, and Becker went 74 yards for a touchdown. That catch pushed him past 1,000 yards for the season. He's the eighth Hoosier ever to do it and the first since Whop Philyor in 2019. He finished with six catches for 167 yards and now sits at 1,117. Ernie Jones has the school record at 1,265. Somebody tell Ernie to keep an eye on the mailbox.

Wilson also ran one in from 5 yards out, and we were up 14-7 in the first quarter. Then the offense went quiet. We went 2 for 15 on third down, and that's the story right there.

Coach Cignetti went to Josh Hoover in the third quarter, and Hoover gave us a jolt. With 9:06 left, he hit Nick Marsh for a 35-yard touchdown to make it 24-17. Hoover went 7 of 13 for 121 yards in about a half. Lee Beebe Jr. ran 15 times for 94 yards, including a 42-yarder.

And zero turnovers, none. Preston Zachman made eight tackles and grabbed an interception. Byron Baldwin Jr. had two sacks. Our defense gave us every chance.

The kicking game is what hurts. Their big offensive lineman blocked a 46-yarder in the third quarter, and then he blocked our 37-yarder in overtime after they'd made theirs. Paddy McAteer did hit a 34-yarder, but in a three-point loss, those two kicks are the ballgame.

I'm not giving up on this team. They won a national title last year, and they've won close games all fall. Losing one doesn't change who they are.

Next up: Purdue at Memorial Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, time to be announced. The Old Oaken Bucket stays in Bloomington. Go Hoosiers!

articles.title: Washington vs Indiana: Drew Azzopardi Blocks Two Kicks, Huskies Stun No. 6 in OT
articles.matchup: Final: Washington Huskies (7-4) 27, Indiana Hoosiers (9-2) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Husky Stadium, Seattle. Next: at Oregon, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Autzen Stadium, Eugene
articles.text:
Give the game ball to an offensive lineman. Washington 27, Indiana 24 in overtime on Saturday at Husky Stadium, and the defending national champs went home losers because Drew Azzopardi got his big paws on not one but two Hoosier field goals. We're 7-4, 4-4 in the Big Ten, and Montlake just rushed the field.

Let's go back to the beginning, because the first quarter was nuts. On the opening drive Demond Williams Jr. took off on a 65-yard touchdown run. That's the longest run by a Washington quarterback since Warren Moon went 71 in 1977. Indiana hit a 74-yarder on its very first snap, and by the end of the quarter it was 14-14. Then nobody scored for a whole quarter.

Third quarter, Indiana tries a 46-yarder. Azzopardi blocks it. File that away.

Indiana went up 24-17 with 9:06 left on a 35-yard throw, and I'll admit my stomach dropped. These Huskies didn't flinch. Williams marched us down, and with 3:34 to go he found Decker DeGraaf for a 20-yard touchdown. Tied at 24. Tyler Robles had already hit a 28-yarder in the fourth, and in overtime he stepped up and drilled one from 46. That put it on our defense and our field goal block team.

Indiana's kicker tries one from 37. Azzopardi again. Blocked. Ballgame. Sixty-four thousand people came pouring out of the stands, and I'm pretty sure I hugged a guy in a Lake Washington rowing jacket I've never met.

Williams finished 24 of 41 for 227 yards and ran for 88 more. Dezmen Roebuck caught 10 balls for 92 yards and even completed a 27-yard throw of his own. Chris Lawson had seven catches. Jayden Limar scored from 5. We outgained the Hoosiers 443-392. Elinneus Davis had a sack and two tackles for loss, and Darin Conley got home too.

Two blocked kicks by the same big man in one game. I'm going to need a framed photo.

No rest, though. Next up: at Oregon, Saturday, Nov. 28, at Autzen Stadium, time to be announced. Bring this energy down I-5. Bow down to Washington!

articles.title: Arkansas vs Texas: Chris Marshall Goes for 106, Hogs Buried Early in Austin
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Longhorns (9-2) 45, Arkansas Razorbacks (4-7) 3, Sat., Nov. 21, DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin. Next: vs LSU, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville
articles.text:
Hog fans, I'll keep this honest, because you deserve honest. Final from Austin: Texas 45, Arkansas 3. We're 4-7 and 2-6 in the SEC, and we were down 14 points before most folks found their seats.

Here's how fast it went sideways. We drew three penalties on our first possession, gave Texas a short field, and they marched 52 yards for a touchdown. On our second series, KJ Jackson put a throw right on Jaden Platt's hands, a Texas defender hit him, the ball popped up, and Jelani McDonald ran it back 31 yards. Fourteen points in about six minutes. Coach Silverfield said afterward the blame begins with him. I respect that. But the players have to answer that bell too.

Now let me give some love where it's earned. Chris Marshall was the best player on our side of the field. Nine catches, 106 yards, a long of 28. Every time Jackson needed somebody to win a one-on-one, Marshall raised his hand. That's a guy you build around.

Jackson went 15 of 28 for 190 yards. Hank Hendrix came in and went 6 for 10. Cam Settles ran hard, 14 carries for 63 yards. And Max Gilbert got us on the board with a 30-yard field goal in the first quarter, so we didn't leave Austin with a zero. Small mercies.

We actually moved the ball some. We had 20 first downs to their 21 and finished with 363 yards. But we went 3 for 14 on third down and 2 for 6 on fourth down, and you can't leave that many drives on the field against a top-10 team.

Khmori House made nine tackles and played like his hair was on fire. Bradley Shaw had a tackle for loss. The fight was there. The finish wasn't.

Now here's the good news. We get a chance to send the seniors out right, in our house, against a big-name SEC opponent. Fayetteville has seen some rowdy late-November afternoons, and I'd love one more.

Next up: LSU at Razorback Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, time to be announced. Fill it up and call the Hogs. Woo Pig Sooie!

articles.title: Texas vs Arkansas: Arch Manning Goes 21 of 25 on Senior Day, Horns Roll 45-3
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Longhorns (9-2) 45, Arkansas Razorbacks (4-7) 3, Sat., Nov. 21, DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin. Next: at Texas A&M, Fri., Nov. 27, 7:30 PM ET, Kyle Field, College Station
articles.text:
Senior Day in Austin, and the Longhorns threw a party. Texas 45, Arkansas 3 on Saturday at DKR, our fifth straight win. We're 9-2, and 103,508 people got to watch a team that looks ready for December.

Arch Manning walked out with the seniors before kickoff, even though he's got a year of eligibility left. Then he went out and played like a guy who wanted to leave the place with a memory. He took us 52 yards on the first drive and scored himself from 3 yards out. By halftime he was 15 of 17 for 230 yards. He found Emaree Winston from 21 yards and Emmett Mosley V from 17, both in the final 2:20 of the half, and we hit the break with a 31-3 cushion. That's our biggest halftime lead of the year.

He finished 21 of 25 for 287 yards with no turnovers and sat down after three quarters. Twenty-one of twenty-five. I've had worse days hitting the side of a barn.

But the play of the day belonged to Jelani McDonald, again. On Arkansas' second possession, a throw bounced off a receiver's hands after Kade Phillips laid a hit, and McDonald caught it and took it 31 yards to the house. Fourteen points in the first six minutes. McDonald has four interceptions in two weeks. That young man has glue on his gloves.

Mosley caught eight balls for 106 yards. Ryan Wingo had six for 68. John Meredith III grabbed our second interception. Lance Jackson got home for a sack. Michael Terry III and Derrek Cooper each punched in short touchdown runs after the backups came in, and the whole sideline got to celebrate.

And the defense has a habit now: the fourth quarter belongs to us. Arkansas is the fourth straight team that didn't score on us in the fourth quarter.

Nine and two, five in a row, and not one turnover all day. I'm feeling good, y'all.

Now the big one. Next up: at Texas A&M, Friday, Nov. 27, at 7:30 PM ET at Kyle Field. Thanksgiving leftovers, then the Aggies. Hook 'em!

articles.title: UCLA vs Michigan: Bruins Fall in Triple Overtime, First Loss at 10-1
articles.matchup: Final: Michigan Wolverines (6-5) 18, UCLA Bruins (10-1) 16, Sat., Nov. 21, Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor. Next: vs USC, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Rose Bowl, Pasadena
articles.text:
Bruin fans, the perfect season is done, and it took Michigan three overtimes to do it. Michigan 18, UCLA 16 on Saturday in Ann Arbor. We're 10-1 and 7-1 in the Big Ten, and I need a minute.

Okay. Minute's up. Here's what happened.

We spent ten games winning the turnover battle. That's been our whole identity in Coach Chesney's first year. In Ann Arbor we coughed it up three times and took it away once. An interception at the Michigan 11 in the first quarter. A sack-fumble right before halftime. Another fumble at the end of the third. You can't hand a team in its own stadium extra chances and expect to walk away a winner.

And yet we almost did. Down 10-3 with the clock dying, we went to the bag of tricks. Anthony Woods took a direct snap, ran at the pile and flipped a 1-yard jump throw to Brayden Loftin with 10 seconds left. Tied 10-10. I screamed so loud my dog left the room.

Mateen Bhaghani was perfect. Three for three, from 44, 38 and 38 yards, and the last two came in overtime with the whole game riding on them. That kid has ice in his veins.

The hardest part was watching Ty Dieffenbach get carted off in overtime after getting hurt on a run. He'd gone 19 of 30 for 188 yards. Madden Iamaleava came in cold, and his brother Nico was our No. 1 quarterback until he got hurt last month. This team has been through a lot. Get well, Ty.

The defense deserves better than a loss. Malik Hartford and Donavyn Pellot each made nine tackles. Aiden Gobaira had seven tackles, a sack and two and a half tackles for loss. Michigan finished with 247 yards and converted 5 of 15 third downs. Our guys did their job.

In the third overtime, Michigan stopped our two-point try and hit theirs. That's football. It stings, but one loss doesn't erase ten wins.

And now the best possible way to bounce back. Next up: USC at the Rose Bowl, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 3:30 PM ET. Rivalry week, at home in Pasadena. Let's make it loud. Go Bruins!

articles.title: Michigan vs UCLA: Underwood Hits Hoffman in Triple Overtime, Wolverines Topple No. 4
articles.matchup: Final: Michigan Wolverines (6-5) 18, UCLA Bruins (10-1) 16, Sat., Nov. 21, Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor. Next: at Ohio State, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Ohio Stadium, Columbus
articles.text:
Three overtimes. Two kickers trading bombs. One throw to the corner of the end zone. Michigan 18, UCLA 16 on Saturday at the Big House, and the fourth-ranked, unbeaten Bruins walked out of Ann Arbor with their first loss. We're 6-5, we're bowl eligible, and 109,618 of us got to say goodbye to this stadium for the season the right way.

I've watched this program for a long time, and I'm not sure I've ever been prouder of a win in a season that tested us this much.

Bryce Underwood got the nod for the first time since Oct. 17, and you could tell the kid had a point to prove. He went 11 of 24 for 127 yards, and early in the fourth he found Mason Bonner from 6 yards out to put us up 10-3. Then UCLA tied it with 10 seconds left on a trick play, a 1-yard jump throw from a running back. Gut punch. We regrouped.

Overtime was a kicking clinic. Jacob Baggett answered their 38-yarder with a 29-yarder. In the second overtime he drilled one from 52 yards, and they matched it again. So it went to the two-point round. Our defense stopped them first. Then Underwood rolled right and fired a bullet to Jalen Hoffman in the corner. Ballgame. Maize and blue poured onto the field, and I'm not sure my voice comes back before Thanksgiving.

Let's talk defense, because that's why we won. Chris Bracy made 12 tackles and intercepted a throw at our 11 in the first quarter. John Henry Daley had two sacks, and one of them knocked the ball loose for Dom Nichols to recover. Trey Pierce fell on another fumble late in the third. A team that came in leading the country in takeaways lost the turnover battle in our house. UCLA's longest play of the day was a 27-yard run on a fake punt. That's how good our guys were.

Savion Hiter carried it 26 times for 104 yards and kept pounding when there wasn't much room. Baggett went 3 for 3, and that 52-yarder in double overtime is going on my wall.

Coach Whittingham turned 67 on Saturday. Not a bad birthday present. And we're praying for their quarterback, who got carted off in overtime.

Now the big one. Next up: at Ohio State, Saturday, Nov. 28, at noon ET at Ohio Stadium. Bring that defense to Columbus. Go Blue!

articles.title: UAB vs UTSA: Jo'Tavion Pierce Makes 17 Tackles, Blazers Fall by Two, 19-17
articles.matchup: Final: UTSA Roadrunners (9-2) 19, UAB Blazers (6-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Protective Stadium, Birmingham. Next: at North Texas, Sat., Nov. 28, 4:00 PM ET, DATCU Stadium, Denton
articles.text:
Seventeen tackles. Jo'Tavion Pierce made 17 tackles on Saturday night at Protective Stadium, 13 of them by himself, and if there's any justice he'll be sore for a week because he earned it. UAB played the best team in the conference to the wire. UTSA 19, UAB 17, and we're 6-5, 4-3 in the American.

We were down 14-0 in the blink of an eye in the second quarter. UTSA scored on a 1-yard run, and 15 seconds later we fumbled the kickoff and they fell on it in the end zone. A lot of teams fold right there. Not this one. Rod Robinson II went to work. He ran it in from 11, then punched in a 1-yarder with 41 seconds left before halftime. 14-14. The Blazer faithful were on their feet.

The second half came down to inches. UTSA kicked a field goal in the third quarter. Early in the fourth, they got a safety. Jonah Delange hit a 39-yarder to make it 19-17 with 9:36 to go. He also missed two others, and in a two-point game you can do the math. That one is going to sting for a while.

Our defense deserved a win. Pierce was everywhere, and with 2:36 left he punched the ball out of a UTSA runner's hands at our 5 to keep us alive. Byard fell on it. Jeremiah Jordan made 12 tackles. Darrell Sweeting intercepted Owen McCown and brought it back 24 yards. Muaaz Byard and Guylijah Theodule each recovered fumbles. We forced three turnovers against a nine-win team, and our offense just couldn't cash the last one.

The offense just couldn't get going after halftime. Ryder Burton completed 10 of 25 throws for 118 yards. Robinson ran 20 times for 68 yards and both scores, and Bam McReynolds added 56 rushing yards and a 26-yard catch.

Here's the thing. We're bowl eligible, and we've got one more chance to prove what this team is, at North Texas next Saturday. Blazer Nation, travel to Denton and make some noise. Go Blazers!

articles.title: UTSA vs UAB: A Safety and a Defensive Stand, Roadrunners Grind Out a 19-17 Win
articles.matchup: Final: UTSA Roadrunners (9-2) 19, UAB Blazers (6-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Protective Stadium, Birmingham. Next: vs Tulsa, Fri., Nov. 27, 12:00 PM ET, Alamodome, San Antonio
articles.text:
Ugly wins count the same, Roadrunner fans, and this one was gloriously ugly. UTSA 19, UAB 17 at Protective Stadium in Birmingham, decided by a safety, two missed UAB field goals and a defense that would not let the Blazers into the end zone after halftime. We're 9-2, 6-1 in the American. Birds Up!

The second quarter was a whirlwind. A'Marion Peterson plowed in from a yard out to open the scoring. Fifteen seconds later, Joel Rogers knocked the ball loose on the kickoff and Jamel Hardy Jr. fell on it in the end zone, and just like that we were up 14-0. I barely had time to sit down. UAB answered with two Rod Robinson II touchdown runs, the second with 41 seconds left in the half, and it was 14-14 at the break.

After that, it was a street fight, and our defense won it. Michael Petro kicked a 26-yard field goal in the third. Early in the fourth, RJ Lester Jr. dropped a UAB runner in the end zone for a safety and a 19-14 lead. UAB got a 39-yard field goal back, and then our guys slammed the door for the last nine and a half minutes.

Darion White made eight tackles, two for loss, and hurried the quarterback twice. Dylan Spencer had a sack and two and a half tackles for loss. Lester also forced a fumble that Jeremiah Bailey recovered. UAB managed 227 yards, went 5 for 15 on third down and completed 10 of 25 throws.

On offense, we pounded the ground game. Will Henderson III carried 23 times for 93 yards, and Peterson broke a 49-yard run on his way to 79 yards. We ran it 47 times for 197 yards and held the ball for more than 32 minutes. Brandon Young Jr. caught four balls for 56 yards. Yes, we gave it away three times, including a fumble at the UAB 5 with less than three minutes left that could have iced it, and I'm not thrilled about that. But nine wins is nine wins.

Tulsa comes to the Alamodome on Friday, and I want that place rocking for the regular-season finale. Ten wins is sitting right there. Let's go take it, 'Runners.

articles.title: Colorado State vs Fresno State: Hauss Hejny Throws for 413, Rams Rally Late but Fall, 49-42
articles.byline: Ansel Rimrock, The Colorado State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Fresno State Bulldogs (6-5) 49, Colorado State Rams (3-8) 42, Sat., Nov. 21, Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno.
articles.text:
Four hundred thirteen yards through the air. Hauss Hejny went into Fresno on Saturday night, carved up the Bulldogs' secondary, and nearly dragged the Rams to the wildest comeback of the year. Fresno State 49, Colorado State 42, and we're 3-8, 1-6 in the Pac-12. Rams fans, that kid is going to be a handful for a long time.

We started in a hole. Barely a minute in, Fresno's Simeon Harris jumped a throw and ran it back 35 yards for a touchdown. Hejny answered right away with a 23-yard touchdown run, and after Fresno scored again, he punched in a 1-yarder to tie it 14-14 before the first quarter ended. That's a quarterback with some grit.

Then Fresno got rolling on the ground, and we couldn't slow them down. They ran for 265 yards, including a 61-yarder to open the second half, and it was 49-27 early in the fourth quarter. Most teams pack it in right there.

Not these Rams. Hejny hit Ryan McConnell for a 5-yard touchdown with 1:48 left. Then he found Daven Amos for a 33-yard score with 26 seconds to go and hit Terrence Smith Jr. for the two-point try. 49-42. We just ran out of clock. I was screaming at my screen in Fort Collins like I could will an onside kick into existence.

Hejny finished 27 of 37 with two touchdown throws and ran for 73 yards and two more scores. Tommy Maher caught six balls for 111 yards, including a 49-yarder. Smith had four catches for 67. As an offense we piled up 571 yards and 29 first downs and went 3 for 3 on fourth down. Kali Nguma hit field goals from 30 and 39, and Mel Brown ran in a 9-yard score.

Oumar Diomande made 10 tackles, two for loss, and Ty Staples recovered a fumble. Ten penalties didn't help anybody.

Three wins isn't the season anybody wanted. But I watched this team refuse to quit on the road where nobody expected anything from us. Stalwart Rams, Hejny's got the keys, and the future in Fort Collins looks a whole lot brighter tonight.

articles.title: Fresno State vs Colorado State: Rayshon Luke Scores Three, Bulldogs Reach Six Wins, 49-42
articles.byline: Rosalind 'Roz' Ayala, The Fresno State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Fresno State Bulldogs (6-5) 49, Colorado State Rams (3-8) 42, Sat., Nov. 21, Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno.
articles.text:
Sixty-eight seconds. That's how long it took Simeon Harris to light up Valley Children's Stadium on Saturday night, jumping a Colorado State throw and taking it 35 yards to the house. Fresno State 49, Colorado State 42, and the Bulldogs are 6-5. Six wins. Bowl eligible. The Valley is fired up.

Rayshon Luke was everywhere. He ran for touchdowns from 18 and 3 yards, caught a 6-yard score, and racked up 119 yards on four kickoff returns, including a 59-yarder. Three touchdowns and a special-teams highlight reel. Give that young man a raise in his meal plan.

Jayden Mandal was almost perfect. Fifteen of 17 for 191 yards and three touchdowns. Josiah Freeman caught two of them, from 5 and 21 yards, and finished with five catches for 104 yards, including a 60-yard catch-and-run that had the place standing. Bryson Donelson ran 16 times for 165 yards, and his 61-yard touchdown at the start of the third quarter made it 35-17. As a team we ran for 265 yards, more than eight a carry. That's bully ball, Bulldog style.

Now, about the ending. We were up 49-27 with almost the whole fourth quarter to play, and I was already planning my bowl road trip. Colorado State scored with 1:48 left, then again with 26 seconds left, added a two-point try, and suddenly it was a one-score game. My nerves are fried. But we closed it out, and that's what counts.

Harris had two tackles for loss to go with the interception return. Tytus Khajavi made eight tackles, and Tommy Nix had six, all solo. Their quarterback threw for 413 yards, so there's film to study, but our defense made the first big play of the night and it set the tone.

Six and five, and the Red Wave gets to keep this ride going into the postseason. Go Dogs, and tell your friends from Clovis to Kerman.

articles.title: Cal vs Stanford: Ian Strong Ties It Before the Half, but the Bears Drop the Big Game, 44-28
articles.matchup: Final: Stanford Cardinal (6-5) 44, California Golden Bears (3-8) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley. Next: vs Pittsburgh, Sat., Nov. 28, 7:30 PM ET, California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley
articles.text:
Golden Bear fans, I'm not going to dress this one up. Losing the Big Game at home, in front of more than 54,000 people, with the Axe at stake, is about as bad as Saturdays get in Berkeley. Stanford 44, Cal 28, and we're 3-8, 2-6 in the ACC.

And it was a game at halftime. Our first touchdown drive went 11 plays and 75 yards, every one of them on the ground, and Taimane Purcell powered in from 2 yards to tie it 7-7. Then Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele came in late in the second quarter and immediately gave us a jolt. With 45 seconds left before the break, he hit Ian Strong for a 12-yard touchdown. 14-14. Strawberry Canyon was rocking.

Then came the turn. We fumbled the ball away, and Stanford kicked a 47-yard field goal with no time left in the half. Early in the third quarter, Micah Ford scored, and minutes later he busted a 63-yard run. 29-14, and we were chasing the rest of the night.

Some bright spots, because there were a few. Adam Mohammed ran 16 times for 90 yards and punched in a 1-yard score in the fourth. Sagapolutele went 14 of 21 for 127 yards and the touchdown. Jackson Brousseau came in late and hit Chase Hendricks for a 4-yard score, then found Mason Mini for two. Kamar Mothudi made 11 tackles. Jae'on Young broke up five throws, which is a monster number.

But 13 penalties for 112 yards will sink you against anybody, and especially against a rival. Five losses in a row is a tough way to end November, and nobody in Berkeley is pretending otherwise.

Pitt comes to Berkeley next Saturday night for the season finale, and the seniors deserve a win on their way out. Go Bears. Show up and send them off right.

articles.title: Stanford vs Cal: Micah Ford Runs for 151, the Axe Stays on the Farm, 44-28
articles.matchup: Final: Stanford Cardinal (6-5) 44, California Golden Bears (3-8) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley. Next: vs SMU, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Stanford Stadium, Stanford
articles.text:
The Axe is ours. Again. Stanford 44, Cal 28 in the Big Game at California Memorial Stadium, two straight years the Axe has come home with us, and the Cardinal are 6-5 and bowl eligible for the first time since 2018. Somebody tell the Band to warm up.

Micah Ford was the best player on the field and it wasn't close. Twenty carries, 151 yards, two touchdowns, and he threw one too. Late in the first quarter, our running back flipped a 1-yard touchdown throw to tight end Chico Holt, and I laughed out loud. Then he opened the second half with a 1-yard plunge and, a few minutes later, broke a 63-yard run to the end zone that ended any thought of a Cal comeback. 29-14. That's four games in his last five with at least 149 rushing yards. He's a problem.

The first half was a fistfight. Cal tied it 7-7 and again at 14-14 with 45 seconds left. But Darrius Davis came up with a Cal fumble in the final seconds, and Emmet Kenney drilled a 47-yard field goal at the gun. 17-14, and the momentum flipped for good.

Davis Warren was sharp: 14 of 25 for 214 yards, two touchdown throws and an 8-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. Early in the fourth, he hit Nico Brown on a 49-yarder, and later found Zach Giuliano for 48 more. Brown finished with five catches for 92. We ran for 197 yards as a team and didn't give the ball away once.

Jahsiah Galvan made 12 tackles and Sam Mattingly had 10. Leroy Bryant broke up two throws. The defense bent at times, but it never broke when the game was in doubt.

One more regular-season game, at home against SMU, and then a bowl game for the first time in a long, long while. The Axe is going back to the Farm where it belongs. Fear the Tree!

articles.title: Pitt vs Louisville: Isaiah Neal Scores on Defense, but Panthers Fade in Louisville, 42-10
articles.matchup: Final: Louisville Cardinals (8-3) 42, Pittsburgh Panthers (6-5) 10, Sat., Nov. 21, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville. Next: at California, Sat., Nov. 28, 7:30 PM ET, California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley
articles.text:
Yinzers, I need you to remember the first half, because the second half didn't happen as far as I'm concerned. At halftime in Louisville, it was 14-10, and Pitt was right there. Then the Cardinals scored 28 straight. Louisville 42, Pitt 10, and the Panthers sit at 6-5, 3-5 in ACC play.

The first half was a defensive brawl, and our guys threw the first punches. Our front sacked Lincoln Kienholz three times and held Louisville to zero net rushing yards before the break. Then Isaiah Neal scooped up a Kienholz fumble and rumbled 31 yards to the end zone to tie it 7-7. I spilled my pierogies.

And at the end of the half, Alex Sanford Jr. intercepted Kienholz at our 29 and brought it back 43 yards. We lost a few yards on a holding call and a sack, and it didn't matter one bit, because Antonio Chadha walked out there and hit a 57-yard field goal as time expired. Fifty-seven! That's one yard shy of the school record he already shares. Fourteen to 10 at the half, and I liked our chances.

Then it all went sideways. Kienholz completed every throw he attempted after halftime, and our offense couldn't get out of its own way. We finished with 150 yards and eight first downs, went 2 for 13 on third down and gave the ball away four times. Holden Geriner threw two interceptions. articles.title: Louisville vs Pitt: Lincoln Kienholz Throws Five, Cards Win a Sixth Straight, 42-10
articles.matchup: Final: Louisville Cardinals (8-3) 42, Pittsburgh Panthers (6-5) 10, Sat., Nov. 21, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville. Next: at Kentucky, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Kroger Field, Lexington
articles.text:
Nine for nine. That's what Lincoln Kienholz did after halftime on Saturday night: nine throws, nine completions, 149 yards. Louisville 42, Pitt 10 at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, and the Cardinals have won six in a row. We're 8-3, 7-2 in the ACC. Red birds rising.

Kienholz threw five touchdowns, a season high, and he did it against one of the best run defenses in the country, a group that made us earn every inch on the ground. So he went to the air. TreyShun Hurry caught a 13-yarder to open the scoring. Lawayne McCoy got two, from 14 and 23. Tre Richardson got two, from 33 and 23, and finished with eight catches for 114 yards. Twenty-five of 41 for 309 yards on the night. Give that man the keys to the city.

The first half was choppy, I'll admit. Pitt scooped up a Kienholz fumble and took it 31 yards to tie it 7-7. Then they intercepted him late in the half and their kicker drilled a 57-yarder at the gun. 14-10 at the break, and the place was a little uneasy.

Then the defense took this game by the throat. We forced four turnovers. Kaleb Beasley and Brycen Scott each recovered fumbles in Pitt territory, and both turned into touchdown throws. Benjamin Perry and T.J. Capers each intercepted Pitt quarterbacks. Pitt's offense ended the night with 150 yards and eight first downs. Eight! Perry also made eight tackles, and Tayon Holloway had a sack.

We outscored them 28-0 in the second half and held the ball for more than 39 minutes. Keyjuan Brown carried it 18 times and punched in a 1-yard score late. Complete control, from the opening kick of the third quarter to the final whistle.

Six straight. Now it's Lexington next Saturday, and you know exactly what that means. Bring the Governor's Cup home where it belongs. Go Cards, and L1C4!

articles.title: Kentucky vs Missouri: Kenny Darby Catches 110 Yards, Wildcats Drop a Third Straight, 28-14
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri Tigers (7-4) 28, Kentucky Wildcats (7-4) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, Memorial Stadium, Columbia. Next: vs Louisville, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Kroger Field, Lexington
articles.text:
Big Blue Nation, I've got a stat that will make you throw your remote. Kentucky had 28 first downs in Columbia on Saturday night. Missouri had 16. We outgained them. We held the ball for nearly 34 minutes. And we lost by two touchdowns. Missouri 28, Kentucky 14, and the Wildcats are 7-4, 5-4 in conference play.

Six and one feels like a long time ago now. That's three straight losses, and this one was all about what happened inside the 20. Adam Zouagui kicked field goals from 23 and 26 yards, and both times I was thinking about the touchdowns we didn't get.

Meanwhile, Austin Simmons had the night of his life against our secondary. Four touchdown throws, including a 60-yarder and a 41-yarder. Every time we made it close in yardage, they made it far on the board.

Kenny Minchey kept slinging. He completed 27 of 43 for 288 yards. Kenny Darby caught eight for 110, including a 44-yarder, and Willie Rodriguez caught eight for 93. Early in the fourth quarter, Jovantae Barnes ran it in and then caught a two-point throw from Minchey, and it was 28-14 with 13:23 left. I thought we had a real chance.

Then, with about five minutes left and the ball at the Missouri 15, Barnes got the ball punched out. A few minutes later, an interception ended it. A fumble at their 15 and an interception, both in the fourth quarter. That's the ballgame.

The defense had some moments. Terhyon Nichols intercepted Simmons and broke up two throws. Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace made a tackle and a half for loss. Sam Greene and Jaden Williams made six tackles apiece.

Seven wins is still seven wins. And next Saturday, Louisville comes to Kroger Field for the Governor's Cup. Beat the Cards and this whole November slide gets a lot easier to swallow. Go Cats, and bring the noise to Lexington.

articles.title: Missouri vs Kentucky: Austin Simmons Throws Four, Tigers Snap the Skid, 28-14
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri Tigers (7-4) 28, Kentucky Wildcats (7-4) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, Memorial Stadium, Columbia. Next: vs Oklahoma, Sat., Nov. 28, 4:15 PM ET, Memorial Stadium, Columbia
articles.text:
Austin Simmons, take a bow. Seventeen of 22, 314 yards, four touchdowns. Missouri 28, Kentucky 14 at Faurot Field, the skid is dead, and the Tigers are 7-4, 4-4 in the SEC. I'm hoarse, and I don't care one bit.

We'd lost two straight and three of four coming in, and you could feel the nerves in Memorial Stadium when Kentucky kicked a field goal on its first drive. Then Simmons went off. He hit Donovan Olugbode for a 7-yard score to take the lead. He found Jude James from 23 for James' first career touchdown catch, finishing a 94-yard drive, and it was 14-3. Early in the third, Naeshaun Montgomery got behind everybody for a 41-yarder. Three touchdowns, three different receivers.

And after Kentucky kicked another field goal, Simmons and Olugbode hooked up again, this time for 60 yards. 28-6. Olugbode finished with five catches for 105 yards and two scores. Cayden Lee caught six for 61. Simmons averaged more than 14 yards a throw. That's a quarterback in rhythm. And Jamal Roberts ground out 67 tough yards on 23 carries to keep Kentucky's defense honest.

The defense bent plenty. Kentucky had 28 first downs and more yards than we did. But when it mattered, our guys made plays. With about five minutes left and Kentucky at our 15, Daeden Hopkins punched the ball loose and Robert Woodyard Jr. scooped it up. A few minutes later, Santana Banner intercepted Kenny Minchey to slam the door. Banner also made 12 tackles. Hopkins had two sacks. Sione Laulea had an interception of his own.

That's two straight against Kentucky, after they'd taken seven of the previous eight. And it's at least seven wins for a fourth straight season. That's a program.

Oklahoma comes to CoMo next Saturday afternoon. Get there early, get loud, and let's send the Sooners home unhappy. M-I-Z!

articles.title: SMU vs Notre Dame: Kendrick Raphael Breaks a 70-Yarder, Mustangs Stall in South Bend, 24-3
articles.matchup: Final: Notre Dame Fighting Irish (10-1) 24, SMU Mustangs (7-4) 3, Sat., Nov. 21, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame. Next: at Stanford, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Stanford Stadium, Stanford
articles.text:
Pony fans, I've watched this team score on just about everybody for years. Then came Saturday night in South Bend. Notre Dame 24, SMU 3. Three points. It's the fewest we've scored in a game since 2016, and we're 7-4.

Here's the part that makes me want to throw my hat across the room. We moved the ball. Kendrick Raphael broke a 70-yard run and finished with 100 yards on just 12 carries. Yamir Knight caught nine balls for 115 yards, including a 41-yarder. Six of our drives died in Notre Dame territory. All we got out of the whole night was one Brendan Baird field goal from 40 yards.

Three times we got stopped on fourth down, at the Irish 19, the 3 and the 2. The 2! Late in the second quarter we were at their 24 and Kevin Jennings threw one into the end zone that their safety went way up and took away. That's 14 points, maybe more, left on that field. Jennings finished 24 of 45 for 216 yards, and he took some big hits.

Our defense did its job for a long stretch. Alexander Kilgore made 12 tackles. Jayvon Thomas intercepted CJ Carr, and Sael Reyes recovered a fumble. After a 21-yard touchdown catch gave Notre Dame a 14-3 lead in the second quarter, we held the Irish to 10 more points. Against a top-10 team, on their field, that's a respectable night for the defense. The offense just couldn't cash a single trip inside the 20.

That's two straight weeks with fewer than 10 points, and this team is better than that. Way better. We've got one more regular-season game, at Stanford next Saturday, and I want to see the old SMU show up out there.

Eight wins is still on the board. Pony Up, Mustangs. Go take it.

articles.title: Notre Dame vs SMU: Jordan Faison's One-Hander and a Brick-Wall Defense, Irish Win 24-3
articles.byline: Declan Moriarty-Chen, The Notre Dame Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Notre Dame Fighting Irish (10-1) 24, SMU Mustangs (7-4) 3, Sat., Nov. 21, Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame. Next: at Syracuse, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, JMA Wireless Dome, Syracuse
articles.text:
Six SMU drives died in our territory on Saturday night, every one of them stuffed by a Notre Dame defense that was flat-out mean. Notre Dame 24, SMU 3 in South Bend, and the Irish are 10-1 and perfect at home. Touchdown Jesus approves.

Three of those stands came on fourth down, at our 19, our 3 and our 2. You want a defense that plays with an attitude? That's it. SMU hadn't scored this few points since 2016. Boubacar Traore was in their backfield all night with two and a half tackles for loss. Adon Shuler got a sack. Joey O'Brien made seven tackles. And late in the second quarter, with SMU at our 24, Jayden Sanders went up in the end zone and came down with a leaping interception. Beautiful.

CJ Carr was cool as ever. He went 19 of 29 for 312 yards, and his best throw of the night found Jordan Faison in the end zone from 21 yards out. Faison reached out with one hand and reeled it in. I screamed so loud the guy in front of me turned around. That made it 14-3. Faison finished with seven catches for 109 yards, and Jaden Greathouse hauled in a 62-yarder.

Cooper Flanagan got us on the board with a 2-yard run in the first quarter. Spencer Porath kicked a 32-yard field goal with two seconds left in the half for a 17-3 lead. Nolan James Jr. ran 15 times for 98 yards and put the final points up with a 4-yard run early in the third.

Was it a perfect night? No. We put the ball on the ground once and threw an interception. But when your defense plays like this, you can afford a mistake or two.

Ten wins. Syracuse next Saturday, and the Irish can clinch a College Football Playoff spot with one more. Cheer, cheer for old Notre Dame. Let's finish the job in the Dome.

articles.title: South Carolina vs Georgia: Malik Orsan Kicks Two, but Gamecocks Can't Hang With No. 1, 34-6
articles.byline: Beaumont 'Beau' Cheraw, The South Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Bulldogs (10-1) 34, South Carolina Gamecocks (6-5) 6, Sat., Nov. 21, Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia. Next: at Clemson, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Memorial Stadium (Clemson, SC), Clemson
articles.text:
When 2001 started blaring and LaNorris Sellers took us inside the Georgia 20 on the first two drives, I thought Williams-Brice was about to host the upset of the year. South Carolina led the No. 1 team in the country 6-3. Then the walls closed in. Georgia 34, South Carolina 6, and we're 6-5, 4-5 in the SEC.

Let's give the opening its due. Sellers drove us for 100 yards in that first quarter, and Malik Orsan drilled field goals from 31 and 32. It was loud, it was rocking, and the Dawgs looked rattled. I'll remember those 15 minutes.

After that, our offense went dark. We managed 118 yards the rest of the night. Sellers got sacked three times, finished with 87 yards through the air and threw an interception inside the Georgia 20 that killed our best drive of the second half. Jabree Coleman ran hard for 44 yards, and Jawarn Howell chipped in 32, but Georgia owned the ball for more than 37 minutes. You can't win when the other team won't give it back.

The defense fought like crazy for as long as it could. Justin Okoronkwo made 12 tackles. Peyton Williams had 11 and broke up a throw. Jaquel Holman intercepted Gunner Stockton and returned it 21 yards, the only mistake their quarterback made all night. Fred Johnson made eight stops. But Georgia converted a fourth down in the second quarter, scored right before halftime, and pulled away from there.

It's been a roller coaster of a year. This team won four straight SEC games in October and November, and nobody can take that away. We're bowl eligible. And the biggest game on the calendar is still ahead.

Clemson. Death Valley. The Palmetto Bowl. Beat the Tigers on their own field and every Gamecock in this state sleeps happy all winter. Forever to Thee, and Go Gamecocks.

articles.title: Georgia vs South Carolina: Nate Frazier Scores Twice, Dawgs Punch a Sixth Straight Atlanta Ticket
articles.matchup: Final: Georgia Bulldogs (10-1) 34, South Carolina Gamecocks (6-5) 6, Sat., Nov. 21, Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia. Next: vs Georgia Tech, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Sanford Stadium, Athens
articles.text:
Six in a row. Nobody in the history of this conference had ever made six straight SEC Championship Games until tonight. Georgia 34, South Carolina 6 at Williams-Brice Stadium, and the Dawgs are 10-1, 8-1 in the SEC and headed back to Atlanta. Book the hotel, Bulldog Nation.

For one quarter, the Gamecocks made it interesting. LaNorris Sellers moved them inside our 20 twice, and Malik Orsan kicked two field goals. They led 6-3, and Columbia was loud. Then our defense figured it out, and the Gamecocks gained just 118 more yards all game. Our front sacked Sellers three times, and we held him to 87 yards throwing.

The second quarter turned it. Gunner Stockton converted a fourth-and-3 to Jaden Reddell near midfield, then dropped a 37-yarder in to Talyn Taylor along the sideline to the 1. Nate Frazier punched it in. 10-6, and we never trailed again. Frazier scored again from 2 yards on our first possession of the second half. He finished with 94 yards on 23 carries, and he ran like every yard was personal.

Stockton was surgical. Nineteen of 23 for 281 yards and a touchdown, a 14-yard catch-and-run by Craig Dandridge in the fourth. Reddell caught a 66-yarder. Peyton Woodring hit from 25 and 40, and Nick Peal finished it with a 1-yard score late. We even recovered an onside kick, and Sacovie White-Helton ripped off a 35-yard punt return to set up points.

Khalil Barnes intercepted Sellers inside our 20 to end South Carolina's best second-half drive. Justin Williams had a sack and a half, Chris Cole got half a sack, and KJ Bolden made seven tackles. Zero turnovers for us. We controlled the clock for more than 37 minutes.

Georgia Tech comes to Sanford next for Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate, and then it's Atlanta, whoever shows up. Ten wins, one more rival to put away. How 'bout them Dawgs!

articles.title: Arkansas State vs Louisiana Tech: AG McGhee Makes 13 Tackles, Red Wolves Fall in Ruston, 48-3
articles.byline: Ty Doucet-Harmon, The Arkansas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs (9-2) 48, Arkansas State Red Wolves (4-7) 3, Sat., Nov. 21, Joe Aillet Stadium, Ruston. Next: vs Troy, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:00 PM ET, Centennial Bank Stadium, Jonesboro
articles.text:
There's no nice way to put this, Red Wolves fans, so I won't try. Louisiana Tech 48, Arkansas State 3 in Ruston, and it was every bit that ugly. We're 4-7, 2-5 in the Sun Belt, and the drive home to Jonesboro felt about twice as long as the drive down to Ruston did this morning.

We were in it for about a quarter. Louisiana Tech scored first on a 1-yard run, and Clune Van Andel answered with a 45-yard field goal early in the second to make it 7-3. I'll be honest, I let myself dream a little. Then Blake Baker threw three touchdowns before halftime, the last a 52-yarder with 44 seconds left, and it was 28-3 at the break.

The numbers tell the rest. We ran it 28 times for 26 yards. We committed 12 penalties for 85 yards. We gave it away twice and went 3 for 13 on third down. You can't beat anybody like that, let alone the team that hasn't lost in league play.

There were a few bright spots, and I'm going to hang onto them. AG McGhee made 13 tackles and never stopped chasing. Tre Stevens and Shaun Williams each got a sack. Trey Owens completed 18 of 28 for 209 yards and stood in there all night while the pocket kept collapsing. Nana Burris caught four balls for 52 yards, and Jaylen Bonelli had a 36-yard grab.

Look, the season ends next Saturday, and a bowl is off the table. But Troy is coming to Jonesboro, and these seniors deserve to walk off that field one more time with a win. Fill Centennial Bank Stadium, bring the scarlet and black, and howl like you mean it.

Wolves Up. We're not done until the last whistle blows on this season, and neither are they.

articles.title: Louisiana Tech vs Arkansas State: Blake Baker Throws Four, Bulldogs Stay Perfect in the Sun Belt
articles.byline: Booker 'Champ' Tullos, The Louisiana Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs (9-2) 48, Arkansas State Red Wolves (4-7) 3, Sat., Nov. 21, Joe Aillet Stadium, Ruston. Next: at Georgia Southern, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro
articles.text:
Seven and oh in the Sun Belt. Say it slow, Bulldog fans, because it sounds even better that way. Louisiana Tech 48, Arkansas State 3 on Saturday night at Joe Aillet Stadium, and we're 9-2 overall, 7-0 in conference play and 6-0 in Ruston.

Blake Baker had himself a night. He went 16 of 23 for 291 yards and a career-high four touchdown throws, and he ran for 47 yards and another score. That's five touchdowns for the quarterback, and he made it look like a Tuesday practice. He shared the wealth, too, finding four different guys in the end zone.

The second quarter was a blowout all by itself. We led 7-3 after Eli Finley's 1-yard plunge and an Arkansas State field goal. Then Baker capped a 12-play, 75-yard drive with a 10-yard touchdown to Finley. Less than two minutes later he hit Marcus Calwise Jr. from 18. And right before the half, Rayshun Hurt caught a 52-yard bomb, his only catch of the night, and made it count. 28-3 at the break. Twenty-one points in one quarter.

Jalen Mickens finished with six catches for 110 yards, and his 24-yard touchdown early in the fourth made it 42-3. Finley had five catches for 84 yards to go with his two scores. Andrew Burnette added a 22-yard touchdown run late. We piled up 488 yards and didn't give the ball away once.

And the defense? Ridiculous. Arkansas State ran 28 times for 26 yards. Zheric Hill had three tackles for loss and a sack, Alonzo Jackson Jr. and Jadon Mayfield each got home once, Sam Fongang came up with an interception, and Jordan McRae recovered a fumble. The Red Wolves managed 13 first downs all night.

One more regular-season game, at Georgia Southern next Saturday, and this team is playing its best football right now. Statesboro, get ready for some red, white and blue. Every Bulldog in Lincoln Parish is fired up, and so am I.

articles.title: San José State vs UNLV: Carson Clark Catches 102 Yards, Spartans Fall Two Short, 24-22
articles.byline: Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, The San José State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: UNLV Rebels (7-4) 24, San José State Spartans (5-7) 22, Sat., Nov. 21, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose. Next: vs North Dakota State, Fri., Nov. 27, 3:30 PM ET, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose
articles.text:
Two points. One throw. That's all that stood between the Spartans and a wild celebration on Saturday night at CEFCU Stadium, and the ball didn't bounce our way. UNLV 24, San José State 22. We're 5-7, 3-5 in the Mountain West, and I'm sitting in my car in the parking lot replaying that last snap.

We were down 24-13 going into the fourth quarter, and this team refused to fold. Trajan Sinatra hit a 27-yard field goal with 6:51 left to make it 24-16. Then Luke Weaver led a drive I'll remember for a long time, and with 45 seconds to go he dropped a 30-yard touchdown in to Carson Clark. The place erupted. Down two. Weaver dropped back for the tie, and the throw fell incomplete.

Clark was the best player on the field. Eight catches, 102 yards and that late touchdown. Weaver threw for 250 yards and two scores, the first a 33-yarder to Jabari Bates in the first quarter that tied it 7-7. Sinatra was money from close range, with three field goals, two from 29 yards and one from 27. Dominique McKenzie ripped off a 79-yard kickoff return that had everybody on their feet.

Dylan Lee was everywhere on defense with 13 tackles. Naseri Danielson made eight, Caleb Womack intercepted Jackson Arnold, and Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa jumped on a fumble. Holding UNLV to 24 points and taking the ball away twice is a good night's work for any defense. We just couldn't get it done on the ground, with 56 rushing yards, and too many drives stalled into field goals.

Here's the good part. We've got one more game, at home, on Friday against North Dakota State. Win it and we're at six wins and headed to a bowl. One game, one goal, everybody in. Spartans Up, and pack CEFCU on Friday.

articles.title: UNLV vs San José State: Jackson Arnold Does It Both Ways, Rebels Hang On, 24-22
articles.matchup: Final: UNLV Rebels (7-4) 24, San José State Spartans (5-7) 22, Sat., Nov. 21, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose. Next: vs Nevada, Sat., Nov. 28, 9:00 PM ET, Allegiant Stadium
articles.text:
Forty-five seconds. That's how long I held my breath on Saturday night in San Jose. San José State had just scored to pull within two, their quarterback dropped back for the two-point try, and the ball hit the turf. UNLV 24, San José State 22. We're 7-4, 5-2 in the Mountain West, and my heart rate is finally coming back down.

Jackson Arnold carried this team. He threw for 197 yards on 17 of 27, including a 38-yard rocket to Keyan Burnett in the second quarter that put us back in front 14-10. He led us in rushing too, with 66 yards on 16 carries, and he finished the job himself with a 1-yard plunge with 16 seconds left in the third quarter. That made it 24-13, and it turned out we needed every point.

Jai'Den Thomas got us started with a 9-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Taeshaun Lyons was Arnold's go-to target all night and caught nine balls for 85 yards. Ramon Villela drilled a 32-yard field goal with 34 seconds left in the half, and we went to the locker room up 17-13.

The defense made the plays that won it. Andre Porter intercepted Luke Weaver and also got a piece of a sack. Jake Pope made nine tackles, and Cam Santee had seven with a tackle and a half for loss. San José State ran for just 56 yards on 23 tries. When their kicker kept trotting out for field goals instead of touchdowns, I knew we were in decent shape.

Was it pretty at the end? No. Weaver hit Carson Clark for a 30-yarder with 45 seconds left, and I aged five years. But a road win is a road win, and we held the ball for more than 34 minutes.

Now it's Nevada at home with the Fremont Cannon up for grabs, in our house. Seven wins and counting. Paint that cannon red, Rebels.

articles.title: Kansas State vs Arizona: Rodney Fields Jr. Runs for 144, Wildcats Fall in Overtime, 35-28
articles.byline: Hattie Brandvold, The Kansas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Arizona Wildcats (8-3) 35, Kansas State Wildcats (4-7) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan. Next: at Iowa State, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Jack Trice Stadium, Ames
articles.text:
Purple people, I stood in that freezing rain for four quarters and an overtime, and I'd do it again tomorrow. Kansas State had Arizona beaten on Senior Day. Up 28-17 with less than 11 minutes to go, at home, in a storm. Then it slipped away. Arizona 35, Kansas State 28 in overtime, and we're 4-7, 1-7 in the Big 12.

Let me tell you about the good stuff first, because there was plenty. Rodney Fields Jr. carried the ball 28 times for 144 yards and a touchdown, and he ran like he was mad at the weather. Dillon Duff took off on a 58-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, nobody laid a finger on him, and that gave us our first lead at 21-17. He finished with 66 rushing yards and also hit Derrick Salley Jr. for a 34-yard touchdown right before halftime.

Then the special teams and defense handed us a gift. Our punter pinned Arizona at its own 2, their quarterback fumbled the snap, and Wendell Gregory pounced on it in the end zone. 28-17 with 10:55 left. The whole stadium was soaked and screaming.

But Arizona kicked a field goal, got the ball right back and scored with 1:52 left, and the two-point try tied it at 28-28. In overtime they scored on a 25-yard throw, and our last try came up short on fourth down at the 3. I couldn't feel my hands, and it wasn't the cold.

Logan Bartley made 10 tackles and broke up two throws. Gabe Powers had eight tackles and a sack, and Asa Newsom added another sack. As a team we ran for 239 yards. The effort was there. The finish wasn't.

Five straight losses, and no bowl this year. It stings. Still, the finale is the one that matters most in Manhattan. Iowa State is waiting in Ames for Farmageddon. EMAW. Beat the Cyclones and this winter won't feel nearly so cold.

articles.title: Arizona vs Kansas State: Noah Fifita Wins It in Overtime in the Manhattan Rain, 35-28
articles.matchup: Final: Arizona Wildcats (8-3) 35, Kansas State Wildcats (4-7) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan. Next: vs Arizona State, Sat., Nov. 28, 9:00 PM ET, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson
articles.text:
Desert kids don't know rain, they said. Tell that to Noah Fifita. In a cold, driving downpour at Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Arizona came back from 11 points down in the last 11 minutes and won it in overtime. Arizona 35, Kansas State 28. Arizona sits at 8-3, 5-3 in Big 12 play, and I'm still wringing out my socks.

It looked bleak. With 10:55 left, Fifita couldn't handle a snap at our 2 after a great Kansas State punt, and Wendell Gregory recovered it for a touchdown. 28-17, and their whole Senior Day crowd was roaring in the rain. My buddy started checking flight times.

Then Fifita went to work. Michael Salgado-Medina knocked in a 26-yard field goal to make it 28-20. We got the ball right back, and with 1:52 left Fifita found Isaiah Mizell for a 35-yard touchdown. Then he hit Giovanni Richardson for the two-point try, and it was 28-28. I hugged a guy from Tucson I'd never met.

articles.title: Virginia Tech vs Miami: Hokies Jump Out 14-0, Then Watch Miami Rally, 28-20
articles.byline: Ruthanne Dellinger, The Virginia Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Miami Hurricanes (10-1) 28, Virginia Tech Hokies (6-5) 20, Sat., Nov. 21, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens. Next: vs Virginia, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:00 PM ET, Lane Stadium, Blacksburg
articles.text:
Hokie Nation, for one quarter in Miami Gardens we looked like the team that runs this conference. Virginia Tech led 14-0, then 20-14 going into the final quarter at Hard Rock Stadium. And then Mark Fletcher Jr. happened. Miami 28, Virginia Tech 20, and we're 6-5, 3-5 in the ACC.

The start was perfect. We won the toss, took the ball and went 75 yards in 15 plays. Ethan Grunkemeyer flipped a 5-yard touchdown to Jeffrey Overton Jr., and the visiting section was on its feet. Three plays later Joshua Clarke intercepted a ball that bounced off a Miami back's hands, and Messiah Mickens ran it in from 15. Fourteen points before Miami could find its helmets.

Clarke was a monster. Two interceptions, 38 return yards and six tackles. John Love was perfect too, with field goals from 38 and 27, and the second one put us up 20-14 in the third. We didn't give the ball away once and got flagged just one time all night. That's disciplined football.

But we couldn't run it. Forty rushing yards on 19 carries won't win you many road games in this league, and Miami kept the ball for more than 35 minutes. The killer was a 17-play, 90-yard drive that ended with Fletcher scoring on the first snap of the fourth quarter. He scored again with 2:08 left, and that was it. Their kicker also hit a 59-yarder at the halftime gun, which, fine, was a great kick.

Grunkemeyer went 22 of 35 for 168 yards. Que'Sean Brown caught seven balls for 94 yards, including a 45-yarder, and Luke Reynolds caught 10. Kaleb Spencer led us with eight tackles, and Tyson Flowers had seven.

We're bowl eligible, and the best game of the year is still on the calendar. Virginia comes to Lane Stadium next for the Commonwealth Cup. Enter Sandman, jump in the stands, and let's send that trophy straight back to Blacksburg where it belongs.

articles.title: Miami vs Virginia Tech: Mark Fletcher Jr. Scores Three, Canes Clinch the ACC Title Game
articles.byline: Javi 'The Breeze' Castillo, The Miami Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Miami Hurricanes (10-1) 28, Virginia Tech Hokies (6-5) 20, Sat., Nov. 21, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens. Next: vs Boston College, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
Charlotte, here we come. Down 14 points before the first quarter was even done, the Canes dug out, and Miami 28, Virginia Tech 20 sends us to the ACC Championship Game against Wake Forest on Dec. 5. We're 10-1, 8-0 in the ACC, and Hard Rock was shaking.

I won't sugarcoat the start. Virginia Tech went 75 yards on the opening drive. Three plays after that, a Darian Mensah throw bounced off Javian Mallory's hands, Joshua Clarke grabbed it, a flag moved it to our 15 and Messiah Mickens scored. 14-0. I paced the aisle for the rest of the quarter.

Then Jake Weinberg got the comeback started. He hit from 49 to get us on the board, Mark Fletcher Jr. plunged in from a yard out, and Mensah found Daylyn Upshaw for two to make it 14-11. And as the first half expired, Weinberg drilled a 59-yard field goal. Fifty-nine! That's the longest in Miami history, breaking a record of 57 that three different kickers shared. It was 17-14 at the break, and the place sounded like we were the ones winning.

Fletcher owned the fourth quarter. On the first play of the period he capped a 17-play, 90-yard drive from a yard out, and we had our first lead of the night, 21-20. With 2:08 left he ran in from 11 to make it 28-20, and our defense stopped the Hokies on downs with 1:27 to go. Three rushing touchdowns for the big man. When it gets tough, you hand it to Fletch.

Cooper Barkate and Vandrevius Jacobs each caught seven balls, Mensah threw for 241 yards, and we converted 9 of 14 on third down. The defense held Virginia Tech to 40 rushing yards. Mohamed Toure made nine tackles, and Xavier Lucas got a sack.

That's 12 straight ACC wins, the longest streak in school history, and six straight against the Hokies. Boston College visits next. Then the title game. It's all right there, Canes. Throw up the U and go get it.

Miami rallied from a 14-0 deficit and has won 12 straight ACC games, the longest run in school history.

articles.title: Maryland vs USC: DeJuan Williams Scores Twice, but Terps Fall at the Coliseum, 35-21
articles.matchup: Final: USC Trojans (8-3) 35, Maryland Terrapins (4-7) 21, Sat., Nov. 21, Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles. Next: vs Penn State, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, SECU Stadium, College Park
articles.text:
Terps, I flew home from Los Angeles with my red shell jacket zipped all the way up and my pride mostly intact. For one half, Maryland was the better team in the Coliseum. We went into the locker room leading 14-13, and the home crowd was booing their own team. The final says USC 35, Maryland 21, and we're 4-7, 2-6 in the Big Ten. But I saw a team that believes.

DeJuan Williams set the tone. On the first snap of the second quarter he busted a 52-yard touchdown run, and the handful of us in red went nuts. Later in the quarter we went 15 plays and Williams finished it from a yard out with 26 seconds left in the half. He ran 17 times for 83 yards and two scores.

Malik Washington was back running the show after missing last week, and he threw for 251 yards on 24 completions. Kaleb Webb and Preston Howard caught six balls apiece. And in the third quarter, Washington hit Chris Durr Jr. for a 67-yard touchdown that should have made it a two-score game. Flag. Illegal formation. Touchdown gone. USC drove for a score, and the whole night tilted.

That's when it got ugly. A tipped ball got intercepted, and USC scored. Then another interception on the very next snap, and another USC touchdown. In about five minutes, a one-point lead turned into 35-14. We threw three interceptions on the night, and you can't do that against a ranked team in its own building.

Lavain Scruggs was everywhere on defense with 12 tackles, nine solo and two for loss. Carlton Smith and Daniel Wingate each made seven. And Washington, who took a hit to his knee in the fourth, came back and scored on a 4-yard run himself late. That's toughness.

This team had won two straight before this trip, and nobody quit out there. Penn State comes to College Park next, and I want SECU Stadium packed and loud for the seniors. Fear the Turtle, today and always.
