articles.title: USC vs Maryland: Trent Mosley Scores Twice, Trojans Flip It After the Half, 35-21
articles.matchup: Final: USC Trojans (8-3) 35, Maryland Terrapins (4-7) 21, Sat., Nov. 21, Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles. Next: at UCLA, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Rose Bowl, Pasadena
articles.text:
I'll admit it. I was one of the grumblers at halftime. Maryland 14, USC 13 at the Coliseum, the Terps had just finished a 15-play drive, and I was staring at my program wondering what happened to my team. Then the second half started and the Trojans remembered who they are. USC 35, Maryland 21. We're 8-3, 5-3 in the Big Ten.

Trent Mosley is the real deal, and I don't care who hears me say it. The freshman caught a 13-yard touchdown from Jayden Maiava in the first quarter and a 9-yarder late in the third that put us back in front, 20-14. Eight catches, 78 yards, two scores. The kid has eight touchdown catches in eight games. Book him for the next three years.

And then the defense took charge. Jontez Williams intercepted a tipped ball, and Waymond Jordan punched it in from a yard out. Maiava found Tanook Hines for two, and it was 28-14. On Maryland's very next snap, Marcelles Williams came up with another interception, and Jordan scored again two plays later. 35-14. That whole avalanche took just a little more than five minutes. Prophet Brown added a third interception and led us with six tackles.

We also caught a break. Maryland had a 67-yard touchdown throw wiped out in the third quarter by an illegal formation flag, and we marched right down the field for Mosley's second score. I'll take it.

Maiava finished 21 of 35 for 237 yards and two touchdowns in his last game at the Coliseum, and Caden Chittenden hit field goals from 30 and 31 yards. Jordan ran 18 times with two scores. We've won 13 of 14 at home the past two seasons.

Now the big one. Across town, in Pasadena, against the team in powder blue. Beat the Bruins and all of this season's frustration gets a lot lighter. Fight On, and bring your voice to the Rose Bowl.

articles.title: Washington State vs Texas State: Isaiah Hung Scores, Cougars Fall in San Marcos, 42-14
articles.byline: Hank Palouse, The Washington State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas State Bobcats (7-4) 42, Washington State Cougars (2-9) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, UFCU Stadium, San Marcos.
articles.text:
Coug fans, I'll give you the good news first, because there's a little of it. Owen Eshelman marched us 60 yards on our first possession in San Marcos and hit Daniel Blood for a 22-yard touchdown. We led 7-0. It was the best five plays of the night. Texas State 42, Washington State 14, and we're 2-9, 1-6 in the Pac-12.

Everything after that drive hurt. Brad Jackson tied it on a 9-yard run. Then our punt got blocked, Texas State recovered at our 5, and Davian Jackson scored three plays later. 14-7. Brad Jackson broke a 44-yarder in the second quarter, and it was 21-7 at halftime. Their quarterback ran for 127 yards on eight carries, and Torrance Burgess Jr. added 146 more. All told, Texas State ran for 299 yards. That's a long night for any defense.

Eshelman is a freshman, and he kept fighting. He went 21 of 33 for 150 yards, didn't throw an interception, and ran 13 times. Branden Ganashamoorthy caught six balls for 58 yards. Kirby Vorhees ran for 55 on 12 carries. We didn't give the ball away once all night, which counts for something in a season like this one. But we went 3 for 13 on third down and 1 for 4 on fourth, and you can't keep pace like that.

Credit the guys on defense who kept swinging. Keith Brown made nine tackles, two for loss, and got a sack. Linus Zunk had a tackle and a half for loss. And Isaiah Hung gave us the play of the night in the fourth quarter, scooping up a Texas State fumble and taking it 30 yards to the house. He also had seven tackles. That kid plays like it's the Apple Cup every week.

Two wins is not what anybody in Pullman signed up for. But I saw a freshman quarterback who doesn't scare, and a defense with a few real hitters. Go Cougs. I'm still waving the flag, and I'm not putting it down.

articles.title: Texas State vs Washington State: Brad Jackson Scores Four, Bobcats Roll to 7-4
articles.byline: Yesenia Calderwood, The Texas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas State Bobcats (7-4) 42, Washington State Cougars (2-9) 14, Sat., Nov. 21, UFCU Stadium, San Marcos.
articles.text:
Somebody check on the Washington State defense, because Brad Jackson just ran through it like a kid cutting through a backyard. Texas State 42, Washington State 14 at UFCU Stadium, and the Bobcats close out the regular season at 7-4, 5-2 in our first year in the new Pac-12.

Yes, the Cougars scored first. Owen Eshelman found Daniel Blood from 22 yards out on their opening drive, and for about three minutes San Marcos got quiet. Then Jackson kept it for 9 yards to tie it, and the special teams flipped the whole night. Jordan Sample blocked a punt, Jordan Martin recovered it at the Washington State 5, and three plays later freshman Davian Jackson plowed in from a yard out. 14-7, and we never looked back.

Brad Jackson was a one-man highlight reel. He ran eight times for 127 yards and three touchdowns, from 9, 44 and 36 yards. The 44-yarder in the second quarter put us up 21-7 at the half. He also went 11 of 19 for 122 yards and hit Beau Sparks for a 15-yard score early in the fourth. Four touchdowns from your quarterback, and he barely broke a sweat.

Torrance Burgess Jr. did the heavy lifting the rest of the way: 19 carries, 146 yards and a 1-yard score in the third quarter. As a team we ran for 299 yards. Two hundred ninety-nine! The offensive front deserves a steak dinner.

The defense was nasty too. DonTerry Russell had a sack and a half, TJ Burkhalter got home for another, and Washington State went 3 for 13 on third down. The only blemish was a fumble that Isaiah Hung scooped and returned 30 yards late, long after this one was decided.

That's three straight wins and five of our last six, and the only loss in that stretch was the 46-45 heartbreaker at Boise State. Bowl eligible, Pac-12 respectable, and building. Eat 'Em Up, Cats! Wherever the bowl committee sends us, the maroon and gold will travel.

articles.title: Southern Miss vs South Alabama: Mario Sanders Goes for 143, Golden Eagles Fall, 40-35
articles.byline: Delphine 'Dee' Broussard, The Southern Miss Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: South Alabama Jaguars (6-5) 40, Southern Miss Golden Eagles (3-8) 35, Sat., Nov. 21, M. M. Roberts Stadium, Hattiesburg. Next: at Old Dominion, Sat., Nov. 28, 1:00 PM ET, S.B. Ballard Stadium, Norfolk
articles.text:
For about 13 minutes on Saturday, this was the best game of our season. Southern Miss led South Alabama by 10 heading into the fourth quarter at M. M. Roberts Stadium, and I was already planning what I'd say to my brother-in-law. Then the fourth quarter happened. South Alabama 40, Southern Miss 35. We're 3-8, 2-5 in the Sun Belt.

The third quarter was everything we've been waiting for. Jamarice Wilder bulled in from 1 yard, John White hit Steven Robinson for the two-point try, and we led 22-19. Then, with 45 seconds left in the quarter, White found Mario Sanders on a 50-yard strike. 29-19. I was hugging strangers.

And then South Alabama ran the ball down our throats. They scored 21 in the fourth, and PJ Martin broke a 50-yard run to take the lead with 7:48 to go. When he scored again from 6 yards with 1:57 left, it was 40-29. They kept our offense on the sideline for more than 37 minutes and ran for 247 yards. Our defense was on the field all day, and you could see it at the end.

But give this offense its due. White threw for 294 yards and three touchdowns. Sanders was unreal: seven catches, 143 yards and two scores, including a 45-yarder with 53 seconds left that made it 40-35. The two-point try didn't connect, and South Alabama recovered the onside kick. Grant Page caught a 46-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and Robinson ran 11 times for 82 yards, including a 23-yard score in the first.

Landon Sylvie led the defense with nine tackles and a sack. Champ Lewis broke up two throws and had seven stops. Tyler Lassiter added a tackle and a half for loss.

Three wins isn't what anybody wanted. But Sanders and White gave us something to hang onto. One more game, at Old Dominion next Saturday, and I want these seniors to walk off that field in Norfolk with a win. To The Top, Eagles. Finish it.

articles.title: South Alabama vs Southern Miss: PJ Martin Runs Wild, Jaguars Rally to a Bowl, 40-35
articles.byline: Azalea Fairhope-Grice, The South Alabama Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: South Alabama Jaguars (6-5) 40, Southern Miss Golden Eagles (3-8) 35, Sat., Nov. 21, M. M. Roberts Stadium, Hattiesburg. Next: vs App State, Fri., Nov. 27, 3:00 PM ET, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile
articles.text:
Ten points down, one quarter left, on the road in Hattiesburg. I've seen this movie before and I usually hate the ending. Not this time. South Alabama 40, Southern Miss 35, and your Jaguars are 6-5 and bowl eligible.

Let's be honest about the third quarter. Southern Miss scored twice, punched in a two-point try, and when Mario Sanders got loose for a 50-yarder with 45 seconds left in the period, it was 29-19 and M. M. Roberts Stadium was rocking. I pulled my hat down across my eyes. Then my guys took the fourth quarter and made it theirs, 21 points' worth.

Bishop Davenport started it. He hit Anthony Eager for 13 yards and a score early in the fourth, and suddenly it was 29-26. Then PJ Martin took a handoff, found a crease and ran 50 yards untouched, and we were up 33-29 with 7:48 to go. Martin wasn't finished. With 1:57 left he went in from 6 yards out, 40-29, and I finally exhaled. Sixteen carries, 128 yards, two fourth-quarter touchdowns. That kid is a closer.

Davenport was sharp all day: 20 of 28 for 267 yards and two scores through the air, plus a 3-yard touchdown run early in the first quarter. Eager caught eight balls for 102 yards and both touchdown throws, including a 38-yarder in the first quarter. Trae Stevenson piled up 128 yards on six catches. As a team we ran for 247 yards, went 3 for 3 on fourth down and held the ball for more than 37 minutes. Dylan Freebury drilled field goals from 29 and 33 yards.

The defense got burned on some deep balls, no point pretending otherwise, but Damyrion Darby came up with an interception and Jayvon Henderson made eight tackles. And when Southern Miss scored with 53 seconds left to make it a five-point game, we recovered the onside kick and that was that.

App State comes to Mobile on Friday for the regular-season finale, and we get to play it with a bowl trip already in our pocket. Six wins, a comeback for the scrapbook, and a running back nobody in the Sun Belt wants to see in the fourth quarter. Go Jags, and get loud at Hancock Whitney.

articles.title: North Carolina vs Virginia: Freshman Travis Burgess Throws for 354 and Runs for 106, but the Heels Fall 41-24
articles.byline: Ainsley Pemberton, The North Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Virginia Cavaliers (6-5) 41, North Carolina Tar Heels (5-6) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Scott Stadium, Charlottesville. Next: vs NC State, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill
articles.text:
Coach Bill Belichick didn't hold back after this one, so I won't either. He called it a bad performance all the way around. Outplayed, outcoached, out everything. Virginia 41, North Carolina 24 in Charlottesville, and we're 5-6, still one win short of a bowl.

But I'm going to start with the kid, because he's why I'm not throwing the remote. With Billy Edwards Jr. hurt from the Louisville game, freshman Travis Burgess got the start. He went 25 of 45 for 354 yards, ran 13 times for 106 more and a score, and threw a touchdown too. Even Virginia's coach, Tony Elliott, said afterward that the kid is going to be special. When the other sideline says it, you know it's real.

Jordan Shipp was a monster, nine catches for 149 yards. Mason Humphrey caught three balls for 95, including a 46-yard grab. Kaleb Jackson pounded in our first score from a yard out. As a team we piled up 581 yards and 28 first downs. That should be a win most Saturdays.

So why wasn't it? We left points everywhere. Two interceptions. A missed field goal and another one blocked. Two fourth-down tries in the third quarter came up empty, right when we needed to make it a game. Rece Verhoff did hit a 33-yarder at the end of the first half, and that was about the last good break we got for a while.

On the other side, Virginia shredded our coverage with throws to backs and tight ends. A running back took a short one 75 yards in the second quarter, and Beau Pribula threw four scores without a turnover. Xavier Lewis made 10 tackles, and Jaylen Harvey kept getting pressure, but it wasn't enough.

Burgess found Trech Kekahuna for 5 yards and then hit Shamar Easter on the two-point try late. He punched in another from 5 at the gun. Kid kept swinging until the very end.

One more chance to get to six wins, and it's against the team we'd most like to beat. NC State comes to Kenan Stadium next Saturday. Fill it in Carolina blue and go get that bowl. Go Heels.

articles.title: Virginia vs North Carolina: Beau Pribula Throws Four Scores, Cavaliers Go Bowling Again After a 41-24 Win
articles.matchup: Final: Virginia Cavaliers (6-5) 41, North Carolina Tar Heels (5-6) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Scott Stadium, Charlottesville. Next: at Virginia Tech, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:00 PM ET, Lane Stadium, Blacksburg
articles.text:
Beau Pribula picked the right Saturday to have the best throwing day of his Virginia career. Nineteen of 24, 297 yards, four touchdowns, no turnovers, and the Cavaliers beat North Carolina 41-24 at Scott Stadium. Wahoowa, and ring the bells across Grounds.

We're 6-5 and 4-4 in the ACC, bowl eligible for the second straight year. Back-to-back wins after a three-game skid. Running back Xavier Brown said this team decided to recommit and finish what it started, and I believe every word.

The game plan was sharp. Carolina loaded up its front, so Coach Tony Elliott said we had to lead with the throw, and we did. Thirteen of Pribula's 19 completions went to backs and tight ends. Da'Shawn Martin caught a 20-yard score in the first quarter. Then Jekail Middlebrook, a running back, took a short toss and ran 75 yards to the house. Middlebrook finished with five catches for 140 yards. Brown caught a 24-yarder in the third to make it 27-10, and tight end Dakota Twitty hauled in a 1-yarder early in the fourth to put it away.

Will Bettridge was perfect, hitting from 42 and 36 and going 5 for 5 on extras. Solomon Beebe added a 32-yard touchdown run late. Brown ran for 83 yards on 13 carries.

And the defense? Carolina piled up yards, but we came up with two fourth-down stops in the third quarter and forced two turnovers while giving the ball away zero times. Christian Ellis and Kam Robinson each intercepted a throw. Myles Brown made 10 tackles. Justin Ross knocked away three throws. Bend, bend, bend, don't break.

Even Bill Belichick had nothing nice to say about his own team afterward. Outplayed, outcoached, out everything, in his words. Not my words, but I won't argue.

Now comes the one that matters most around here. Virginia Tech in Blacksburg next Saturday. We're playing our best ball of the year, so let's go take the Commonwealth Cup. Go Hoos.

articles.title: North Texas vs Tulane: Jahiem White and Brendon Haygood Run for 251, but the Mean Green Fall 28-24 in New Orleans
articles.byline: Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, The North Texas Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Tulane Green Wave (6-5) 28, North Texas Mean Green (7-4) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Yulman Stadium, New Orleans. Next: vs UAB, Sat., Nov. 28, 4:00 PM ET, DATCU Stadium, Denton
articles.text:
Three quarterbacks. That's how many North Texas used on Saturday night in New Orleans, and a wide receiver was the last one standing. We still almost won. Tulane 28, Mean Green 24, and I don't know whether to be furious or proud. Both, I think.

Here's how it went down. Chris Jimerson Jr. made his first career start with Tayven Jackson hurt from last week. He was 8 of 16 for 124 yards before he went down with a non-contact injury early in the third quarter and didn't return. A freshman came in briefly. Then wide receiver James Tyre, a former high school quarterback, took the snaps, with some direct snaps to Brendon Haygood mixed in. Tyre went 4 of 7 for 63 yards. Wild.

And through all that chaos, we kept running the ball down Tulane's throat. Fifty-nine carries for 302 yards. Jahiem White ran 28 times for 148 yards. Haygood ran for 103 and two scores, including a 46-yard burst in the first quarter that put us up 14-0 and a 2-yarder in the fourth that made it 24-14. We held the ball for 37:27 and went 11 of 20 on third down. That's a team that refuses to quit.

Jimerson opened the scoring with a 6-yard run. Dominic De Freitas hit a 23-yard field goal for a 17-14 lead in the third. Max Reese caught six balls for 73 yards. Peyton Taylor picked off a throw and brought it back 27 yards. CJ Coombes made seven tackles.

Then Tulane hit two deep strikes in the final seven minutes, and that was that. With an emergency quarterback, we couldn't answer.

That's two straight losses after a 35-16 loss at UTSA last week snapped our six-game win streak. We're 7-4, 5-2 in league play, and we started the day sharing first place. The title picture is cloudy now, and I hate it.

But here's the thing. This team just played a road game with its fourth-string guy and a receiver taking the snaps and nearly stole it. That's heart. UAB comes to DATCU Stadium next Saturday for the finale, and the Mean Green faithful need to pack the place. Let's go, Mean Green.

articles.title: Tulane vs North Texas: Trace Johnson Throws Four Scores, Freshman Cameron Roberts Wins It Late, Green Wave Go Bowling 28-24
articles.matchup: Final: Tulane Green Wave (6-5) 28, North Texas Mean Green (7-4) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Yulman Stadium, New Orleans. Next: at South Florida, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa
articles.text:
Tulane didn't lead for one second of this game until there were 2:13 left on the clock. That's when Trace Johnson dropped a back-shoulder throw into the hands of Cameron Roberts at the front of the end zone, Yulman Stadium lost its mind, and the Green Wave beat North Texas 28-24 to become bowl eligible. Roll Wave, baby!

Let me tell you about Cameron Roberts. Freshman tight end. Came into Saturday with five catches all season. Left with four catches for 81 yards and two touchdowns, the 6-yarder that tied it at halftime and the 28-yard winner. Somebody get that kid a po'boy and a parade.

That winning drive was four plays and 87 yards. Johnson hit Roberts for 11, found Oliver Mitchell Jr. for 12, then went deep to Roberts for 36, and then the dagger. Four plays! I barely had time to stand up.

Johnson was terrific all night: 17 of 21 for 283 yards and four touchdowns. He hit Jaylin Lucas for a 69-yard strike in the first quarter to get us on the board after we fell behind 14-0, and he found Destyn Hill for 37 yards to cut a 24-14 deficit to three with 6:52 left. Hill had two catches for 44, and Lucas had three for 79.

North Texas pounded the ball, no doubt. They ran it 59 times for 302 yards and held it for more than 37 minutes. But our defense came up with the big ones. Joshua Moore and E'zaiah Shine each intercepted a throw. Makai Williams had two sacks. Dickson Agu was everywhere, with 13 tackles. North Texas went through three quarterbacks before the night was done, and our guys kept swarming.

Tulane football: down two touchdowns early, down 10 in the fourth, and still finding a way. That's the kind of team that's fun to follow in November.

We're 6-5 and 4-3 in the American. Bowl eligible. Next Saturday we head to Tampa to face South Florida to close the regular season. Take care of business in Tampa and we'll be choosing a nice December destination. Roll on, Wave.

articles.title: Memphis vs Navy: Jaylin Carter Runs for a Career-High 229 and Three Scores, but the Tigers Fall 38-34 in Annapolis
articles.matchup: Final: Navy Midshipmen (4-6) 38, Memphis Tigers (8-3) 34, Sat., Nov. 21, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, Annapolis. Next: vs Temple, Fri., Nov. 27, 3:30 PM ET, Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, Memphis
articles.text:
Jaylin Carter ran for 229 yards and three touchdowns on Saturday. He broke a 68-yarder. He broke a 60-yarder. And Memphis still walked out of Annapolis with a 38-34 loss to Navy that I'm going to be chewing on all week.

Coach Charles Huff summed it up in four words: we didn't tackle well. Against Navy, that's the whole ballgame. Jackson Gutierrez ran for 241 yards. The Mids ran for 335 as a team. And on the last drive, 13 plays and 66 yards, they ground it out and pushed a back across on fourth-and-1 with 15 seconds left. Fifteen seconds. Ugh.

It didn't have to go that way. We led 34-24 after Carter's 1-yard score with 12:38 to play. Then Gutierrez broke a 68-yard run, and then came that drive. Huff said the staff has to put guys in better spots and drill tackling harder in practice. I'll hold him to that.

Let me give Carter his flowers, because this was a career day. He tied it 7-7 with a 68-yard sprint in the first quarter, put us ahead 24-17 with a 21-yarder in the third, and pushed the lead to 10 in the fourth. Twenty-three carries, 10 yards a pop. That's a grown man.

Manny Covey ran 24 yards for a touchdown on the very next play after Marcus Stokes got sacked, fumbled, and we somehow recovered. Jermane Hayes caught five balls for 111 yards. Philippe Laforge hit from 48 and 47. We piled up 528 yards, and 273 of them came in the third quarter alone.

The giveaways killed us. An interception in the end zone wiped out Carter's 60-yarder early in the third, and a Navy fumble we turned into a field goal was about the only break we got. We finished with three turnovers to their one. Mike Montgomery made 11 tackles, and Dylan Smith and J'Mond Tapp each had 10.

We're 8-3 and 5-2 in the American, and we came in tied for first. The race just got a lot messier.

Temple comes to the Liberty Bowl on Friday. Get back to tackling, get back to winning, and let's see where the chips fall. Go Tigers, Go.

articles.title: Navy vs Memphis: Jackson Gutierrez Runs for 241, Vic Listorti Gets Pushed In With 15 Seconds Left, Mids Stun No. 24 Memphis 38-34
articles.byline: Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather, The Navy Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Navy Midshipmen (4-6) 38, Memphis Tigers (8-3) 34, Sat., Nov. 21, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, Annapolis. Next: at Charlotte, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte
articles.text:
Fourth-and-1 at the 6, down three, 15 seconds left. A field goal ties it and probably sends it to overtime. Coach Brian Newberry said go. Vic Listorti got stood up in a heap of bodies, the entire Navy offense shoved the pile, and the whole thing rolled into the end zone. Navy 38, No. 24 Memphis 34. Anchors aweigh, and somebody find me a chair.

Listorti said afterward he couldn't have scored without the guys behind him. That's Navy football in one sentence.

But that sentence doesn't happen without Jackson Gutierrez. Our quarterback ran 35 times for a career-high 241 yards and two scores, including a 68-yard sprint in the fourth quarter that cut a 34-24 hole to 34-31. He also threw a 72-yard touchdown to Charles Robinson on a reverse flea-flicker late in the third that had the whole stadium screaming. Four completions on the day, 110 yards. Quality, not quantity.

The final drive was a thing of beauty: 13 plays, 66 yards, so methodical that Memphis never even called a timeout. Newberry gave credit to offensive coordinator Drew Cronic and to Danny Payne on the sideline, and said everyone agreed they wanted to go for it. That's the kind of trust you can't fake.

The defense bent plenty against Jaylin Carter, but it made the plays that mattered. Maxwell Williams picked off a throw in the end zone early in the third to wipe out a 60-yard run. Aiden Lyczek made 10 tackles with a sack, and Griffen Willis added 10 more. Michael Barrow ran in our first score from 10 yards out. Nolan Bartley was 5 for 5 on extra points and drilled a 26-yard field goal at the halftime horn.

We ran it 54 times for 335 yards. That's who we are.

Yes, we're 4-6 and 3-4 in the league, and this season hasn't gone the way we wanted. But we just knocked a ranked team out of first place in the American, and this team looks like it's peaking at the right time.

Next up is a trip to Charlotte on Saturday. And after that, well, every Mid knows what's coming next month. Go Navy, Beat Army.

articles.title: Army vs East Carolina: Dawson Jones Kicks Two Field Goals on Senior Day, but a Trick Play Beats the Black Knights 10-6
articles.byline: Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke, The Army Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: East Carolina Pirates (7-4) 10, Army Black Knights (5-5) 6, Sat., Nov. 21, Michie Stadium, West Point. Next: at Rice, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, First Community Stadium, Houston
articles.text:
Senior day at Michie Stadium is supposed to end with a salute and a win. On Saturday it ended with a salute and a 10-6 loss to East Carolina, and I'm still standing at attention out of sheer stubbornness.

First, the salute, because these men earned it. Army recognized 30 seniors before kickoff, a group that won back-to-back bowl games in 2024 and 2025 and 36 games in all. They carried this program. Whatever happened afterward doesn't change that.

Now the game. It was a fistfight in a phone booth. Dawson Jones banged home a 46-yard field goal as the first half ended, the only points before the break. After ECU tied it in the third, Jones hit again from 43 early in the fourth quarter to give us a 6-3 lead. For a long stretch I thought that might be enough.

Then came the trick play. With about four and a half minutes left, ECU handed it to a wide receiver, we nearly sacked him, and he found a man alone in the end zone from 7 yards out. One play, the only touchdown of the day, and it beat us.

We had one last chance. We marched to the ECU 31, went for it on fourth down, and the throw was intercepted. That's the cruel part of football: you can play tough for 59 minutes and lose it on two snaps.

Don't let the scoreboard fool you about the defense. Caleb Williams intercepted a throw. Stephen Nnadozie and Dillon Stowers each made seven tackles. We held the ball for 33:44, ran it 47 times for 180 yards, and gave up only 10 points. Cale Hellums battled, running for 62 yards on 19 carries, and Godspower Nwawuihe added 44. Parker Poloskey caught five for 58.

We're 5-5 and 4-3 in the league. Two games remain, and this team is chasing a third straight bowl, which has happened only once before in program history.

First comes a trip to Houston to face Rice next Saturday. Win that, and the bowl is in sight. Then we'll talk about the other game on the schedule. Beat Rice, and Go Army.

articles.title: East Carolina vs Army: Receiver Jason Dickerson Throws the Only Touchdown as the Pirates Win a 10-6 Slugfest
articles.byline: Bartholomew 'Bart' Quidley, The East Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: East Carolina Pirates (7-4) 10, Army Black Knights (5-5) 6, Sat., Nov. 21, Michie Stadium, West Point. Next: vs Florida Atlantic, Sat., Nov. 28, 1:00 PM ET, Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium, Greenville
articles.text:
Ugly? Sure. Beautiful? Absolutely. East Carolina went to West Point on Saturday, slugged it out for 60 minutes, and walked out with a 10-6 win on a trick play I'll be drawing on napkins for a month.

Here's the play. Fourth quarter, down 6-3, about four and a half minutes left. The ball goes to wide receiver Jason Dickerson, and instead of running, he pulls up to throw. Army nearly sacks him. He slips it, looks up, and Landon Sides is standing all alone in the end zone. Seven yards, touchdown, Pirates. Dickerson is 1 for 1 for his career as far as I'm concerned, and he can keep that record forever.

Then the defense finished it. Army drove to our 31 on its last possession, went for it on fourth down, and our secondary jumped the throw and intercepted Cale Hellums. Ballgame. I may have scared the neighbors.

Let's talk about that defense, because it deserves the headline as much as Dickerson does. Army came in with the country's No. 2 rushing attack, putting up 324.7 yards a game on the ground. We held them to 180. Hellums, who does it all for them, finished with 65 yards throwing and 62 running. DJ Johnson Jr. made 10 tackles with two for loss. Crews Law and Kamaurri McKinley also had 10 stops apiece. Army went 3 of 13 on third down. That's discipline, folks. Every guy did his job against that offense, snap after snap.

TJ Engleman Jr. carried the load on offense with 113 yards on 22 carries. Emory Williams went 15 of 23 for 130 yards, and Sides caught seven balls for 74. A third-quarter field goal tied it at 3 and kept us in it until the magic happened.

We're 7-4 and 5-2 in the American, already bowl eligible, and headed for a third straight bowl for the first time since the 2012-2014 run. That's a program that knows how to win close ones.

Florida Atlantic comes to Dowdy-Ficklen next Saturday for the finale. Fill the stands in purple and gold and send these seniors out the right way. Go Pirates, and arrgh.

articles.title: Purdue vs Wisconsin: Charles Correa Makes 15 Tackles as the Boilermakers Fall 42-10 at Ross-Ade
articles.matchup: Final: Wisconsin Badgers (7-4) 42, Purdue Boilermakers (3-8) 10, Sat., Nov. 21, Ross-Ade Stadium, West Lafayette. Next: at Indiana, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Memorial Stadium (Bloomington, IN), Bloomington
articles.text:
Saturday at Ross-Ade was the kind of afternoon that makes you check the calendar to see how many days until spring practice. The scoreboard said Badgers 42, Boilermakers 10, and Wisconsin ran for 381 yards doing it. We're 3-8.

Coach Barry Odom didn't sugarcoat it, and I'm not going to either. He said we didn't play on their side of the ball, didn't tackle well, and were really bad against the quarterback run game we knew was coming. Then he said it sounds like excuses, but the coaches have to coach better and the players have to execute better. I appreciate a head coach who says it straight.

Colton Joseph ran for 187 yards. Darrion Dupree ran for 125. They led 14-0 before we had a first down. That's the story, and there isn't a rewrite button.

But I'm a Boilermaker, which means I look for the good stuff. Jacobo Echeverria Lozano opened the second quarter with a career-long 53-yard field goal. That's a big-boy kick. Fame Ijeboi powered in from a yard out to cut it to 21-10 at halftime, and for a little while it felt like a game. Ijeboi finished with 40 yards on 10 carries.

Charles Correa was a tackling machine with 15 stops and a tackle for loss. Emoni Smith made 11 and John Slaughter made 10 with one in the backfield. Those guys were on the field for 35-plus minutes and never stopped running to the ball.

Ryan Browne went 13 of 32 for 133 yards, and Cooper McCutchan caught three for 36 with a 24-yard grab. It wasn't a day for the offense, and nobody needs me to explain that.

The Wisconsin streak in this series is now 19 games. Odom was still in college the last time we beat the Badgers at home. Somebody has to end that thing, and I'd love for it to be this staff.

But first, the only game that matters to a lot of us: Indiana in Bloomington next Saturday night. The Old Oaken Bucket. Throw out the record, throw out the five-game skid, and go win the Bucket. Boiler Up.

articles.title: Wisconsin vs Purdue: Colton Joseph Runs for 187, Catches a Score, and the Badgers Pile Up 381 Rushing Yards in a 42-10 Rout
articles.matchup: Final: Wisconsin Badgers (7-4) 42, Purdue Boilermakers (3-8) 10, Sat., Nov. 21, Ross-Ade Stadium, West Lafayette. Next: vs Minnesota, Fri., Nov. 27, 7:30 PM ET, Camp Randall Stadium, Madison
articles.text:
Three hundred eighty-one rushing yards. That's not a typo. It's the most this program has run for in a game since October 2021. That's the Badgers on Saturday at Ross-Ade Stadium, mashing Purdue 42-10 and running the ball like we're supposed to run the ball. Finally.

And the man in the middle of it was Colton Joseph. He waited two weeks to get his starting job back, and when he got it, he went off. Sixteen carries, 187 yards, a 32-yard score in the first quarter and a 66-yarder in the fourth that sent half of West Lafayette to the parking lot. He went 12 of 18 throwing. He threw the lead block on Eugene Hilton Jr.'s 24-yard touchdown run to start the scoring.

Oh, and he caught a touchdown too. Hilton took a handoff, pulled up and threw it to Joseph for 13 yards in the fourth quarter. First touchdown catch of Joseph's career, first touchdown throw of Hilton's. Coach Luke Fickell said there aren't enough words to say how proud he is of Joseph. I've got a few: tough, smart, fun to watch.

Darrion Dupree ran 16 times for 125 yards and two scores, including a 49-yarder two plays after Purdue's field goal. That made it 21-3, and that was that. We had a quarterback, a running back and a receiver all run for scores, something this program hadn't done since 2009 at Hawaii.

The defense was nasty. Purdue went 13 of 34 throwing and ran for 66 yards, period. We led 14-0 before they even had a first down. Eric Fletcher Jr. came away with an interception, and we never gave the ball away. Twelve of 16 on third down, 35:42 of possession. That's Badger football.

That's 19 straight wins against Purdue, the longest active streak in the Big Ten. We haven't lost to them since 2003 and haven't lost in West Lafayette since 1997. And a week after a loss I'd rather not discuss, we're 7-4, 5-3 in the league, with our first winning record since 2023 clinched.

Now the big one. Minnesota comes to Camp Randall on Friday night, and Paul Bunyan's Axe is at stake. Fill the place, jump around, and keep that Axe in Madison. On Wisconsin.

I've got a few: tough, smart, fun to watch.

Darrion Dupree ran 16 times for 125 yards and two scores, including a 49-yarder two plays after Purdue's field goal. That made it 21-3, and that was that. We had a quarterback, a running back and a receiver all run for scores, something this program hadn't done since 2009 at Hawaii.

The defense was nasty. Purdue went 13 of 34 throwing and ran for 66 yards, period. We led 14-0 before they even had a first down. Eric Fletcher Jr. came away with an interception, and we never gave the ball away. Twelve of 16 on third down, 35:42 of possession. That's Badger football.

That's 19 straight wins against Purdue, the longest active streak in the Big Ten. We haven't lost to them since 2003 and haven't lost in West Lafayette since 1997. And a week after a loss I'd rather not discuss, we're 7-4, 5-3 in the league, with our first winning record since 2023 clinched.
Now the big one. Minnesota comes to Camp Randall on Friday night, and Paul Bunyan's Axe is at stake. Fill the place, jump around, and keep that Axe in Madison. On Wisconsin.

Colton Joseph ran for 187 yards and two touchdowns and caught a 13-yard scoring throw from Eugene Hilton Jr.
Wisconsin ran for 381 yards, and Darrion Dupree added 125 yards and two scores.
Purdue knew we were going to run it. They just couldn't do anything about it, for the 19th year running.

articles.title: Northwestern vs Minnesota: Nicco Marchiol Ties It With 27 Seconds Left, but a Last-Second Kick Drops the Cats 20-17
articles.matchup: Final: Minnesota Golden Gophers (6-5) 20, Northwestern Wildcats (6-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis. Next: vs Illinois, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:30 PM ET, Ryan Field, Evanston
articles.text:
Twenty-seven seconds. That's how long Northwestern got to enjoy one of the gutsiest drives of the season before Minnesota kicked a field goal at the gun in Minneapolis. Final from Huntington Bank Stadium: 20-17, Gophers. It's going to take me a while.

That drive, though. Down 17-10 with about three minutes left, Nicco Marchiol marched us 71 yards. Third straight start for the guy, filling in for an injured Aidan Chiles, and he played like he'd been the starter since August. He finished it himself, scrambling 7 yards into the end zone to tie it. Jackson Kleather's kick made it 17-all, and I was already planning overtime snacks.

Then one throw beat us. Drake Lindsey found a receiver along the left sideline for 34 yards, and their kicker, who'd missed twice into the wind in the first half, hit from 44 at the horn.

It hurts more because of how well we hung in. The first half was a field-position slugfest, and a Minnesota punt pinned us at our own 2 late in the second quarter. We converted two third downs to get out, and then Marchiol beat a blitz and hit Griffin Wilde in stride for a 49-yard score and a 7-0 halftime lead. That's a 98-yard drive, folks. Ninety-eight!

Caleb Komolafe ran hard, 19 carries for 109 yards. Marchiol went 13 of 23 for 169 yards, and Luke Dehnicke caught three for 66. As a team we ran for 196 yards. Robert Fitzgerald led the defense with nine tackles, and Braden Turner made eight with a tackle for loss.

The one that got us was a strip-sack in the third. Minnesota recovered at our 33 and scored five plays later. One play, seven points, and that was the difference until the end.

We're 6-5, and that's four losses in a row now. I know, I know. But this team is already bowl eligible and nobody in Evanston is quitting.

Illinois comes to Ryan Field next Saturday. Beat the Illini, end the skid, and send the seniors out with something to smile about. Go Cats.

articles.title: Minnesota vs Northwestern: Luke Drzewiecki Drills a 44-Yarder at the Gun, Gophers Go Bowling 20-17
articles.matchup: Final: Minnesota Golden Gophers (6-5) 20, Northwestern Wildcats (6-5) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis. Next: at Wisconsin, Fri., Nov. 27, 7:30 PM ET, Camp Randall Stadium, Madison
articles.text:
He missed from 48. He missed from 53. Both into the wind at the open west end of Huntington Bank Stadium. And with the clock hitting zero, Luke Drzewiecki stepped up for a 44-yarder into that same wind and split the uprights. Gophers 20, Wildcats 17, and we are bowl eligible.

That's the second time this season the man has won a game at the final gun. He beat Iowa with a 46-yarder in October. Afterward he said all he wanted was the opportunity, and that everybody knew the next one was going in. Ice in the veins, Minnesota style.

Let's rewind 27 seconds. Northwestern had just tied it at 17 on a Nicco Marchiol scramble. Plenty of teams take a knee there. Not us. Drake Lindsey read the safety, saw the space, and hit Noah Jennings along the left sideline for 34 yards to the Northwestern 29. Then Drzewiecki trotted out.

Lindsey was sharp all day: 23 completions for 224 yards and two scores. Down 7-0 out of halftime, Coach P.J. Fleck went for it on fourth-and-3 at the Northwestern 9, and Lindsey found Jennings across the back of the end zone to tie it. Fleck said it was the right call, and it worked. Then Anthony Smith sacked Marchiol, forced a fumble, and recovered it himself. Five plays later Lindsey hit Jalen Smith from 14 yards out for the lead.

Darius Taylor ran for a season-high 108 yards on 15 carries. TJ Thomas added 61. We ran for 155 and gained 379 yards, our best numbers in both since September against Akron. Tight ends coach Eric Koehler is calling the plays now, and the offense looked alive.

Maverick Baranowski led the defense with 10 tackles. We had zero turnovers and were flagged only twice.

We're 6-5 and 4-4 in the Big Ten. That's bowl eligibility for the eighth time in Fleck's 10 seasons, after a rough week and a three-game skid. Fleck said he never takes winning for granted. Neither do I.

Next stop is Madison on Friday night, and the Axe is up for grabs. Bring it home where it belongs. Ski-U-Mah.

articles.title: Syracuse vs Boston College: Umari Hatcher Catches 11 for 212, but Red-Zone Misses Cost the Orange 27-15
articles.matchup: Final: Boston College Eagles (5-6) 27, Syracuse Orange (5-6) 15, Sat., Nov. 21, Alumni Stadium (Chestnut Hill, MA), Chestnut Hill. Next: vs Notre Dame, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, JMA Wireless Dome, Syracuse
articles.text:
Five hundred and thirty yards. Twenty-eight first downs. No turnovers. And somehow the scoreboard at Alumni Stadium read BC 27, Syracuse 15 when it was all done. Explain that one to me, because I've been staring at the box score for an hour.

Here's the explanation, and it hurts. We got deep into Boston College territory four times and didn't score a single touchdown on those trips. Tripp Woody went 3 for 4 on field goals, from 24, 50 and 24. Coach Fran Brown said it plain: we're getting down there, we've got to capitalize. Field goals don't win road games in late November.

Then there's Steve Angeli. The guy who led late comebacks against SMU and NC State took a hard hit from Demetrius Ballard, a roughing-the-passer flag on BC, and left the game. He was down on the turf for a while and later stood on the sideline with his throwing arm in a sling. He'd gone 13 of 21 for 164 yards before that. Get well, Steve. This team needs you.

Malachi Nelson came in and battled. He went 12 of 26 for 202 yards and hit Umari Hatcher for a 27-yard score early in the fourth to cut it to 20-15. Hatcher was unreal all day: 11 catches, 212 yards. Calvin Russell III caught eight for 107. Those two were open all afternoon.

The run defense is where it slipped. Bo MacCormack III, a guy who once committed to us, ran for 236 yards, including a 56-yard score in the third when we were down only 13-9. That one stung twice.

Chris D'Appolonia was a bright spot with 11 tackles and 3.5 tackles for loss. Braheem Long Jr. and Chris Peal each made nine stops.

We're 5-6, and this loss cost us a chance to clinch a bowl. One chance left, and it's a big one: Notre Dame comes to the JMA Wireless Dome next Saturday at noon. Pack the Dome, stand behind this team, and let's go Orange.

BC needed one guy with 30 carries to beat us. We needed a finisher in the red zone and never found one.

articles.title: Boston College vs Syracuse: Bo MacCormack III Runs for 236 Against the School He Spurned, Eagles Win 27-15
articles.byline: Siobhan Dunleavy, The Boston College Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Boston College Eagles (5-6) 27, Syracuse Orange (5-6) 15, Sat., Nov. 21, Alumni Stadium (Chestnut Hill, MA), Chestnut Hill. Next: at Miami, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
Bo MacCormack III once committed to Syracuse. Then he flipped to Boston College in November of his senior year of high school. On Saturday, on senior day at Alumni Stadium, he ran for 236 yards against the Orange, and the Eagles won 27-15. Best call that kid ever made, if you ask me.

Thirty carries. Two hundred thirty-six yards. And the dagger came in the third quarter, with us clinging to a 13-9 lead, when Bo split the middle and went 56 yards with three Orange defenders chasing his jersey. Coach Bill O'Brien said Bo is what this place is all about, one of the most improved guys on the team. You won't get an argument from me.

Mason McKenzie was steady. He went 14 of 24 for 131 yards and two scores without a turnover. He rolled left on our opening drive, an 81-yard march, and flipped a touchdown to tight end Zeke Moore. In the fourth, he found Nedrick Boldin Jr. from 22 yards out to make it 27-15. Luca Lombardo drilled field goals from 46 and 32, the second one at the halftime gun.

Our defense did what it had to. Syracuse threw for 406 yards and got deep into our end again and again, and we kept them to field goals. Charlie Comella had nine tackles and two for loss. Marcus Upton added 1.5 tackles for loss and broke up two throws. Zero turnovers on our side, too.

Comella wore No. 31 on Saturday, the jersey BC hands out every senior day in memory of Jay McGillis, the defensive back who died of leukemia in 1992 at age 21. That's the kind of thing that makes this place special, and Comella honored it.

We snapped a three-game skid after a rough day at Notre Dame last week. We're 5-6 and 3-5 in the ACC. Bowl hopes are still alive, barely.

One more to get there: a trip to Miami next Saturday at noon. It'll take a big upset in Hard Rock Stadium. Bo, start stretching now. Ever to Excel, Eagles.

articles.title: Colorado vs Cincinnati: Isaac Wilson Throws for 312 and Three Scores, Buffs Fall 35-28 After a Travel Nightmare
articles.matchup: Final: Cincinnati Bearcats (6-5) 35, Colorado Buffaloes (4-7) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati. Next: vs UCF, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Folsom Field, Boulder
articles.text:
Our bus broke down on the way to the airport. Then the flights got delayed. Then we didn't land in Cincinnati until late Friday. And then, on Saturday, we coughed up the ball four times and lost 35-28. That's the whole week in four sentences, Buffs fans.

Coach Deion Sanders didn't make excuses. He said early in the game we were still on the tarmac, and that the early turnovers crippled us. Then he said all of it's on him. I respect that. I also respect my blood pressure, which is a mess.

Here's what kills me. Cincinnati intercepted us on our opening drive and recovered a fumble on the next one, and we were down 14-0 before we'd blinked. You can't spot a bowl-hungry home team two touchdowns in a building like Nippert.

But this team swung back. Isaac Wilson hit Ernest Campbell for 36 yards on fourth-and-1 to get us on the board. Richard Young plowed in from 4 to tie it at 14 late in the half. Then in the third, Wilson went big. A 54-yarder to DeAndre Moore Jr. And then a deep ball down the right sideline to Joseph Williams, who made a one-handed grab near the 40 and outran everybody for a 70-yard score. That might be the catch of the year in Boulder, and it came in Ohio.

Wilson finished with 312 yards and three touchdowns. Williams had four catches for 112. Moore caught five for 91.

Defensively, Randon Fontenette was a one-man wrecking crew: 14 tackles, a sack, and 2.5 stops in the backfield. Liona Lefau added 10 stops and a sack. The trouble was Cole Tabb, who did a little of everything, and those screens. Sanders said it himself: they knew it was coming and still couldn't stop it.

We're 4-7. No bowl again, and that's a gut punch for a program that expected more. Sanders said there's no true consistency, and he's right.

UCF comes to Folsom Field next Saturday for the finale. Send the seniors off right, play a clean four quarters for once, and make Boulder loud. Sko Buffs.

articles.title: Cincinnati vs Colorado: Cole Tabb Makes Program History With 100 and 100, Bearcats Go Bowling After 35-28 Win
articles.matchup: Final: Cincinnati Bearcats (6-5) 35, Colorado Buffaloes (4-7) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati. Next: at BYU, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo
articles.text:
A hundred yards rushing and a hundred yards receiving in the same game. No Bearcat had ever done it. Cole Tabb did it Saturday at Nippert, and Cincinnati beat Colorado 35-28 to snap a three-game skid and punch a bowl ticket. We're 6-5. Breathe, everybody.

Tabb was everywhere. He carried 23 times for 120 yards and two scores, then caught seven balls for 110 yards and two more. The 22-yard grab right before halftime gave us a 21-14 lead, and the 50-yard screen in the third made it 35-21. Even Deion Sanders admitted afterward that those screens hurt. Coach Scott Satterfield called Tabb a special talent who can block, catch and run. He also cleared 1,000 rushing yards for the season, the eighth Bearcat since 2000 to get there.

JC French IV might have had the quietest great day in the country. He completed 18 of 19 throws for 208 yards and two scores, and ran one in from a yard out. Eighteen of 19! I've seen guys miss more than that playing catch in the backyard.

The defense set the tone right away. MJ Cannon picked off Colorado on its opening drive, Tabb scored a few plays later, and a Buffs fumble set up French for a 14-0 lead. Damaine Wilson got home for a sack and made two stops in the backfield, and Jonathan Thompson broke up two throws.

I won't lie, the third quarter was a track meet, and Colorado hit us for a couple of long ones. But in the fourth, nobody scored, and that's on our guys holding firm. Kenny Worthy sealed it with an interception on fourth down with 33 seconds left. I screamed so loud the dog left the room.

Fifty-four runs. Thirty-six minutes of possession. Ten of 15 on third down. That's how you close out a game when the other team has big-play guys.

And let's be honest about November. We were 2-13 in this month since joining the Big 12 before Saturday. That number had been hanging around our necks. One down.

Next up, the trip to Provo to face BYU. Bowl eligible, playing loose, nothing to lose. Bring it on. Go Bearcats!

Fifty-four runs. Thirty-six minutes of possession. Ten of 15 on third down. That's how you close out a game when the other team has big-play guys.
And let's be honest about November. We were 2-13 in this month since joining the Big 12 before Saturday. That number had been hanging around our necks. One down.
Next up, the trip to Provo to face BYU. Bowl eligible, playing loose, nothing to lose. Bring it on. Go Bearcats!

Cole Tabb ran for 120 yards and two scores and caught seven balls for 110 yards and two more, a first in program history.
JC French IV completed 18 of 19 throws for 208 yards and two scores and ran for another.

articles.title: Ole Miss vs Wofford: Trinidad Chambliss Goes 19 of 20 With Five Scores in a 59-17 Rout
articles.byline: Langston Fairbanks, The Ole Miss Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Ole Miss Rebels (7-4) 59, Wofford Terriers (5-7) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford. Next: vs Mississippi State, Fri., Nov. 27, 12:00 PM ET, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford
articles.text:
Nineteen of 20. Read that slowly. Trinidad Chambliss threw 20 balls on Saturday in Oxford and 19 of them were caught by a Rebel. Five went for touchdowns. Ole Miss 59, Wofford 17, and it was 49-3 at halftime.

After back-to-back losses to Georgia and Oklahoma, coach Pete Golding said this team had a chance to feel sorry for itself. Instead it came out swinging. We had three touchdowns on our first 11 plays and led 21-0 with 7:15 still left in the first quarter. We scored on the opening drive for the first time since Week 2. Took 65 seconds.

Chambliss finished with 367 yards. He hit Luke Hasz from 7 and 15, Deuce Alexander from 18, Caleb Odom from 41 and Joshua Dye from 43. Alexander ended up with five catches for 128 yards and two scores. Odom caught three for 110, including a 55-yarder on the first drive where he stumbled, steadied himself off the defender and kept going. Tight ends, man. We've got a couple of good ones.

Then the kid came in. Deuce Knight went 5 of 6 for 107 yards, found Alexander for a 70-yard score, and ran 20 yards for another. Walker Howard hit Caleb Cunningham for 26 more in the third. Lucas Carneiro was 8 for 8 on extra points and kicked a 28-yard field goal for good measure.

Seven hundred eighty-nine yards of offense. Thirty-four first downs. We were 8 of 10 on third down. And we did it with two starting offensive linemen and our top two running backs sitting out. JT Lindsey stepped in and carried 18 times for 62 yards.

On defense, Jonathan Maldonado had a sack and 2.5 tackles for loss, and Suntarine Perkins got home too. Wofford got a long touchdown throw and a 91-yard fumble return once the reserves were in. Fine. That's what reserves are for.

The best part of the day was Chambliss talking about how emotional he's been since the Oklahoma game, soaking in his last days in Oxford. Give that man a standing ovation every time he walks through the Grove.

We're 7-4. Mississippi State comes to Vaught-Hemingway on Friday for the Egg Bowl. Win the trophy, keep the bragging rights, and Hotty Toddy, everybody.

articles.title: Vanderbilt vs Florida: Brock Taylor Goes 4 for 4 From Deep, but a Fluky Bounce Sinks the Commodores 34-27
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Gators (7-4) 34, Vanderbilt Commodores (4-7) 27, Sat., Nov. 21, Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville. Next: vs Tennessee, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, FirstBank Stadium, Nashville
articles.text:
For one half in Gainesville on Saturday, the Commodores had a Swamp crowd of 88,025 booing its own team. That's what I'll remember, even after the final read Gators 34, Vandy 27.

We led 24-17 at halftime, and we earned it. Brock Taylor drilled field goals from 53, 52 and 42 yards in the first half. That's three kicks most teams wouldn't even try. Then Jared Curtis went to work: a 9-yard touchdown throw to Sedrick Alexander, a two-point conversion to Cole Spence, and with 39 seconds left before the break, a 75-yard bomb to Junior Sherrill. Florida's crowd let its team have it.

So what happened? A few things, and none of them easy to swallow. Early in the third, Curtis picked up a fourth-and-1 at our 36, but his helmet came off on the run, and the officials reversed it and ruled him short. Florida took the short field and tied it. Then, with the game tied at 27, a Gator throw sailed high, got tipped, and dropped right into a receiver's arms for 37 yards. They scored the winner a few plays later.

Coach Clark Lea said we left too many plays on the field, and he's right. But I won't let one bounce erase what these guys did.

Taylor finished 4 for 4, adding a 51-yarder to tie it at 27 in the fourth. Sherrill caught six balls for 149 yards. Alexander ran for 129 yards on 15 carries with a 51-yard burst. CJ Heard made 11 tackles and played like a man who didn't want his senior year to end. Curtis hurt his left wrist late and came back anyway to give us one more chance. A fourth-down sack at the Florida 45 ended it.

We're 4-7, 1-7 in the league. No bowl this year, the first time we've missed one since 2023, and that hurts. But Curtis is the future, and Saturdays like this show what he can be.

One game left, and it's the one everybody in Nashville circles: Tennessee at FirstBank Stadium. Let's send Sherrill and Heard out with a win against the Vols. Anchor Down.

articles.title: Florida vs Vanderbilt: A Tipped Ball, Jadan Baugh's Late Run and a 34-27 Win in the Swamp
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Gators (7-4) 34, Vanderbilt Commodores (4-7) 27, Sat., Nov. 21, Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville. Next: at Florida State, Fri., Nov. 27, 3:30 PM ET, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee
articles.text:
Sometimes football hands you a gift, and a real Gator fan says thank you and asks for another. Florida 34, Vanderbilt 27 in the Swamp on Saturday, and coach Jon Sumrall said it perfectly afterward: he'll take all the luck he can get. Me too, Coach. Me too.

Here's the play that'll be on loop in Gainesville all week. Fourth quarter, tied at 27, third-and-5. Aaron Philo throws high for Micah Mays, the ball ricochets, and Eric Singleton Jr. snatches it out of the air for a 37-yard gain. Philo was on the ground and didn't even see it. A roughing call on Vandy pushed us closer, and Jadan Baugh took a direct snap out of the wildcat and ran 10 yards for the go-ahead score with 2:18 to play.

Then Jayden Woods spun past a blocker and sacked Jared Curtis on fourth down at our 45. Ballgame. I may have hugged a stranger.

Let's not pretend the first half was fun. Brock Taylor kept booting field goals from the parking lot, and Vandy hit a 75-yard bomb right before the break to lead 24-17. The Swamp let the team hear about it on the way to the locker room. Fair enough.

The second half was a different team. Philo went 20 of 26 for 241 yards and ran for 73 yards and both of his scores, the second tying it at 24. Singleton finished with a career-high 117 yards on six catches. Patrick Durkin was 2 for 2 on field goals, including the 20-yarder that put us up 27-24. We converted 11 of 16 third downs, which is how you win a grinder.

And how about Myles Graham? Ten tackles and a 57-yard fumble return for a touchdown in the second quarter. That's a football player. Alfonzo Allen Jr. added a sack, and Cam Dooley chipped in eight tackles.

We're 7-4, 5-4 in the SEC. That's our first winning conference record since 2020 and back-to-back wins for the first time since September. Progress, people.

Now the one that matters most. Friday in Tallahassee against Florida State. Bring every ounce of that fourth-quarter fight, Gators, and bring a little more luck too. Go Gators, and chomp them.

articles.title: Ohio State vs Nebraska: Jeremiah Smith Goes for 165 and Two Scores, but the Buckeyes Fall 31-28 in Lincoln
articles.byline: Brecken 'Buck' Holloway, The Ohio State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Nebraska Cornhuskers (7-4) 31, Ohio State Buckeyes (7-4) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, Memorial Stadium (Lincoln, NE), Lincoln. Next: vs Michigan, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Ohio Stadium, Columbus
articles.text:
Some losses make you yell. This one made me sit in my truck in the driveway for 20 minutes without turning the key. Nebraska 31, Ohio State 28. We're 7-4, and I'm not sure what to do with my hands.

Here's the gut punch, in plain numbers. That's our third loss to an unranked team this season, and the last time that happened was 2011. We had won eight straight against the Huskers. Gone.

We got pushed around. There's no other way to say it. Seventy-six rushing yards. Nebraska held the ball for more than 35 minutes and converted 10 of 16 third downs. When the other team moves the chains on fourth-and-1 in the fourth quarter of a tie game and you can't stop it, that's a problem with the whole operation, not one guy.

Now let me talk about the one guy who was unstoppable. Jeremiah Smith caught six balls for 165 yards and two touchdowns, a 67-yarder on our first drive and a 31-yarder just before halftime. Luke Fahey went 16 of 27 for 259 yards. Every time Smith touched the ball, I thought we were fine. We should have fed him 20 more times.

The second half started right. A 14-play, 76-yard march, capped by Bo Jackson from a yard out, tied it 21-21. Then the fourth quarter fell apart: a punt return set up a Nebraska field goal, then a ball meant for Smith got batted up and intercepted, and the Huskers turned that into a 10-point lead. Jackson scored again with 3:52 left, and we never got the ball back with a real chance.

Jaylen McClain and Earl Little Jr. made eight tackles apiece. Connor Hawkins was perfect on four kicks. Small comfort.

Center Carson Hinzman said it best afterward: it's hard to choke down a season like this, but there's one more game, and it's the most important one of the year.

He's right. Michigan comes to Columbus next Saturday at noon. Every bit of this hurt should be pointed straight at that team up north. Beat Michigan. Nothing else matters now.

articles.title: Nebraska vs Ohio State: Anthony Colandrea Throws Three Scores, Huskers End the Top 25 Drought 31-28
articles.matchup: Final: Nebraska Cornhuskers (7-4) 31, Ohio State Buckeyes (7-4) 28, Sat., Nov. 21, Memorial Stadium (Lincoln, NE), Lincoln. Next: at Iowa, Fri., Nov. 27, 12:00 PM ET, Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City
articles.text:
Thirty-one games. That's how many times in a row Nebraska had lost to an AP Top 25 team. Done. Finished. Buried. Nebraska 31, No. 16 Ohio State 28, on senior day, on a misty afternoon at Memorial Stadium, and when Anthony Colandrea took that last knee, the whole state poured onto the field.

I was one of them. I'm not ashamed. The last time we beat a ranked team was Oregon, 35-32, back in September of 2016. I've waited a long time to say this: we beat Ohio State.

And we didn't sneak it. Coach Matt Rhule said it after: no tricks, no crazy game plan, we played our style of football. We ran it 45 times. We held the ball for 35:05. We went 10 of 16 on third down and committed zero turnovers. The Buckeyes managed 76 rushing yards all day. That's a whipping at the point of attack, and it was beautiful.

Colandrea was the man. He went 19 of 28 for 200 yards and three scores, hit Luke Lindenmeyer from 11 and Kwazi Gilmer from 7, and ran for 63 yards and a 13-yard touchdown of his own. Gilmer caught seven balls. Jamal Rule carried 23 times and moved the sticks on a huge fourth-and-1.

Here's the sequence I'll be telling my grandkids about. Tied 21-21 to open the fourth, Jacory Barney Jr. returned a punt 21 yards to set up John Hohl's 33-yard field goal. Then Jamir Conn broke up a ball meant for Jeremiah Smith, it popped up, and Victor Evans III came down with it. Five plays after Rule's fourth-down push, Colandrea found Quinn Clark from 26 yards out. Ten-point lead.

Ohio State scored late, and sure, my stomach dropped to my shoes. This team had blown fourth-quarter leads to Indiana, Oregon and Washington. Not this time. Colandrea ran for one first down, then another, and the clock did the rest.

Smith is a monster, six catches for 165 yards and two scores. Didn't matter. Cameron Lenhardt got a sack, Dexter Foster made eight tackles, and the defense bent without breaking.

We're 7-4. Iowa on Friday at Kinnick. One more, Huskers. GBR, forever.

articles.title: Georgia Tech vs Wake Forest: Grady Adamson Runs for 143, but a 29-0 Hole Sinks the Jackets 50-29
articles.byline: Wendell Quist, The Georgia Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Wake Forest Demon Deacons (10-1) 50, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (3-8) 29, Sat., Nov. 21, Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta. Next: at Georgia, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Sanford Stadium, Athens
articles.text:
Bobby Dodd Stadium had 45,296 people in it on Saturday, and for about 20 minutes most of them were glaring at the scoreboard like it owed them money. The final was 50-29, Wake. We're 3-8.

The start was brutal, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Wake scored on its first four drives and led 29-0 early in the second quarter. By halftime it was 36-7. Gio Lopez had all day, Carlos Hernandez was running free, and we coughed up the ball three times on the afternoon. You can't do that against a team headed to the ACC title game.

But I'm going to tell you what I saw after that, because it matters. This team won the second half 22-14. Nobody quit. Grady Adamson, one half of our two-quarterback plan, ran wild, 143 yards on 16 carries with a 43-yard burst and a 12-yard touchdown. He also went 6 of 8 throwing. That kid plays with his hair on fire.

Justice Haynes scored from 4 yards out for our first points and then ran in a two-point try. Trelain Maddox ran for 79 yards and a score. Graham Knowles punched in a 7-yarder late. As a team we piled up 289 rushing yards at 6.7 a carry and 26 first downs. That's real football, folks, even on a day when the scoreboard disagreed.

Cayman Spaulding made 11 tackles and never stopped chasing. E.J. Lightsey had a tackle for loss. Aidan Birr was perfect on three extra points.

Look, a week ago we were running through Death Valley and beating Clemson. This week a top-10 team showed us how far we still have to climb. Both things are true. The Jackets are building something, and Saturdays like this are part of the bill.

Now comes the big one: a trip to Athens to face No. 1 Georgia in the regular-season finale. Nobody gives us a prayer, which is exactly how I like it. Beat the Dawgs, and Go Jackets.

But I'm going to tell you what I saw after that, because it matters. This team won the second half 22-14. Nobody quit. Grady Adamson, one half of our two-quarterback plan, ran wild, 143 yards on 16 carries with a 43-yard burst and a 12-yard touchdown. He also went 6 of 8 throwing. That kid plays with his hair on fire.

Justice Haynes scored from 4 yards out for our first points and then ran in a two-point try. Trelain Maddox ran for 79 yards and a score. Graham Knowles punched in a 7-yarder late. As a team we piled up 289 rushing yards at 6.7 a carry and 26 first downs. That's real football, folks, even on a day when the scoreboard disagreed.
Cayman Spaulding made 11 tackles and never stopped chasing. E.J. Lightsey had a tackle for loss. Aidan Birr was perfect on three extra points.

Look, a week ago we were running through Death Valley and beating Clemson. This week a top-10 team showed us how far we still have to climb. Both things are true. The Jackets are building something, and Saturdays like this are part of the bill.
Now comes the big one: a trip to Athens to face No. 1 Georgia in the regular-season finale. Nobody gives us a prayer, which is exactly how I like it. Beat the Dawgs, and Go Jackets.

articles.title: Wake Forest vs Georgia Tech: Gio Lopez Accounts for Four Scores, Deacs Roll 50-29 Into the ACC Title Game
articles.byline: Eloise Brightman-Rowe, The Wake Forest Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Wake Forest Demon Deacons (10-1) 50, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (3-8) 29, Sat., Nov. 21, Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta. Next: vs Duke, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, Winston-Salem
articles.text:
Clear your calendar for championship weekend, Deacon nation. The Deacs hung 50 on Georgia Tech in a 50-29 rout on Saturday afternoon in Atlanta, and with Miami beating Virginia Tech, the Demon Deacons are headed to the ACC Championship Game. That's only the third time in program history. Read that again.

We're 10-1 and 7-1 in the league. That's the third double-digit win season this school has ever had, and the eight straight wins are the longest streak in program history. Somebody check on the record books, because they're getting a workout this fall.

The first half was a demolition. Touchdowns on our first four drives, 29-0 before Georgia Tech knew what hit them, and 36-7 at the break. Ty Clark III scored twice on the ground. Gio Lopez punched one in, then hit Jack Foley for a 66-yard strike to open the second quarter. In first halves across the last five games, we've outscored people 181-7. Those aren't football scores. Those are basketball scores with the other team forgetting to show up.

Lopez was surgical: 17 of 22 for 324 yards, two scores through the air and two on the ground. Carlos Hernandez caught eight balls for 145 yards, his fifth 100-yard game of the year. Deuce Lawrence ran for 105 yards and a score and added 81 more as a receiver. Dominick Barry got in on the fun with a 14-yard touchdown grab. Even Clark threw a 25-yard completion, because why not.

Six hundred and seven yards of offense. That's five straight games with 500 or more, the longest such run in the FBS this season. Coach Jake Dickert credited the big guys up front, and he's right. They're moving people.

Fine, the second half got sloppy, and we were flagged 12 times for 111 yards. I'll yell about that on Monday. Tonight I'm busy.

Dickert put it plainly afterward: don't undersell winning on the road. Nobody in Winston-Salem is underselling anything right now.

Duke comes to town next Saturday with a title-game ticket already in our pocket. Win that one and the whole country hears about this team. Go Deacs.

articles.title: Kansas vs BYU: Isaiah Marshall and the Jayhawks Take a Top-15 Team to Three Overtimes, Fall 31-29
articles.matchup: Final: BYU Cougars (9-2) 31, Kansas Jayhawks (4-7) 29, Sat., Nov. 21, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence. Next: at Oklahoma State, Sat., Nov. 28, 6:15 PM ET, Boone Pickens Stadium, Stillwater
articles.text:
I've been a Jayhawk long enough to know heartbreak has a home address, and on Saturday it moved into David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium for three overtimes. BYU 31, Kansas 29. We're 4-7, and I'm proud and miserable at the same time.

Proud first. Down 16-6 entering the fourth quarter against the 12th-ranked team in the country, this team refused to fold. Martin Connington booted a 26-yarder to cut it to a touchdown. Then, on fourth down with four minutes left, Isaiah Marshall threw a strike to Cam Pickett from 24 yards out to tie it. Our crowd of 30,121 made that place shake.

Then BYU missed a 37-yard field goal at the gun, and we got free football.

Marshall kept making plays. On a third-and-12 in the first overtime he took off for the first down, then sprinted in from 10 yards out. In the second overtime, facing fourth down again, he found Nahzae Cox for 20 yards to tie it at 29. The kid finished 20 of 28 for 186 yards and two scores, plus 90 rushing yards and another score. That's a quarterback, folks.

Connington was perfect, 3 for 3 on field goals. Keaton Kubecka caught six balls for 73 yards, and Pickett grabbed seven. On defense, Leroy Harris III and David Santiago each had a sack and two tackles for loss, and Corey Gordon made nine stops. We also stripped Bear Bachmeier before halftime and turned it into a 6-3 lead at the break.

Now the miserable part. Two interceptions hurt, and both turned into BYU points. Our two-point try in the second overtime didn't get in, and neither did our last try in the third. That's our fourth loss this year by a touchdown or less, and every one of them stings.

Coach Lance Leipold said these guys have no quit in them, and anyone who watched Saturday saw it with their own eyes. This senior class deserves a happy ending.

One more chance to give them one: a trip to Stillwater to face Oklahoma State next Saturday night. Give this senior class the goodbye it has earned. Rock Chalk.

articles.title: BYU vs Kansas: Bear Bachmeier Finds Jojo Phillips in the Third Overtime, Cougars Survive 31-29
articles.matchup: Final: BYU Cougars (9-2) 31, Kansas Jayhawks (4-7) 29, Sat., Nov. 21, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence. Next: vs Cincinnati, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo
articles.text:
Three overtimes in Lawrence. My heart rate is still somewhere back on I-70. Final: BYU 31, Kansas 29, and the Cougars are 9-2 with the playoff dream still alive.

It came down to one snap. Third overtime, both teams down to two-point tries, and Bear Bachmeier rolled around until he found Jojo Phillips in the back of the end zone. Then the Kansas try came up empty, and I let out a yell my neighbors will be talking about at church.

Let's be honest about how we got there. Regulation should have been ours. We led 16-6 going into the fourth after Bachmeier bulled in from 7 yards out, and the Jayhawks ripped off 10 straight points, the tying score coming on fourth down with four minutes left. Matthias Dunn then missed a 37-yarder as time ran out. Coach Kalani Sitake called it a mishit, and I'll leave it there, because Dunn also hit from 52, 36 and 26 and kept us alive all afternoon.

LJ Martin was the workhorse. Twenty-five carries, 127 yards and the touchdown that opened the second overtime. Bachmeier went 15 of 26 for 173 yards and ran for two scores, including the 2-yard answer in the first overtime after Kansas had punched first. Walker Lyons hauled in a 41-yarder, and Legend Glasker led the group with five grabs.

The defense deserves a statue. Cade Uluave piled up 10 tackles. Tausili Akana and Raider Damuni each came away with an interception off Isaiah Marshall, and the second one set up our first touchdown of the day. Jake Clifton had two tackles for loss. Kansas converted third downs and fourth downs all day, and our guys kept getting off the field when it counted most.

This was the first time in four tries that we beat the Jayhawks, and yes, I remember 2024 in Provo. Consider that one paid back, with interest and three extra periods.

Was it pretty? Not even close. Two lost fumbles, a missed kick at the gun and a whole lot of gray hair for this fan base. But Sitake said it best afterward: they just kept fighting back. So did we.

Cincinnati comes to Provo next Saturday for the regular-season finale. Bring the noise to LaVell Edwards Stadium, because a team chasing 10 wins deserves a full house. Rise and Shout.

articles.title: UTEP vs Air Force: Carlos Arreola's 42-Yard Field Goal the Lone Bright Spot in a 52-3 Loss
articles.matchup: Final: Air Force Falcons (9-2) 52, UTEP Miners (1-10) 3, Fri., Nov. 20, Falcon Stadium, USAF Academy. Next: at Northern Illinois, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Huskie Stadium, Dekalb
articles.text:
Mira, I'm not going to sugarcoat this one for my people in El Paso. Air Force 52, UTEP 3 on Friday night in Colorado, and that's as rough as it sounds. We're 1-10, 0-7 in conference. But a real Miner fan doesn't hide from a tough night, so let's go through it together.

First, the good. Down 14-0 early in the second quarter, our offense put together an 11-play, 51-yard drive, and Carlos Arreola drilled a 42-yard field goal to make it 14-3. That's a real kick at altitude, and I jumped off my couch like it was a touchdown. Arreola went 1 for 1, and I'm calling him the player of the game from our side.

Jayden Wilson was a warrior on defense with 12 tackles. Garrett Hawkins made seven with one for loss, and Justin Lee had six with a tackle for loss of his own. Those guys were on the field for almost 40 minutes, because Air Force held the ball for 39:46, and they kept battling.

Raymond Moore III went 13 of 19 for 89 yards, and Jaden Smith caught six balls for 30. Carver Cheeks had three catches for 34, with a long of 16. Bodey Weaver came in and completed his only throw.

Now the hard part. Air Force ran it 64 times for 429 yards, and that triple-option style is a nightmare to defend for 60 minutes. We lost a fumble on our first possession and threw an interception right before halftime, and both turned into Falcon touchdowns. We finished with 116 yards and six first downs. When the other team has 18 different guys carrying the ball, it's like trying to tackle fog.

This was our first game against the Falcons since 1995, back in the WAC days. Some reunions go better than others.

Here's the deal, Miners. Nobody in Sun City quits on this team. One game left, and these players deserve one more loud weekend of support.

Next up: at Northern Illinois, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 3:30 PM ET at Huskie Stadium in DeKalb. Let's go finish strong. Orange and blue forever. Go Miners!

articles.title: Air Force vs UTEP: 429 Rushing Yards, 18 Ball Carriers and a 52-3 Blowout
articles.byline: Lt. Col. (Ret.) Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, The Air Force Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Air Force Falcons (9-2) 52, UTEP Miners (1-10) 3, Fri., Nov. 20, Falcon Stadium, USAF Academy. Next: at New Mexico, Fri., Nov. 27, 4:30 PM ET, University Stadium (NM), Albuquerque
articles.text:
Mission debrief, Falcon fans: objective achieved. Final from Falcon Stadium on Friday night: Falcons 52, Miners 3, and the ground game flew in formation all night long. We're 9-2, 5-2 in the Mountain West, and I'd like to salute every single one of the 18 Falcons who carried the football.

Yes, 18. We ran it 64 times for 429 yards, 6.7 a pop. Rocco Conti led the way with 64 yards on just five carries, including a 33-yard burst. Evan Medders added 46, Oswaldo Morales ran for 38 and a 29-yard touchdown, and Gage LaDue punched in the first score from 3 yards out. Owen Allen scored from a yard out and Matt Long from 13. When everybody eats, everybody's happy.

And then there's the air raid, Academy style. We threw only six times and completed four. Three of those four went for touchdowns. Medders hit Adam Hrynciw for 31 yards in the first quarter and Jonah Dawson for 77 to open the second half, and Maguire Martin's one and only throw of the night was a 35-yard touchdown to Major Quin. Medders went 3 of 4 for 122 yards. That's not a box score, that's a magic trick.

The defense was flat-out mean. Alexander Perez forced a fumble on UTEP's first possession that set up a quick score, then grabbed an interception right before halftime that led to another touchdown. Connor Vasek had three sacks. UTEP finished with 116 yards, 24 of them on the ground, and six first downs. We had 27 first downs and held the ball for 39:46.

Carter Cremascoli was perfect on five extra points and added a 19-yard field goal, and Jacob Medina came on late and went 2 for 2. This was the first meeting with UTEP since 1995, back in our WAC days, and the overall series now stands at 15-1 with us 8-0 at home. Some traditions are worth keeping.

Nine wins with one regular-season game to go. That's a winning program, ladies and gentlemen.

Next up: at New Mexico, Friday, Nov. 27, at 4:30 PM ET at University Stadium in Albuquerque. One more mission. Fly, Fight, Win!

articles.title: Bowling Green vs Toledo: Five Sacks and a Fight, but No Points in the Glass Bowl, 19-0
articles.byline: Darcy Fenwick, The Bowling Green Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Toledo Rockets (9-2) 19, Bowling Green Falcons (3-8) 0, Fri., Nov. 20, Glass Bowl, Toledo. Next: vs Massachusetts, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Doyt L. Perry Stadium, Bowling Green
articles.text:
That was a long drive home up I-75. The Rockets blanked us 19-0 in Toledo on Friday night, and nobody in orange and brown wants to talk about the scoreboard. We're 3-8, 3-4 in the MAC. So let's talk about the defense instead, because those guys deserved a lot better.

Our defense sacked John Alan Richter five times. Five! Myles Bradley had two of them and three and a half tackles for loss, and he knocked the ball loose on one, though Richter got it back. Kal-El Pascal was a heat-seeking missile with 15 tackles, 10 of them solo. Toledo averaged 2.4 yards a carry, went 5 for 16 on third down, and the only touchdown we allowed came on a two-play drive in the last minute of the first half. Dorian Pringle added nine tackles.

The problem was that the other side of the ball never got going. Our very first play of the night, Nakai Amachree ran for 10 yards and had the ball knocked loose, and Toledo recovered. That's a rough way to say hello.

Our best chance to get on the board came early. In the second quarter we drove 51 yards in eight plays, and Austin Novosad had us knocking on the door. Then the 32-yard field goal didn't go through, and it was still 9-0. That one hurt. We got into Toledo territory again early in the fourth quarter, too, and came away empty on fourth down.

Novosad went 12 of 22 for 144 yards with no interceptions, and he hung in there while getting hit. Joseph Saffold made three catches for 60 yards, including a 29-yarder, and Eli Jacon-Duffy had a 28-yard grab. Amachree carried 19 times for 57 yards. But as a team we ran for 44 yards and converted just one of 12 third downs, and you can't win a rivalry game like that.

Toledo's Reice Griffith kicked four field goals. Tip of the cap. He was the difference.
