articles.title: Duke vs Clemson: Nate Sheppard's 55-Yard Burst Not Enough as the Blue Devils Fall, 20-10
articles.byline: Harrison Wexley-Moore IV, The Duke Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Clemson Tigers (7-4) 20, Duke Blue Devils (7-4) 10, Fri., Nov. 20, Wallace Wade Stadium, Durham. Next: at Wake Forest, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium, Winston-Salem
articles.text:
We had a drone show. We had a Heisman campaign. We had Nate Sheppard ripping off a 55-yard touchdown that made Wallace Wade Stadium shake. What we didn't have, sadly, was enough offense, and Clemson left Durham with a 20-10 win on Friday night. Duke is 7-4, 4-4 in the ACC.

First, our guy, because he deserves it. Sheppard came into the night leading the country in all-purpose yards, and he ran 19 times for 116 yards. The big one came in the third quarter, right after Clemson went up 10-0. He burst through the right side, dodged a diving tackle at the sideline, and was gone. 10-7, and the place came alive. Folks, that is a Heisman run, and I'll argue with anybody about it.

The defense gave us every chance. Andrew Pellicciotta was everywhere with 12 tackles, DaShawn Stone had eight and broke up two throws, and Kevin O'Connor made two tackles for loss. Evan Smith grabbed an interception in the first quarter, and we fell on a Clemson fumble in the second. Nobody scored until a Clemson field goal with 17 seconds left in the half, and our guys kept the Tigers out of the end zone for nearly 39 minutes.

The trouble was on our side of the ball. Walker Eget went 16 of 38 for 149 yards, and we went 6 for 16 on third down. Javen Nicholas did his part with six catches for 87 yards, and Jeremiah Hasley caught six for 55. After Clemson went up 17-7, Gavin Strange drilled a 46-yard field goal to make it a one-score game at 17-10. We got the ball back with a chance, but a blitzer came free on fourth down with 3:34 left and knocked the throw down.

Clemson owned the clock, 37:15 to 22:45, and ran 51 times. That's a lot of snaps for any defense to handle.

Here's the good news. Seven wins is seven wins, and this team still has a lot to play for.

Next up: at Wake Forest, Saturday, Nov. 28, to close the regular season against an old in-state foe ranked No. 10. Get on the road to Winston-Salem, Duke fans, and bring the noise. Go Duke!

articles.title: Clemson vs Duke: Walk-On Trent Pearman and Chris Denson Run the Tigers Past the Blue Devils, 20-10
articles.matchup: Final: Clemson Tigers (7-4) 20, Duke Blue Devils (7-4) 10, Fri., Nov. 20, Wallace Wade Stadium, Durham. Next: vs South Carolina, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Memorial Stadium (Clemson, SC), Clemson
articles.text:
Y'all, a walk-on did that. Trent Pearman showed up at Clemson in 2022 with no scholarship and a whole lot of want-to, and on Friday night in Durham, in the first game he ever opened at quarterback, he led the Tigers to a 20-10 win at Duke. We're 7-4, 5-3 in the ACC, and my heart is full.

After losing Tait Reynolds and Christopher Vizzina to injuries in that home loss to Georgia Tech, Coach Swinney rolled out a two-man plan. Pearman went 17 of 27 for 164 yards and ran six times for 51. Chris Denson, who had moved from quarterback to receiver, flipped right back and carried it 16 times for 71 yards. Two guys, one job, and they got it done.

It was a grind. Neither team scored in the first quarter, and we had a fumble and an interception in the first half. Nolan Hauser got us on the board with a 36-yard field goal with 17 seconds left before halftime. Then in the third, Pearman got around the left side and beat a defender to the pylon from 9 yards out. 10-0.

Duke answered fast. Four snaps after the kickoff, Nate Sheppard went 55 yards, and it was 10-7. That man is a load. But our guys came right back with an eight-play, 71-yard drive, and Denson bounced a keeper outside and hugged the sideline for a 7-yard touchdown. 17-7 midway through the fourth.

Then the defense closed the door. With 3:34 left and Duke facing fourth down, Jahiem Lawson came screaming in untouched on a blitz and batted Walker Eget's throw right out of the air. Hauser hit a 39-yarder with 1:01 left for his 31st field goal of the year, an ACC single-season record. Corey Myrick added an interception in the final seconds, plus two and a half tackles for loss. We held Duke to 247 yards and Eget to 16 of 38.

We also snapped a two-game skid against the Blue Devils. Jarvis Green ran for 84 yards and T.J. Moore caught four for 68. Everybody chipped in.

Next up: South Carolina comes to Death Valley on Saturday, Nov. 28. The Palmetto Bowl, Thanksgiving weekend, the whole state watching. Wear orange, wear paw prints, and make it shake. Go Tigers!

articles.title: Iowa State vs UCF: Aiden Flora Runs for 171, Four Turnovers Sink the Cyclones, 48-17
articles.byline: Twyla Hemmingsen, The Iowa State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: UCF Knights (6-5) 48, Iowa State Cyclones (5-6) 17, Fri., Nov. 20, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando. Next: vs Kansas State, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Jack Trice Stadium, Ames
articles.text:
If you only watched Aiden Flora on Friday night, you'd swear Iowa State won this game. The sophomore came to Orlando leading the country in rushing, and he ran for 171 yards and two touchdowns on 23 carries, including a 62-yard dash in the third quarter. That kid is a problem for every defense in the Big 12. Sadly, the scoreboard says UCF 48, Iowa State 17, and we're 5-6, 3-5 in conference.

Here's the honest truth, Cyclone fans. We gave the ball away four times, and you can't do that on the road against a team playing for a bowl.

We actually got on the board first. Our opening drive went 12 plays and 66 yards, and Kyle Konrardy knocked in a 27-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead. Then the second quarter got away from us. UCF scored twice through the air, and with 8:41 left in the half we put the ball on the ground at our own 23. One play later it was 24-3. That stung.

Flora answered with a 17-yard touchdown run to make it 24-10. Late in the half, Jaylen Raynor hit Flora for 13 yards into UCF territory, and the ball got knocked loose. Another one gone.

After halftime Flora broke that 62-yarder, and we were back to 31-17 with plenty of time. That's when the night really slipped. Flora got stopped short on fourth-and-1, and on the very next drive Jamal Polite caught one for 20 yards and had it punched out. Then an interception in the fourth. We went 1 for 10 on third down. Tough to win like that.

Credit to the defense for keeping swinging. Drew Surges made 10 tackles, and Sullivan Schlimgen had nine, seven of them solo. Raynor went 14 of 23 for 109 yards and kept battling.

So here's where we are. Bowl eligibility comes down to one game, at home, against our biggest rival. Couldn't script it better.

Next up: Kansas State at Jack Trice Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET. Farmageddon with a bowl on the table. Wear cardinal and gold and be loud. Go Cyclones!

articles.title: UCF vs Iowa State: Barnett Finds Derry Three Times, Knights Go Bowling, 48-17
articles.matchup: Final: UCF Knights (6-5) 48, Iowa State Cyclones (5-6) 17, Fri., Nov. 20, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando. Next: at Colorado, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Folsom Field, Boulder
articles.text:
Pack a bag, Knights fans. UCF 48, Iowa State 17 at the Bounce House on Friday night, and that sixth win punches our bowl ticket, our first one since 2023. We're 6-5, 4-4 in the Big 12, and Orlando is buzzing.

Alonza Barnett III was the conductor of this whole show. He went 17 of 27 for 255 yards and four touchdowns, ran for 43 more and added a 15-yard touchdown run of his own. Three of those scoring throws went to Josh Derry, from 21, 65 and 24 yards. Derry caught four balls for 125 yards and became our first receiver with three touchdown catches in a game since Jacob Harris against South Florida in 2020. Four catches, three touchdowns. That's efficient.

The second quarter was a blur. Derry from 21 to make it 10-3. Derry from 65 to make it 17-3. Then Lewis Carter jumped on a fumble at the Iowa State 23, and Barnett ran it in on the very next play. Three touchdowns in about four and a half minutes, 24-3, and the place was rocking.

Best moment of the night? Fourth quarter, Barnett throws a 5-yard touchdown to Jacob Maiava. An offensive lineman. Big man touchdowns are the best touchdowns, and I will hear no arguments.

Credit the Cyclones: Aiden Flora is the real deal. He came in leading the nation in rushing and ran for 171 yards and two scores. But our defense took the ball away four times. Antione Jackson forced one fumble and intercepted Jaylen Raynor, returning it 28 yards. Kahmel Johnson punched one loose, and Jayden Williams recovered it. Carter recovered two. Iowa State went 1 for 10 on third down. Cole Kozlowski led us with nine tackles, and Isaiah Nixon had three tackles for loss and a sack.

Duke Watson ran 16 times for 113 yards, Tyren Hornes caught five for 80, and Duane Thomas Jr. punched in a 2-yarder early in the fourth. Zero turnovers for us. That's how you clinch a bowl.

Next up: at Colorado, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET at Folsom Field to close the regular season. Let's go get number seven in the mountains. Charge On!

articles.byline: Shay Kowalczyk, The Michigan State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Oregon Ducks (8-3) 45, Michigan State Spartans (3-8) 7, Fri., Nov. 20, Spartan Stadium, East Lansing. Next: at Rutgers, Sat., Nov. 28, 4:15 PM ET, SHI Stadium, Piscataway
articles.text:
Okay, Spartan Nation, let's do the honest version. Oregon 45, Michigan State 7, Friday night at Spartan Stadium in front of 61,331 people who deserved a better second quarter. We're 3-8, 1-7 in the Big Ten, and I'm going to tell you the truth because that's what friends do.

The game turned in about 15 minutes of football. We were in Oregon territory twice in the second quarter. articles.title: Oregon vs Michigan State: The Kicker Runs One In, Brandon Smith Runs Wild, 45-7
articles.matchup: Final: Oregon Ducks (8-3) 45, Michigan State Spartans (3-8) 7, Fri., Nov. 20, Spartan Stadium, East Lansing. Next: vs Washington, Sat., Nov. 28, time TBA, Autzen Stadium, Eugene
articles.text:
Our kicker scored as many rushing touchdowns in East Lansing as the entire Michigan State offense. Let that sink in. Gage Hurych, a guy who had five offers to play Division I lacrosse, took a pitch on a fake field goal with two seconds left in the first half and went 15 yards to the house, and Oregon walked out of Spartan Stadium with a 45-7 win on Friday night. Ducks are 8-3, 6-2 in the Big Ten, and we've won four straight.

Dan Lanning, you beautiful mad scientist. Bailey Ettridge took the snap, set the ball on the grass like a normal hold, then flipped it to Hurych, who broke a tackle and made it 17-0. I screamed so loud my dog left the room.

And then there's Brandon Smith. The freshman was our third-string running back. On Friday he ran 14 times for 121 yards and two touchdowns, both career highs, with a long of 48. He opened the scoring from 5 yards out late in the first quarter and punched in a 1-yarder with one second left in the third. Next man up? More like next man takes off.

Dylan Raiola was sharp, going 21 of 34 for 234 yards. His best throw was a 31-yard strike to Dakorien Moore, who snagged it one-handed in the end zone for a 38-7 lead early in the fourth. Simeon Price added two short touchdown runs, and Hurych hit a 40-yard field goal and went 6 for 6 on extra points. Busy night for the lacrosse guy.

The defense was nasty. Michigan State finished with 200 yards and 80 on the ground on 37 carries. Matayo Uiagalelei grabbed an interception early in the fourth, Gavin Nix made eight tackles, and A'Mauri Washington had a tackle and a half for loss. We had zero turnovers. The Spartans had two, plus a missed 47-yard field goal and a fourth-down run that went nowhere. We outscored them 28-7 after halftime.

We're No. 13 in the playoff rankings, and every week is a tryout now. This one looked like a team that wants in.

Next up: Washington comes to Autzen Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, for the regular-season finale. Wear green, wear yellow, bring your loudest voice for the Huskies. Sko Ducks!

articles.title: Wyoming vs New Mexico: Landon Sims and Kyle Frendt Rally the Pokes, but the Cowboys Fall 24-17 at War Memorial
articles.matchup: Final: New Mexico Lobos (9-2) 24, Wyoming Cowboys (7-4) 17, Fri., Nov. 20, War Memorial Stadium, Laramie. Next: vs UConn, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, War Memorial Stadium, Laramie
articles.text:
Down 24-7 late in the third quarter on our own field, plenty of teams would have packed it in. This Wyoming team didn't. We came all the way back to within a touchdown, and then New Mexico ran out the clock. Lobos 24, Cowboys 17, and that one's going to sting for a while in Laramie.

Let's start with the fight, because 22,002 people at War Memorial saw it. Erik Sandvik drilled a 29-yard field goal early in the fourth to make it 24-10. Then Landon Sims went to work, marching us 64 yards in eight plays and finding Kyle Frendt for a 34-yard touchdown with 2:57 to play. The place was rocking. One stop and we had a chance.

We never got it. New Mexico moved the chains when it had to, and the clock did the rest. That's the part that'll keep me up tonight.

Sims battled all night. He went 13 of 23 for 142 yards and a touchdown and punched in a 2-yard run right before halftime to get us on the board. Frendt caught five balls for 69 yards, and Jackson Holman hauled in a 37-yarder. Samuel Harris ran for 36 yards on seven carries.

The defense kept us in it. Gary Rutherford was a tackling machine with 11 stops and two breakups. Tyson Shamsid-Deen made nine with 1.5 tackles for loss. Ethan Stuhlsatz added nine tackles and a sack. They took the ball away twice, and New Mexico missed a field goal. We never gave the ball away.

But the numbers tell the story of the night. New Mexico held the ball for 38:01 and went 3 of 4 on fourth down. We finished with 188 yards and 10 first downs, and 46 rushing yards won't beat a nine-win team. We dug the hole early, falling behind 17-0 before we scored.

We're 7-4, and that's still a good season with one game to go. UConn comes to War Memorial on Saturday, Nov. 28. Home crowd, last game, one more chance to finish strong. Ride 'em, Cowboys.

articles.title: New Mexico vs Wyoming: Luke Moga Runs and Throws for Scores, Lobos Hold On in Laramie 24-17
articles.byline: Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, The New Mexico Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: New Mexico Lobos (9-2) 24, Wyoming Cowboys (7-4) 17, Fri., Nov. 20, War Memorial Stadium, Laramie. Next: vs Air Force, Fri., Nov. 27, 4:30 PM ET, University Stadium (NM), Albuquerque
articles.text:
Nine wins. Say it out loud, Albuquerque. The Lobos went up to Laramie on Friday night, built a 24-7 lead, held on through a nervy finish, and beat Wyoming 24-17. We're 9-2, and I'm not sure my voice is coming back before Thanksgiving.

The first half was all New Mexico. Luke Moga hit Cade Keith from 5 yards out on our opening scoring drive, Grant Glasgow banged home a 48-yard field goal before the first quarter ended, and Moga ran one in from a yard out in the second for a 17-0 lead. Wyoming couldn't get anything going for a long stretch.

Kiefer Sibley was the workhorse. Twenty carries, 79 yards, and a 1-yard touchdown in the third that made it 24-7. He also caught three balls for 40 yards, including the biggest catch of the night: a 15-yarder on the final drive that moved the chains and let us run out the clock. He carried it twice more, and Moga took a knee. Lights out.

Moga went 22 of 40 for 234 yards and a score without an interception. Bailen George caught eight balls for 76 yards, and Keith added four grabs for 42. We piled up 433 yards and 26 first downs, went 3 of 4 on fourth down, and held the ball for 38:01. That's how you win on the road in November.

The defense smothered the Cowboys. Wyoming finished with 188 yards, 46 of them on the ground, and just 10 first downs. They went 3 of 12 on third down. Mercury Swaim made eight tackles with one for loss, Jayden Flaker added six, and CJ McBean had a tackle for loss of his own.

I won't pretend the fourth quarter was relaxing. We lost two fumbles, missed a field goal, and Wyoming scored 10 straight to make it a one-score game with 2:57 left. My heart was pounding. But the offense took the ball and never gave it back.

Air Force comes to University Stadium next Friday afternoon for the regular-season finale. Ten wins is right there. Pack the place, Lobo nation, and howl.

articles.title: Indianapolis Colts vs Houston Texans Week 11: Three Points, Three Kicks, One Long Night, 26-3
articles.matchup: Final: Houston Texans (4-6) 26, Indianapolis Colts (3-8) 3, Thu., Nov. 19, Reliant Stadium, Houston. Next: vs New York Giants, Sun., Nov. 29, 1:00 PM ET, Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis
articles.text:
Texans 26, Colts 3. I'd love to tell you it was closer than that, but I don't do fairy tales on Thursdays. The Indianapolis Colts are 3-8 after a night in Houston where the only stretch that worked for us was the first 10 minutes.

And those first 10 minutes were great! Daniel Jones moved us 44 yards on the opening drive, and Spencer Shrader knocked through a 34-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead. Then A.J. Haulcy intercepted C.J. Stroud on Houston's very first possession. I was out of my seat, already mapping a parade route down Meridian Street.

Then Shrader's 56-yard try drifted wide left, and Stroud hit Nico Collins for 42 yards and a touchdown three plays later. Kamari Lassiter intercepted Jones on the first play of the second quarter, Houston went 85 yards for a 14-3 lead, and Shrader's 62-yarder got blocked. 17-3 at the half. Three field goal tries, one make, and that was our whole scoring night.

The third quarter didn't help. Will Anderson Jr. sacked Jones in our own end zone for a safety, and a 13-yard Marlin Klein touchdown made it 26-3.

Let's be fair to our guys. We were missing both of our regular tackles, Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis, and both of our outside corners, Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward Sr. Jonathan Taylor had nowhere to run, finishing with 21 yards on 11 carries. Jones went 12 of 27 for 144 yards. We finished with 167 yards of offense and 38 rushing yards, both season lows, and it's the first time we failed to reach the end zone since a 24-6 loss to Detroit in November 2024.

Bright spots, because I'm a Colts fan and I always find them: CJ Allen made 16 tackles and played like a man possessed. Rigoberto Sanchez boomed three punts for a 49.0 average. Anthony Gould caught two balls for 48 yards, and Seth McGowan ran back three kickoffs for 117 yards before a hamstring injury in the second quarter.

Ten days to regroup. Next up: the New York Giants come to Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1:00 PM ET. Pack the place, Colts fans. Go Colts!

articles.title: Houston Texans vs Indianapolis Colts Week 11: Roof Open, Stroud Hot, Anderson Safety, 26-3
articles.matchup: Final: Houston Texans (4-6) 26, Indianapolis Colts (3-8) 3, Thu., Nov. 19, Reliant Stadium, Houston. Next: vs Baltimore Ravens, Sun., Nov. 29, 1:00 PM ET, Reliant Stadium, Houston
articles.text:
They opened the roof, Houston! For the first time since a November night against Detroit in 2024, Reliant Stadium let the sky in, and the Houston Texans finally gave the home crowd a reason to howl. Texans 26, Colts 3. Our first home win of the season after four straight losses at Reliant. We're 4-6, and last week's collapse against Cleveland feels like it happened to some other team.

It didn't open pretty. Indy kicked a field goal on the first drive, and C.J. Stroud's first deep throw got tipped four times before A.J. Haulcy came down with it. Fine. Our defense shrugged, Spencer Shrader pushed a 56-yarder wide left, and three plays later Stroud dropped a 42-yard rainbow into Nico Collins' hands. 7-3, and we never looked back.

Kamari Lassiter intercepted Daniel Jones on the first snap of the second quarter, and Stroud marched us 85 yards in 12 plays, finishing with a 24-yard strike to Kayshon Boutte. Logan Hall blocked a 62-yard field goal try, Ka'imi Fairbairn hit from 27 with 15 seconds left, and it was 17-3 at the half.

Then Will Anderson Jr. went full Will Anderson Jr. Third-and-8 at the Colts 7, Jones dropped back into his own end zone, and Anderson ate him alive for a safety. 19-3. That's 11 and a half sacks for the NFL's sack leader, plus four quarterback hits on the night. On the next drive, rookie Marlin Klein caught a 13-yard touchdown, and it was 26-3 in the third quarter.

Stroud was surgical: 21 of 27, 194 yards, three touchdowns, his third straight game with at least three touchdown throws. David Montgomery, back after missing four games, pounded out 107 yards on 26 carries, his best of the season. And the defense? Indy managed 167 yards of offense and 38 on the ground. Jonathan Taylor got 21 yards on 11 carries. Jadeveon Clowney added a sack, too.

Ten days to rest up. Next up: the Baltimore Ravens come to Reliant Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1:00 PM ET. Somebody check the weather and leave that roof open. We are Texans!

articles.text:
Rice 31, Temple 27, and I'm still glaring at the Linc scoreboard like it owes me money. Six seconds. We were six seconds from a win in the first-ever meeting between these two programs, and the visiting Owls snatched it. We're 2-9, 1-6 in the American.

The maddening part? Our guys ran the ball all night. Temple rushed for 300 yards on 35 carries, 8.6 a pop, our best rushing night since 329 yards against Howard on Sept. 6, 2025. Keveun Mason carried 15 times for 98 yards. Colin Chase broke a career-long 42-yard run on the opening drive, and Jaxon Smolik found him from 10 yards out for a 7-0 lead. First opening-drive touchdown since Charlotte.

Our defense had a moment too. After Koa Akui intercepted Smolik in the second quarter, Jayce Freeman chased him down and punched the ball out, and Mason fell on it. Carl Hardin's 21-yard field goal sent us to the half up 10-7.

Rice took a 14-10 lead on a 46-yard D'Andre Hardeman Jr. run, and the Owls in cherry and white answered like a Philly crowd answers a bad call. Mason ripped off 31 yards, Smolik hit Freeman for 29, then found him from 2 yards out. 17-14. Two plays later, De'Carlos Young took a handoff 79 yards for the first touchdown of his career. 24-14.

Hardin added a 35-yarder for 27-17 with 5:18 left. Ten points, five minutes. And then it slipped. Rice converted a fourth-and-10 with a 47-yard throw, scored with 1:55 left, and after our three-and-out and a punt, got the ball back at its own 42 with less than a minute left and no timeouts. Another fourth-and-10 conversion, an offside flag, and Patrick Crayton Jr. found Jacurri Brown for a 30-yard touchdown with six seconds left.

Credit where it's due. Curly Ordonez made 11 tackles, eight solo. Smolik threw for two touchdowns and ran for 49 yards. Young averaged 17 yards a carry. This team fought.

Next up: at Memphis on Friday, Nov. 27, at 3:30 PM ET for the finale. One more Friday, Owls fans. Let's send this season out the right way. T for Temple U!

articles.title: Rice vs Temple: Crayton Finds Jacurri Brown With Six Seconds Left, 31-27
articles.matchup: Final: Rice Owls (2-9) 31, Temple Owls (2-9) 27, Thu., Nov. 19, Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia. Next: vs Army, Sat., Nov. 28, 2:00 PM ET, Houston
articles.text:
Rice 31, Temple 27, and somebody please check on my voice, because I left it in Philadelphia. Down 10 with 5:18 to go, no timeouts on the final drive, a freshman quarterback who had thrown six times all season, and the Owls of Houston still walked out of Lincoln Financial Field with their first American win of the year. We're 2-9, 1-6 in conference, and I have never loved a 2-9 team more.

Our school notes said the Linc would be the 11th NFL home stadium to host Rice in a regular-season game. Fitting. The night ended like a Sunday highlight.

Temple scored on its first drive and led 10-7 at the half. Gael Ochoa hit Payton Matthews for a 33-yard touchdown, and D'Andre Hardeman Jr. went 46 yards up the middle early in the third quarter for our first lead, 14-10. Then the other Owls answered twice in about a minute of game clock, and a 79-yard De'Carlos Young run made it 24-14.

Here's what I love about this group: it refused to fold. We put together a 20-play, 55-yard drive that ate 11:43, converted two fourth downs along the way, and Tommy Bauchiero knocked through a 37-yard field goal. Temple kicked one back for 27-17 with 5:18 left.

Then the fun began. On fourth-and-10 from our own 25, Patrick Crayton Jr. dropped a 47-yard strike to Max Mosey. Jacurri Brown ran for 10 yards on fourth-and-1, and Ochoa found Mosey from 9 yards out. 27-24 with 1:55 left. Our defense forced a three-and-out, and we got the ball back at our 42 with less than a minute on the clock.

Crayton converted a fourth-and-10 with an 18-yard throw to Jordan Clark. A Temple offside flag moved us to the 35, and Clark caught a 5-yard ball to the 30. And with six seconds left, Crayton lofted it deep to Jacurri Brown, who hauled it in for the 30-yard touchdown. Eight plays, 58 yards. I may frame the replay.

Hardeman finished with 137 yards on 17 carries. We ran for 264 yards, went 5 for 7 on fourth down, and Koa Akui intercepted Jaxon Smolik in the second quarter. Crayton went 5 of 10 for 106 yards, the most fun 106 yards I've seen all year.

Next up: Army comes to Houston on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2:00 PM ET for the finale. Wear blue, bring the noise, and Go Owls!

articles.title: Central Michigan vs Buffalo: Glasser Throws Three, and It All Comes Down to Muncie, 40-21
articles.byline: Brynn Haverkamp, The Central Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bulls (8-3) 40, Central Michigan Chippewas (5-6) 21, Wed., Nov. 18, Broadview Stadium, Buffalo. Next: at Ball State, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Scheumann Stadium, Muncie
articles.text:
Buffalo 40, Central Michigan 21, and I've had plenty of time to stew since the final whistle Wednesday night at Broadview Stadium. The Chippewas are 5-6, 3-4 in the MAC, and it comes down to one game: win at Ball State on Nov. 28, and we're bowl eligible.

The first drive went exactly how I'd hoped. Our guys went 11 plays and 75 yards, and Jadyn Glasser found Braylen Naves for a 32-yard touchdown. 7-0. Then came the turnovers: an interception on the first play of one drive and a fumble on the first play of the next, and Buffalo turned them into 10 points.

Then Declan Duley did what no Chippewa had ever done. He boomed an 86-yard punt that was downed at the Buffalo 1, a school record. We forced a three-and-out, got the ball back at the Buffalo 45, and Glasser hit Myles Peters from 5 yards out with 39 seconds left in the half. 14-13, Chippewas!

And then 35 seconds of heartbreak. Buffalo hit a 49-yard throw, and Chance Morrow made a 17-yard touchdown catch with four seconds left. 20-14 at the half.

We didn't fold. Buffalo went up 26-14 early in the third after its two-point try failed, and our guys put together a 12-play, 75-yard march that chewed up 6:51. Glasser found Brock Townsend from 2 yards out with 3:55 left in the third. 26-21. Then Messiah Burch ran 75 yards on Buffalo's next snap, and Terrance Shelton Jr. scored from 2 yards out early in the fourth. 40-21.

Glasser threw a career-high three touchdowns, going 10 of 19 for 101 yards. Jayden Clerveaux ran for 70 yards on 15 carries, Nick Woodford added 57, and Mayson Hitchens led the defense with seven tackles. Coach Matt Drinkall put it plainly: "Very good team. They made plays and we made too many mistakes." Three turnovers against a team like that is too many, and everybody in maroon and gold knows it.

Next up: at Ball State, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 12:00 PM ET, Scheumann Stadium in Muncie. One win for a bowl. Fire Up Chips!

articles.title: Buffalo vs Central Michigan: Burch Hits 200 Again as the Bulls Win Six Straight, 40-21
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bulls (8-3) 40, Central Michigan Chippewas (5-6) 21, Wed., Nov. 18, Broadview Stadium, Buffalo. Next: at Akron, Fri., Nov. 27, 12:00 PM ET, InfoCision Stadium, Akron
articles.text:
Buffalo 40, Central Michigan 21, and that's six straight. Wednesday was the home finale at Broadview Stadium, and the Bulls sent everybody home happy. We're 8-3, 6-1 in the MAC, sharing first place, and this is our longest winning streak since the seven-game run in 2013. We finished 5-1 at home, too, matching the best home record since the Bulls joined the FBS.

Messiah Burch, again. He ran for exactly 200 yards and two touchdowns, the second straight game he has hit 200 and scored twice. That gives him 1,310 yards this season, and I'd like the rest of the MAC to know he isn't tired.

It began a little shaky. Central drove 75 yards on its first possession, and Jadyn Glasser hit Braylen Naves for a 32-yard touchdown. 7-0. Oliver Hautanen got us on the board from 27. Then Ronnell Davis went to work. He intercepted Glasser on the very next snap, and Hautanen kicked a 26-yarder. On Central's next play, Davis forced a fumble, SaVeon Brown fell on it at the CMU 26, and Burch scored from 10 yards out. 13-7.

Central went ahead 14-13 on a 5-yard Myles Peters catch with 39 seconds left in the half. Jason Wright needed 29 seconds to fix that. He hit Jaylen Andrews for 49 yards, and after two incompletions, Chance Morrow made a falling catch in the end zone from 17 yards out with four seconds left. 20-14. That was Morrow's 10th touchdown catch of the season.

Wright opened the third by running in from the 1 to finish a 75-yard drive. The two-point try failed, 26-14. Central answered with a 12-play drive and a 2-yard Brock Townsend catch, 26-21, and my stomach dropped. For one snap. Burch went straight up the middle for 75 yards on the very next play. 33-21. Terrance Shelton Jr. added a 2-yard run early in the fourth, 40-21.

Davis finished with 11 tackles to go with that interception and forced fumble, and Miles Greer also made 11 tackles and came up with an interception of his own. Shelton ran for 81 yards. As a team we ran for 283 yards, piled up 435 yards of offense, and didn't give the ball away once.

Next up: at Akron, Friday, Nov. 27, at 12:00 PM ET, InfoCision Stadium. Seven in a row sounds good to me. Go Bulls!

articles.title: UMass vs Akron: A 26-7 Lead Slips Away on Senior Night, 34-33
articles.matchup: Final: Akron Zips (2-9) 34, Massachusetts Minutemen (5-6) 33, Wed., Nov. 18, Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium, Amherst. Next: at Bowling Green, Sat., Nov. 28, 3:30 PM ET, Doyt L. Perry Stadium, Bowling Green
articles.text:
Akron 34, Massachusetts 33, and I'm still in my seat at McGuirk Alumni Stadium trying to figure out how. It was Senior Night and Fan Appreciation in Amherst on Wednesday, we led 26-7 in the second quarter, and we didn't lead at the end. The Minutemen are 5-6, 2-5 in the MAC.

The first half went exactly the way I wanted. Elijah Faulkner went 52 yards for a touchdown on our opening drive. Isaiah Reed intercepted Cibastian Broughton, and Derek Morris drilled a 49-yard field goal. Akron answered with a 73-yard Jordan Gant run, but Logan Inagawa hit Matt Ogunniyi from 3 yards out, and it was 17-7 after one quarter.

Reed got his second interception and returned it 68 yards to the Akron 2. We came away with a 23-yard Morris field goal from there, and that still bugs me. Max Dowling caught a 2-yard touchdown, the two-point try failed, and it was 26-7.

Akron chipped back. Miles Burris caught a 36-yard touchdown, an interception set up a field goal, and Morris missed from 50 right before the break. 26-17.

Then the second-half kickoff. Brandon Hills took it 100 yards, and it was 26-24 just like that. Our guys answered with a 13-play, 75-yard drive, and Inagawa found Dowling from 11 yards for 33-24. Akron came back with Gant from the 1 to make it 33-31, then went 13 plays for a 28-yard Aidan Stire field goal with 5:34 left. 34-33.

We had our chances. Our last real drive went 11 plays to the Akron 46, and on fourth down with 58 seconds left, the throw to Dowling fell incomplete. A final series from our own 17 ended with a sack.

There's plenty to be proud of. Faulkner ran for 105 yards on 13 carries. Inagawa threw three touchdowns and ran for 64 yards. Reed's two interceptions for 68 return yards deserve a plaque, and Tyler Martin had seven tackles and a sack. We ran for 269 yards and held the ball for 35:57.

To the seniors: thank you. One more Saturday. Next up: at Bowling Green, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 3:30 PM ET, Doyt L. Perry Stadium. Go Minutemen!

articles.text:
Akron 34, Massachusetts 33, and the eight-game skid is dead. Wednesday night at McGuirk Alumni Stadium, the Zips trailed 26-7 in the second quarter, didn't lead until the final six minutes, and still came home with the win. We're 2-9, 1-6 in the MAC, and it's our first victory since September. I yelled myself hoarse in Amherst and regret not one second of it.

The first half was rough. UMass scored on a 52-yard Elijah Faulkner run on its first drive, and Isaiah Reed intercepted Cibastian Broughton twice. The second one came back 68 yards to our 2. The best moment of the half? Our defense pushed them backward from the 2, and they had to take a field goal. A short touchdown catch and a failed two-point try later, it was 26-7.

Jordan Gant had already given us a spark with a 73-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, the longest of his career. articles.title: Kent State vs Miami (OH): Senior Night Ends in a 20-3 Loss at Dix Stadium
articles.byline: Ozzie Brannigan, The Kent State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Miami (OH) RedHawks (7-4) 20, Kent State Golden Flashes (3-8) 3, Tue., Nov. 17, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium, Kent. Next: at Eastern Michigan, Tue., Nov. 24, 7:00 PM ET, Rynearson Stadium, Ypsilanti
articles.text:
Miami (OH) 20, Kent State 3, and my Gold Jacket koozie spent the whole night holding cold air. It was Senior Night at Dix Stadium on Tuesday, our home finale, and I stood and clapped for every senior who ran out of that tunnel. Then Miami ran the ball 58 times. We're 3-8, 2-5 in the MAC.

The hole got dug early. Miami went 67 yards in seven plays, and D'Shawntae Jones scored from the 1. We answered with a 13-play, 61-yard march, and Tommy Newcomb hit a 39-yard field goal. 7-3, and for a minute I was dreaming. Then Jones scored again from the 1 on fourth down with 22 seconds left in the first quarter. 13-3.

We had our chance early in the second quarter. Dru DeShields hit Da'Realyst Clark for 23 yards to the Miami 39, and on the very next snap his throw got intercepted at the Miami 11. That was as close as we got all night.

Credit where it's due on defense. We forced a missed 30-yard field goal before halftime, and after Miami's 16-play drive reached our 2 early in the fourth, Camdon Wilborn forced a fumble on fourth down for a 6-yard loss and a turnover on downs. Rocco Nicholl and Joel Cordoba made 10 tackles apiece, Nicholl added a sack, and Davion Pritchard had eight stops.

Drew Bellisari's 23-yard touchdown run in the third made it 20-3, and that was the last of the scoring. We managed 170 yards, 31 on the ground, and Miami held the ball for 38:36. That's a long night for any defense.

There were a couple of bright spots for the record book. Wayne Harris caught four balls for 46 yards and moved past Nykeim Johnson for the 10th-most catches in a season in Kent State history. DeShields, 8 of 15 for 92 yards, climbed to eighth on the program's career list for yards of offense.

Thank you, seniors. You showed up every week. Next up: the season finale at Eastern Michigan, Rynearson Stadium, Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 7:00 PM ET. I'll bring the koozie. Go Flashes!

articles.title: Miami (OH) vs Kent State: 58 Carries, 301 Yards and a 20-3 Win for the RedHawks
articles.byline: Cordelia Van Doren, The Miami (OH) Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Miami (OH) RedHawks (7-4) 20, Kent State Golden Flashes (3-8) 3, Tue., Nov. 17, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium, Kent. Next: at Western Michigan, Tue., Nov. 24, 7:00 PM ET, Waldo Stadium, Kalamazoo
articles.text:
Miami (OH) 20, Kent State 3, and I'd like everyone in Oxford to write down the date. Freshman Drew Bellisari ran the show from the opening snap for the first time Tuesday night at Dix Stadium, the RedHawks are 7-4 and 5-2 in the MAC, and Chuck Martin now has a winning record at Miami: seventy-nine wins, seventy-eight losses. The Cradle of Coaches has a new page to add.

We ran the ball 58 times for 301 yards. Fifty-eight! Our athletics office says the last time Miami ran that many times in a game was Nov. 8, 1997, with Hall of Famer Travis Prentice in the backfield. I'm adding a footnote to my binder tonight.

D'Shawntae Jones ran like a bulldozer, with a career-high 29 carries for 121 yards and two 1-yard touchdowns. Rodney Nelson set up the first one with a 47-yard catch on a shovel throw, and Jones finished the seven-play march for 7-0. After Kent kicked a field goal, Jones scored again on a fourth-down direct snap with 22 seconds left in the first quarter. The extra point missed, so it was 13-3. Nelson added 90 yards on 16 carries.

Bellisari kept it simple and smart. He went 7 of 12 for 124 yards, and in the third quarter Scoop Smith set him up with an 11-yard catch and a 25-yard run. Four plays later, Bellisari kept it himself and ran 23 yards up the middle for a touchdown. 20-3.

Now let's talk about the defense. Kent State gained 170 yards, the fewest by any Miami opponent this season, and just 31 on the ground. Amariyun Knighten intercepted Dru DeShields at our 11 to end their best chance, Malcolm McCain made nine tackles, and Grant Lyons, Devin Bell and OJ Alexander each had a sack. The Flashes went the final 51 minutes without a point.

We did leave a few chances behind, with a missed 30-yard field goal and a fourth-down stop at their 2, so I'll keep my applause polite. We held the ball for 38:36. I'll take it.

Next up: at Western Michigan, Waldo Stadium, Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 7:00 PM ET. Love and Honor, RedHawks.

articles.title: Ball State vs Ohio: Luster, Hohlt Push the Bobcats to the Wire, 35-28
articles.byline: Gus Ponder, The Ball State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Ohio Bobcats (8-3) 35, Ball State Cardinals (3-8) 28, Tue., Nov. 17, Peden Stadium, Athens. Next: vs Central Michigan, Sat., Nov. 28, 12:00 PM ET, Scheumann Stadium, Muncie
articles.text:
Ohio 35, Ball State 28, and I've never been so proud and so grumpy at the same time. The Cardinals walked into Peden Stadium on Tuesday night, where Ohio hadn't lost in 17 straight home games, and led 20-14 after three quarters. Garfield hates Mondays. After this, I'm not too fond of late Tuesdays. We're 3-8, 2-5 in the MAC.

Keldric Luster was terrific. He threw for 257 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 109 more. His 10-yard throw to Donovan Hamilton gave us a 10-7 lead. Then Quentavius Scandrett intercepted Nick Poulos in our end zone, and two snaps later Luster hit Eli Hohlt on a short throw that turned into an 80-yard touchdown. 17-7! Hohlt caught four balls for 112 yards. Hudson Fiene made both his field goals, including a 43-yarder at the end of the half for 20-14.

The second half is where it slipped. TJ Horton broke a 26-yard run on our first drive and lost a fumble three snaps later. Our defense still kept Ohio off the board in the third, and Mikeah Webster and Jared Badie dropped their quarterback for a 10-yard sack that forced a punt.

Then the fourth quarter. Darren James-Hamilton intercepted Luster and returned it 34 yards for a touchdown, 21-20 Ohio, and Poulos ran in from 12 to make it 28-20. I put my head in my mittens. But these Cardinals don't quit. Luster drove us 68 yards in 10 plays, Horton scored from the 2 with 2:23 left, and Hamilton caught the two-point try. 28-28!

Ohio answered fast. Dom Dorwart caught a 29-yard touchdown with 1:16 left, and the replay booth let it stand. We got to the Ohio 43, but a sack and a last deep throw that James-Hamilton knocked away ended it.

We outgained Ohio 448 yards to 365. Horton ran for 64 yards and a score, Kaleb Stewart made eight tackles, and Webster made eight more. Coming this close in that building stings, but it beats getting run off the field, and these guys made Athens sweat.

Next up: Central Michigan at Scheumann Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 12:00 PM ET. Bring the red, Muncie. Chirp Chirp!

articles.title: Ohio vs Ball State: Dorwart's Late Catch Makes It 18 Straight at Peden, 35-28
articles.matchup: Final: Ohio Bobcats (8-3) 35, Ball State Cardinals (3-8) 28, Tue., Nov. 17, Peden Stadium, Athens. Next: vs Toledo, Fri., Nov. 27, 12:00 PM ET, Peden Stadium, Athens
articles.text:
Ohio 35, Ball State 28, and the black-shirted crowd at Peden Stadium got its money's worth Tuesday night. It was Wear Black night in Athens, and the Bobcats spent three quarters in the dark before Darren James-Hamilton and Dom Dorwart turned the lights back on. We're 8-3, 6-1 in the MAC, and that's 18 straight wins at home, still the longest home streak in the country.

It began the right way. Duncan Brune plunged in from the 1 on our first drive, 7-0. Then Ball State got rolling: a field goal, a 10-yard throw to Donovan Hamilton, and, right after Nick Poulos got intercepted in their end zone, an 80-yard catch-and-run by Eli Hohlt. 17-7. Poulos ran in from 8 to make it 17-14, and the Cardinals kicked a 43-yarder at the horn. 20-14 at the half, and my black boots were nervous.

The third quarter was a grind. DJ Walker forced a fumble and recovered it on Ball State's first drive, and we built a 13-play drive that ate 9:23 of clock before a sack pushed us back and we punted. Nobody scored. I walked a lap around my seat.

Then James-Hamilton happened. Early in the fourth, he intercepted Keldric Luster and went 34 yards the other way. 21-20, and Peden shook. After a Ball State three-and-out, Poulos capped an eight-play drive by running in from 12 yards, 28-20 with 7:15 left.

Ball State tied it with 2:23 to go on a TJ Horton touchdown and a two-point try to Hamilton. 28-28. So Poulos went to work. Riley Neer caught a 14-yarder, and on the next play Poulos threw deep to Dorwart, who came down with it for a 29-yard touchdown with 1:16 left. The review upheld it. 35-28. Ty Neubert and Evan Herrmann shared a late sack, and James-Hamilton knocked away the final heave into the end zone.

Poulos went 9 of 13 for 155 yards, ran for 58 more and had a hand in three touchdowns. Neer caught five for 92. Michael Molnar made 12 tackles, Walker made 11, and our defense allowed just 122 yards after halftime.

Next up: Toledo comes to Peden Stadium on Black Friday, Nov. 27, at 12:00 PM ET. Keep the black shirts handy, Bobcat fans. Nineteen has a nice ring to it.

articles.title: Eastern Michigan vs Western Michigan: Blue's 160 Yards Fuel a Rally, 34-27
articles.byline: Imogen Tremblay, The Eastern Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Western Michigan Broncos (8-3) 34, Eastern Michigan Eagles (4-7) 27, Tue., Nov. 17, Waldo Stadium, Kalamazoo. Next: vs Kent State, Tue., Nov. 24, 7:00 PM ET, Rynearson Stadium, Ypsilanti
articles.text:
Western Michigan 34, Eastern Michigan 27, and if you left Waldo Stadium at halftime Tuesday night, I feel bad for you. The Eagles trailed 31-7 at the break in Kalamazoo, clawed back to one score, and had the ball at the Broncos' 22 in the final minute. We're 4-7, 3-4 in the MAC, and I'm worn out in the proudest way.

We came in after a 13-day break with the Michigan MAC Trophy already staying in Kalamazoo, so this one was for pride, and the first half didn't give us much. Jalen Buckley ran 72 yards on their first snap, then capped a 93-yard drive, and it was 14-0. Our bright spot came off a Daniel Hull punt, when their returner muffed it and Donmiel Rogers fell on it. On the very next play, Amareon Blue ran it in from 7 yards. 14-7.

We stopped them on fourth down at our 3 early in the second quarter, and then it got away. A field goal, a 2-yard Cole Cabana touchdown with 40 seconds left, and a 50-yard interception return by Dillon Moore with two seconds on the clock. 31-7.

Then Brogan McCaughey came in at quarterback, and the Eagles woke up. We scored on our first three drives of the second half. Blue broke a 41-yard touchdown run, and the two-point try didn't make it, 31-13. McCaughey hit Joshua Long from 1 yard out to finish an 81-yard drive, 31-20. After their field goal, Blue scored from the 1 with 7:36 left. 34-27. McCaughey went 12 of 16 for 135 yards.

articles.byline: Corwin Dahlquist, The Western Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Western Michigan Broncos (8-3) 34, Eastern Michigan Eagles (4-7) 27, Tue., Nov. 17, Waldo Stadium, Kalamazoo. Next: vs Miami (OH), Tue., Nov. 24, 7:00 PM ET, Waldo Stadium, Kalamazoo
articles.text:
Western Michigan 34, Eastern Michigan 27, and Waldo Stadium can finally breathe again. Tuesday was the Broncos' annual Military Appreciation Game, the night Kalamazoo honored the veterans on our own staff, and our defense saved its best salute for the very last snap. We're 8-3, 6-1 in the MAC, and the Michigan MAC Trophy stays in Kalamazoo for a third straight year.

Eight seconds. That's how long it took. Jalen Buckley took our first snap 72 yards for a touchdown, and I spilled cocoa on my own boots. He added a 1-yard score to cap a 93-yard march, and it was 14-0. Buckley finished with 140 yards on 20 carries, and that second score moved him to third in program history in rushing touchdowns.

Then came the last minute of the half, which I would frame if I could. Cole Cabana punched in a 2-yard run with 40 seconds left for 24-7. Eastern tried one more throw, and Dillon Moore jumped it and ran 50 yards the other way with two seconds on the clock. 31-7 at the break. Moore also made 12 tackles, because one big play wasn't enough for him.

The second half was a test of my heart. Eastern scored on its first three drives. Amareon Blue broke a 41-yard touchdown run, the two-point try failed, and a 1-yard throw to Joshua Long made it 31-20. Our kicker steadied us with a 27-yard field goal for 34-20 with 12:45 left, and Blue answered from the 1 at 7:36. 34-27. Blue ran for 160 yards and three scores, and I tip my cap to him.

Then the finish. Eastern got the ball at its own 23 with 1:51 left and pushed all the way to our 22. Fourth down. Joshua Franklin came on a blitz from the secondary and sacked Brogan McCaughey for a 17-yard loss, and Broc Lowry took a knee. Scoop Gardner Jr. added 1.5 sacks, and our ground game rolled up 235 yards, with Lowry running for 57 of them.

It wasn't pretty after halftime, and I'll admit I aged a little. But on a night set aside to thank the people who served, a defense that answered the call on fourth down felt about right. That's four straight wins against Eastern, too.

Next up: Miami (OH) comes to Waldo Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 7:00 PM ET. Bring your voice, Kalamazoo. Go Broncos!
